title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When the submission reports computed quantitative results, its tables and narrative must agree with the submitted executable code and other public supporting evidence; discrepancies must not materially alter the stated comparison or interpretation.

title: Resolution of quantitative discrepancies before interpretation
requirement: When a submission reports computed quantitative results, its interpretive narrative and summaries must resolve any discrepancy with the submitted computation or supporting tables before relying on the result; merely acknowledging a contradiction while retaining the conflicting interpretation is insufficient.

title: Consistency of the human-analysis population
requirement: When reporting human-proteome composition, fold changes, or predictor results, use one explicitly defined human subset consistently across all such analyses, and reconcile any human-labelled rows excluded by the organism filter or other population rule.

title: Direct support for claimed computed results
requirement: Quantitative results claimed as completed analyses must be directly inspectable in the submitted material and consistent with the accompanying computation; code alone, planned calculations, or unreported objects must not serve as proof of the claimed output.

title: Evidence alignment and inspectable computational outputs
requirement: For claimed computed results, the submission must distinguish executed, directly inspectable outputs from code-only procedures and ensure each quantitative or derived claim is supported by the corresponding computation and output.

title: Consistency Between Reported Results and Supporting Computation
requirement: When the artifact reports quantitative results, its headline tables and prose must agree with the documented code and any displayed outputs; when multiple computational paths exist, it must clearly identify which path supports each claim and avoid attributing results to a loop that does not produce them.

title: Consistency Between Claims and Supporting Evidence
requirement: For every reported quantitative or methodological claim, the submitted material must align with the actual code, displayed output, and stated data processing; claims of completed analyses must have directly inspectable supporting evidence.

title: Claim-to-computation and output consistency
requirement: For every reported numerical result or claimed completed analysis, the submission must align the claim with the exact computation and provide directly inspectable supporting output; results must not be asserted from code that computes a different task, from unshown execution, or from inconsistent values elsewhere in the submission.

title: Alignment of composition estimands with reported interpretation
requirement: When using more than one composition estimand, the submission must identify whether each statistic is a per-protein composition summary or a pooled-residue frequency and must interpret and compare the statistic according to that definition.

title: Inspectable support for reported computations
requirement: When claiming completed calculations or generated quantitative results, provide directly inspectable outputs or artifacts that allow the result to be verified, rather than only executable code or a statement that code would print it.

title: Composition estimand is explicitly identified
requirement: When reporting amino-acid composition statistics, identify whether values represent per-protein composition summaries or pooled-residue frequencies, and do not present one estimand as the other.

title: Numerical claims remain internally consistent
requirement: Ensure that repeated or summarized numerical results agree with the supporting tables, code, and other public statements in the submission.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When reporting quantitative evaluation results, the submitted material must provide directly inspectable evidence that the reported values were produced by an executed analysis using the same label definitions, comparison sets, filters, and transformations described in the method; results from a materially different or unreconciled computation must not be presented as the requested findings.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: For any claimed computed result, the report must keep the stated method, displayed code, execution evidence, and interpretation consistent; material discrepancies must be disclosed and the unsupported result withdrawn rather than presented as the task answer.

title: Consistency between reported method and executed computation
requirement: When the analysis claims to use a particular labeling or background-set design, the submitted method description, code, and reported results must agree, or any material deviation must be explicitly disclosed so readers can correctly interpret the findings.

title: Directly Inspectable Result Evidence
requirement: For every claimed dataset–predictor performance result, provide a directly inspectable result table or equivalent included output showing the dataset, predictor, final positive and negative counts, and AUC; do not rely solely on code, prose summaries, or references to an unseen CSV.

title: Consistency Between Analysis Code and Reported Results
requirement: When computational results are claimed, the submitted code, intermediate counts, tables, and conclusions must agree with one another and provide inspectable support for the claimed computation.

title: Consistency Between Reported Method and Executed Analysis
requirement: When the response claims that a methodological safeguard or data transformation was performed, the documented code and reported results must directly support that claim; material discrepancies between the stated procedure and executed implementation must be disclosed.

title: Execution-to-report concordance
requirement: When reporting computed results, the artifact must ensure that stated dataset validity, class counts, overlap handling, and summary values agree with the executed code and recorded outputs.

title: Verified integration of auxiliary predictor data
requirement: When predictor scores are obtained from an auxiliary table rather than the primary labeled table, the artifact must establish a reliable identifier-level join before using those scores in evaluation.

title: Requested benchmark-scope coverage
requirement: When claiming a comprehensive benchmark, the analysis must cover the requested dataset variants and supplied predictor families, or explicitly identify and justify any exclusions and label the resulting analysis as partial or sensitivity-only.

title: Auditable ORA background construction
requirement: When the analysis claims a specific ORA universe, it must make that universe traceable to the supplied data or an explicitly identified source, with executable code showing its construction and consistent use in pathway-size and p-value calculations.

title: Preservation of the requested significance estimand
requirement: When reporting significance for the requested analysis, the submission must apply the question's stated p-value criterion to the requested test rather than silently replacing it with a different multiple-testing estimand or cutoff.

title: Consistency Between Computation and Reported Results
requirement: When claiming quantitative analysis results, the reported statistics and conclusions must be consistent with the submitted executable code and its stated inputs.

title: Coherent Tested-Universe Definition
requirement: When performing enrichment, the contingency table and pathway denominators must consistently use the explicitly declared tested universe; genes outside that universe must not be counted as background members, and any alternative estimand must be clearly distinguished.

title: Authoritative overlap definition under duplicate rows
requirement: When the input explicitly marks shared membership with overlap flags, the analysis must define the query set from those flags and deduplicate symbols, rather than infer overlap from independently intersecting row-derived lists in a way that lets duplicate records alter membership counts.

title: Eligibility-aligned ORA background
requirement: When performing ORA on supplied DEG lists, the background must represent genes eligible to occur in those lists (with pathway membership intersected to that universe), rather than using only the union of pathway annotations, unless the analysis explicitly justifies a different eligible universe from the data.

title: Consistency between analysis specification, computation, and reported results
requirement: When reporting computed or statistically derived findings, the artifact must keep the stated predictor scale, transformations, model code, intermediate outputs, and final numerical claims mutually consistent; unsupported analytical changes or conclusions that contradict the documented computation incur a penalty.

title: Direct evidence for completed numerical analysis
requirement: Claims about fitted models, feature counts, rankings, or statistical results must be supported by inspectable analysis outputs or directly reproducible executed evidence, rather than code snippets and prose claims alone.

title: Consistency of Reported Effect Scale with the Executed Analysis
requirement: When reporting a hazard ratio or p-value, the artifact must use the same predictor transformation and effect scale in its code, intermediate outputs, tables, and interpretation; claimed significance and threshold filtering must be based on those reported results.

title: Consistency Between Analysis Code, Effect Scale, and Reported Results
requirement: When reporting computed model results, the stated covariate scale, transformations, model inputs, and numerical outputs must agree with one another; claims derived from an external results artifact must not be presented as outputs of code that uses a materially different specification.

title: Consistency Between Computation and Reported Statistics
requirement: When claiming computed statistical results, the submitted executable analysis must use transformations, effect-size definitions, and inferential formulas that directly produce the reported values.

title: Inspectability of Claimed Computations
requirement: When reporting computed statistical results, the submission must provide enough executable code and directly inspectable output in the submitted material to reproduce and verify the claims, rather than relying on an unavailable script, file, or prose assertion.

title: Consistency Between Documented Method and Executed Analysis
requirement: When the response claims that a preprocessing step, model specification, transformation, or reported result was executed, its narrative, code, intermediate counts, and conclusions must be mutually consistent and must not contain a material contradiction that could change the analyzed data or estimates.

title: Inspectability of Claimed Computation and Outputs
requirement: When claiming that an analysis is reproducible or complete, the submission must include the substantive executable operations and directly inspectable generated results needed to verify the claim, rather than relying on an unseen script, file, or output that is not included in the submitted material.

title: Correct Construction of Survival Risk Sets
requirement: When claiming Cox survival estimates, the submitted implementation and evidence must correctly construct at-risk sets and handle censored observations and tied event times so that the reported hazard ratios and p-values correspond to the stated Cox model.

title: Regimen-specific claims must be supported by a direct interaction test
requirement: When an analysis claims that a protein's response is specific to, or differs between, CPA and SPIRO, it must base that claim on a direct statistical comparison of subject-level changes (or an equivalent regimen-by-time interaction), rather than on significance in one regimen but not the other or on overlap of within-regimen significant sets.

title: Formal support for regimen-specific claims
requirement: If the submission claims that a protein’s change is specific to, larger under, or caused by one regimen relative to another, it must provide a direct between-regimen comparison of subject-level changes (or an equivalent interaction test) with appropriate multiplicity control, and align the claim with that test’s result.

title: Consistency of reported results with supporting computation
requirement: When reporting computed numerical findings, the submission must ensure that the values, directions, counts, and conclusions in the narrative and answer are directly consistent with the displayed analysis code and any public result tables.

title: Direct evidence for regimen-specific differences
requirement: When claiming that protein changes differ between regimens, base the claim on a direct comparison of subject-level changes (or an equivalent regimen-by-time interaction) with multiplicity correction; do not infer differences from separate within-regimen significance or significant-set membership alone.

title: Consistency of reported quantitative results with supporting evidence
requirement: When reporting computed numerical findings, keep reported effect sizes, directions, p-values, adjusted values, counts, and conclusions consistent with the publicly shown computation or result tables.

title: Directly substantiate regimen-specific claims
requirement: When asserting that protein changes differ between regimens, directly compare participant-level paired changes (or fit an equivalent regimen-by-time interaction), apply multiplicity correction across proteins, and distinguish a nonsignificant difference from evidence of equivalence; significance in one regimen but not the other or set overlap alone is insufficient.

title: Evidence-supported regimen interaction claims
requirement: When claiming that protein changes differ between regimens, the analysis must provide a directly inspectable, reproducible between-regimen comparison with the tested proteins, effect estimates, p-values, and multiplicity-adjusted results; within-regimen significance or significance-set membership alone does not establish an interaction.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative summaries
requirement: Quantitative summaries and rankings must agree with the documented computation and with other reported counts, directions, and examples throughout the submission.

title: Conflict-aware timepoint assignment
requirement: When sample metadata and identifier-encoded timepoints disagree, the analysis must explicitly detect, adjudicate, and quantify the discrepancy rather than silently prioritizing one field; the chosen rule must be applied consistently to pairing and results.

title: Complete application of available QC fields
requirement: When multiple assay- and sample-level QC fields are supplied and used to define the cohort, claimed QC-filtered results must be based on all relevant stated QC requirements, with directly inspectable counts before and after each applicable filter.

title: Claim-to-code reproducibility consistency
requirement: When claiming computed results, the submitted analysis must provide code whose inputs, variables, filters, and outputs are defined consistently with the reported computation, so the claimed result can be directly reproduced from the submitted material.

title: Direct regimen-by-time contrast
requirement: When claiming that changes differ (or do not differ) between CPA and SPIRO, directly compare participant-level paired changes with a stated statistical test and multiplicity correction; do not infer regimen specificity from one arm being significant while the other is not.

title: Evidence for claimed generated results
requirement: When claiming that a complete result table or other computed output was generated, provide the output itself or direct, inspectable execution evidence that produces it from the supplied data and code.

title: Consistency of Derived Quantitative Summaries
requirement: When reporting counts or other summaries derived from filtered associations, ensure they are arithmetically consistent with the reported endpoint totals, effect directions, and supporting results.

title: Internal consistency of reported computations
requirement: When reporting computed counts, directions, rankings, or other quantitative findings, the artifact must keep those claims consistent with its shown code, intermediate results, and final answer.

title: Consistency between claimed results and supporting analysis
requirement: When the submission claims computed results, its narrative, reported outputs, and reproducibility code must agree on the same data interpretation, counts, rankings, and values.

title: Consistency of Reported Derived Results
requirement: When making claim-conditional numerical summaries, reported counts and classifications must agree with the submitted computation and with each other.

title: Consistency of reported quantitative summaries
requirement: When reporting aggregate counts or direction totals, ensure they are internally consistent with the stated filtering rule, effect estimates, and other reported results.

title: Integrity of claimed effect-size ordering
requirement: When claiming that results are ranked by effect-size magnitude, the displayed order must actually be non-increasing in the absolute estimate within each endpoint.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative summaries
requirement: When reporting counts, directions, rankings, or other derived quantitative results, the claims must agree with the documented filtering code and the corresponding reported data values.

title: Internal numerical consistency of reported summaries
requirement: When reporting computed association counts, directions, rankings, or overlap, the claims must be mutually consistent with the supplied data and with the analysis code and intermediate results shown.

title: Direct reproducibility evidence for completed analysis
requirement: When claiming that filtering, ranking, or summarization was completed, the submission must provide executable operations and inspectable intermediate outputs sufficient to verify those claims from the submitted material, rather than relying only on assertions or inaccessible output files.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims
requirement: Claimed counts, signs, rankings, and numeric values must agree with the submitted computation or displayed outputs and must not materially contradict one another.

title: Numerical claims match source data and computations
requirement: When the response claims computed values, signs, counts, rankings, or p-values, those claims must agree with the supplied data and the documented computation; reported summaries must also be internally consistent with the underlying values.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When an analysis reports computed counts or statistics, its code, intermediate results, final results, and answer must use consistent definitions and agree numerically.

title: Matched-universe denominator integrity
requirement: When overlap or enrichment is reported after joining datasets with incomplete assay coverage, distinguish total significant proteins from those present in the comparison universe and use the matched count as the overlap denominator and hypergeometric K.

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Results
requirement: When an artifact reports quantitative results or conclusions, its intermediate calculations, trace, and final answer must agree on the same definitions and values.

title: Schema and Header Validation
requirement: When quantitative results depend on tabular input, the submission must demonstrate that each file was loaded with the intended header and schema before downstream analysis; silently treating metadata or a blank row as the header can invalidate otherwise correct-looking results.

title: Question-aligned reference-set definition
requirement: When answering a broad overlap question, do not substitute an arbitrary top-k subset for the stated population of sex-associated proteins without explicitly establishing that restriction as part of the question or analysis objective.

title: Eligibility-matched enrichment universe
requirement: When testing overlap enrichment, the null universe must contain only unique entities eligible to appear in both the tested sets; entities unavailable to one set must not inflate the denominator.

title: Consistency of the Enrichment Eligibility Universe
requirement: When overlap or enrichment is claimed, the GAHT sets, reference set, and hypergeometric universe must be defined over the same clearly stated eligible protein population, with exclusions and denominator effects inspectably accounted for.

title: Coherent Enrichment Universe and Set Denominators
requirement: When claiming overlap enrichment, define a universe that contains every protein in both the tested GAHT set and the sex-associated reference set, and use denominators and percentages consistent with that same universe and set definition.

title: Effect-size pattern assessment beyond thresholded overlap
requirement: When making claims about overall proteomic resemblance or concordance, assess the continuous effect estimates across the matched protein universe, rather than relying only on significance-selected overlap and sign counts.

title: Alignment between claims and analyzed comparators
requirement: Claims comparing GAHT with a comparator must be limited to comparators and contrasts actually analyzed in the submitted work.

title: Avoidance of selective or double-counted comparator estimates
requirement: When multiple comparator estimates exist for each protein, the analysis must use a prespecified, non-duplicative comparison rule and disclose the resulting selection or multiplicity limitation, ideally with age-stratum sensitivity results when selecting one estimate.

title: Effect-size correspondence beyond thresholded overlap
requirement: When making a broad claim that GAHT and a comparator share a protein-level pattern, assess the relationship of effect estimates across the matched protein universe in addition to thresholded significant-set overlap, and distinguish global effect correspondence from significance-based concordance.

title: Consistency between computation and reported claims
requirement: When reporting quantitative comparison results, the stated counts, denominators, classifications, and examples must be directly reproducible from the documented code and the same analysis definition; do not substitute a GAHT-significant total for a joint overlap or carry results from a different comparator/selection rule into the final claim.

title: Consistency of estimand and reported results
requirement: When reporting overlap or concordance, the submission must apply one explicitly defined inclusion rule consistently across executable code, intermediate counts, final results, and denominators.

title: Consistency of eligibility rules, denominators, and implementation
requirement: When reporting an overlap or concordance result, the analysis must define whether eligibility requires significance in one or both analyses (and how matched availability is handled), apply that rule consistently in executable calculations and narrative, and label denominators accordingly.

title: Separate significance overlap from effect-size agreement
requirement: When interpreting concordance across comparator phenotypes or strata, distinguish significant-set overlap and sign agreement from agreement in effect magnitudes by reporting comparator-specific effect-size association summaries (or explicitly limiting claims to set-based evidence) and avoiding broad conclusions based on overlap alone.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting analysis
requirement: When reporting computed quantities or derived groupings, the submission must keep the narrative, final answer, code, and intermediate results mutually consistent so that each claimed value is supported by the documented computation.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When reporting quantitative results, the stated values and conclusions must agree with the submitted executable code and directly inspectable intermediate outputs.

title: Claim-to-evidence consistency
requirement: Reported preprocessing decisions, quantitative results, and conclusions must be directly supported by the submitted reproducible code and public intermediate evidence.

title: Complete and justified score-variable coverage
requirement: When the supplied table contains multiple continuous score or probability representations relevant to the clustering question, the analysis must explicitly define the eligible feature set and justify inclusion or exclusion of each relevant representation; omitting an entire class of available score variables without a task-based rationale can materially understate the correlation structure.

title: Consistency of reported analysis scope
requirement: When the submission reports computed results, its final claims must accurately identify the analyzed feature set and distinguish it from un analyzed columns or the full source table, so that the reported matrix dimensions and conclusions are consistent with the documented computation.

title: Primary-score variable selection
requirement: When computing the requested endotype-score correlation structure, the analysis must explicitly define and use a coherent set of primary continuous signature scores, distinguishing them from derived probabilities, categorical labels, and clinical covariates so that mixed variable types do not drive clustering.

title: Evidence for completed generated outputs
requirement: Claims that computations, plots, or other output files were generated must be supported by directly inspectable outputs or execution evidence; code that would generate them is not sufficient proof of completion.

title: End-to-End Reproducibility of Reported Computation
requirement: When the submission claims that code produced its reported results, the documented computation must be executable from the supplied inputs without undefined variables, missing steps, or contradictions between code and reported outputs.

title: Patient-Level Subgroup Stability
requirement: When deriving one subgroup assignment per patient from multiple qualifying records, assess whether subgroup labels vary within patient and make the resulting selection-dependent ambiguity inspectable.

title: Avoidance of Unsupported Subgroup Reclassification
requirement: When the data provide subgroup labels used for the reported proportions, do not replace them with a newly selected score threshold or other undocumented reclassification unless the alternative rule is independently justified and its agreement or disagreement with the supplied labels is inspectably assessed.

title: Internal Arithmetic Consistency
requirement: When reporting subgroup counts and percentages, the stated counts, denominator, percentages, and category total must reconcile internally.

title: Internal Consistency of Duplicate-Record Audit
requirement: When the analysis claims to deduplicate repeated patient or baseline records, its reported duplicate counts, per-patient multiplicities, and sensitivity interpretation must be mutually consistent with the documented cohort counts and aggregation.

title: Accurate Duplicate-Record Accounting
requirement: When the analysis claims to characterize or resolve duplicate patient records, its reported duplicate counts, affected patients, and implications must be consistent with the inspectable cohort data and deduplication procedure.

title: Internal Consistency of Quantitative Interpretation
requirement: Claimed qualitative conclusions, subgroup ordering, and interpretation must agree with the reported counts, percentages, and reproducible computations.

title: Control multiplicity in score-based gene selection
requirement: When gene-set membership is inferred by testing gene–score associations or claiming statistical significance across many candidate genes, account for the multiple-comparison problem with an inspectable correction or equivalent error-control rule before selecting members.

title: Maintain internal consistency between reported findings and supporting evidence
requirement: When reporting a claim supported by quantitative results or code, ensure the prose conclusion agrees with those results and does not state a materially contradictory finding.

title: Consistency between computations and reported results
requirement: When a submission reports computed findings, its final claims must agree with the reproducible code and quantitative intermediate outputs provided in the same submission; contradictory summaries must not assert a different result from the inspectable computation.

title: Maintain consistency between reported findings and supporting analysis
requirement: When claiming computed results, ensure the final answer and interpretive conclusions agree with the submitted code and quantitative intermediate outputs; do not report a value, count, or comparison that contradicts directly inspectable supporting evidence.

title: Validate the analyzed feature universe
requirement: When the supplied expression table’s dimensions, metadata columns, or intended feature subset are ambiguous, explicitly inspect and validate the selected columns and ensure the documented feature universe matches the code and reported results.

title: Align gene-set selection and coherence metrics
requirement: When gene sets are selected using score–gene associations and within-set coherence is then evaluated by correlation, the analysis should use the same association concept for both stages (for example, Spearman in both stages), or explicitly justify and assess the consequences of using different metrics.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting analysis
requirement: When reporting computed findings, ensure that the quantitative claims and interpretations agree with the submitted code and directly inspectable outputs.

title: Maintain consistency between reported findings and supporting evidence
requirement: When reporting computed results, ensure narrative claims and interpretations agree with the directly inspectable code outputs and quantitative evidence, especially for threshold-based classifications or exceptions.

title: Bound conclusions to the verified analysis universe
requirement: When the supplied data do not identify the task’s intended entities or membership universe, explicitly distinguish the operationally reconstructed analysis from the intended universe and limit conclusions accordingly.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Supporting Evidence
requirement: Claimed numerical findings must be consistent across the analysis code, reported tables, output files, and final answer.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with the Tested Analysis Universe
requirement: When claiming computed counts, significance results, or ranked outputs, the response must keep the reported testing universe and numerical summaries consistent with the documented filtering code and generated results.

title: Consistency of the Tested Feature Universe
requirement: When claiming differential-expression counts or ranked results, the artifact must consistently identify which features passed filtering, were actually modeled, and were included in multiple-testing correction.

title: Consistency Between Reported Analysis and Executed Evidence
requirement: Claimed model specifications and computed results must be supported by the submitted analysis code or directly inspectable outputs.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When reporting quantitative results or model specifications, the submitted claims must agree with the executable analysis code and documented intermediate outputs.

title: Expression-prevalence control
requirement: When differential-expression results are presented as genome-wide findings, the analysis must address genes with insufficient expression prevalence so that unstable near-zero tests do not inflate or distort the reported discovery set.

title: Claim-to-execution and evidence consistency
requirement: When claiming that an analysis, computation, sensitivity check, or extremal result was performed, the submission must ensure that the stated model and result are supported by the submitted implementation and directly inspectable execution output; planned code or an absent output must not be presented as completed evidence.

title: Quantitative accounting consistency
requirement: Reported sample, gene, tested-set, filtered-set, and significant-result counts must be internally consistent with the stated filtering rules and analysis universe.

title: Consistency Between Reported Results and Supporting Analysis
requirement: When claiming computed quantitative results, the submission must keep the reported values consistent with the accompanying code and documented intermediate outputs.

title: Claim-to-evidence consistency for computed results
requirement: When reporting quantitative outputs, the submission must make claims that match the supplied executable code and captured results; it must not present unexecuted, missing, or contradictory computation as completed evidence.

title: Consistency Between Reported Results and Executed Analysis
requirement: When reporting computed statistical results, the solution must accurately identify the analysis specification that produced them and distinguish verified outputs from planned, recommended, inherited, or otherwise unverified computations.

title: Result-to-analysis provenance
requirement: When claiming computed differential-expression results, the submission must distinguish executed analyses and their outputs from proposed code, planned reruns, or inherited tables, and must support the claimed model/results relationship with inspectable evidence.

title: Expression filtering and test-set accounting
requirement: When performing gene-level differential-expression testing, the submission must apply and document a defensible low-expression rule and report the resulting gene/sample accounting so that tests are not dominated by near-zero measurements.

title: Alignment of quantitative claims with executed analysis
requirement: When reporting computed differential-expression results, the response must identify the executed model and ensure that the stated covariates, transformations, filters, and results are supported by the same directly inspectable computation; proposed or unexecuted reruns must not be presented as the source of existing estimates.

title: Alignment between reported results and the specified analysis
requirement: When claiming results for a defined analysis, distinguish them from results produced by a materially different exploratory design (for example, different sample inclusion, gene-selection rules, or network parameters); do not use the latter as evidence that the specified analysis was completed.

title: Consistency between claimed execution and supporting evidence
requirement: When reporting computational results, distinguish completed analyses from proposed or unfinished workflows and ensure that the claimed cohort and method match the directly inspectable execution evidence; do not present exploratory mixed-cohort results as results of an ALS-only analysis.

title: Alignment between claimed analysis and executed evidence
requirement: When reporting analytical results, distinguish completed computations from planned or unexecuted workflows and ensure that reported values correspond to the cohort, preprocessing, and method actually used.

title: Covariate-aware disease association testing
requirement: When claiming disease associations for module scores or eigengenes, account for measured technical and demographic covariates relevant to the dataset, or explicitly qualify the result as unadjusted exploratory evidence.

title: Consistency between claimed and executed analysis
requirement: When claiming that an analysis or result was completed, ensure the stated cohort, input data, preprocessing, and method agree with the directly inspectable execution evidence; do not present a planned or contradicted rerun as completed.

title: Consistency between execution evidence and reported results
requirement: When making claims about completed analyses or results, reconcile the executable code, execution logs, and saved artifacts, and distinguish planned or unexecuted analyses from completed computations; do not report results contradicted by the public execution evidence.

title: Consistency between claimed and executed analysis
requirement: When reporting analytical results, distinguish planned methods from completed execution and ensure that cohort, input data, preprocessing, parameters, and reported outputs match the publicly inspectable computation; do not present intended or contradictory exploratory results as completed evidence for the requested analysis.

title: Consistency between claimed analysis and executed evidence
requirement: When describing completed computations or biological results, claims must match the publicly inspectable execution: the actual input files, cohort inclusion, truncation or subsampling, parameters, and generated outputs. Planned code, intended analyses, or historical results must be clearly separated from executed results and must not be presented as completed evidence.

title: Consistency between execution status and reported conclusions
requirement: When describing an analysis, distinguish planned code, completed executions, sensitivity or smoke-test runs, and exploratory results; ensure each quantitative or biological conclusion is attributed only to the execution that demonstrably produced it, without conflating contradictory runs or unsupported artifacts.

title: Execution-evidence alignment for method claims
requirement: When claiming that a specified cohort, data type, preprocessing pipeline, network construction, or statistical procedure was executed, provide direct evidence that the public implementation and execution actually used those choices, rather than merely describing them in a proposed workflow.

title: Consistency between executed analysis and reported conclusions
requirement: When reporting computed methods or results, distinguish executed analyses from planned code, exploratory runs, and intended outputs; do not attribute results to an analysis variant whose public code or execution evidence shows different inputs, cohort, preprocessing, or parameters.

title: Scope calibration for truncated or sensitivity analyses
requirement: When results come from a truncated, resource-limited, compact, or otherwise nonrepresentative input, calibrate biological and general-data conclusions to that run and disclose why its module, enrichment, or replication results cannot stand in for the intended full analysis.

title: Direct evidence for completed quality-control analyses
requirement: When claiming that QC, dimensionality reduction, or batch/covariate diagnostics were performed, provide inspectable outputs or execution evidence showing that those analyses actually ran; metadata fields, prose assertions, or hard-coded summary values do not establish completion.

title: Independence of network-parameter selection from outcome results
requirement: When reporting disease associations from a co-expression network, avoid selecting or changing clustering, filtering, or module-retention parameters after inspecting disease-association results; if exploratory outcome-informed tuning occurs, disclose it and provide sensitivity analysis or independent validation before presenting the resulting associations as confirmatory.

title: Transparent, non-outcome-driven module-parameter selection
requirement: When module-cut or related network parameters are selected or tuned, disclose whether they were chosen before inspecting results and provide a rationale or validation evidence supporting the selected setting; do not present outcome-driven parameter changes as confirmatory findings.

title: Covariate-adjusted disease association testing
requirement: When interpreting module–disease associations, account for relevant measured confounders in the association model, or clearly limit claims to unadjusted exploratory associations; provide direct evidence of the model or test used.

title: Integrity of marker universes across enrichment tests
requirement: When claiming cell-type enrichment, preserve each marker panel and its tested gene universe independently across modules and levels so that filtering one test cannot silently alter later tests; report the resulting universe and overlaps directly.

title: Pre-specification of outcome-determining network parameters
requirement: When presenting module structure or associations as inferential findings, disclose whether choices that materially determine modules—such as clustering cut heights, module-size thresholds, or network parameters—were fixed before inspecting the resulting structure; post hoc tuning must be identified as exploratory rather than presented as an independent confirmatory result.

title: Consistency between claimed findings and reported evidence
requirement: When making substantive claims about computed associations, enrichment, or generated results, ensure that the claim agrees with the directly reported statistics, overlaps, tables, or other inspectable evidence in the submission.

title: Consistency between claimed workflow and reported results
requirement: When attributing reported findings to a completed analysis, ensure the described method, code, output schema, and quantitative results are mutually consistent; do not present results from a different or merely planned workflow as completed findings.

title: Multiplicity control for module–disease associations
requirement: When claiming statistically supported or significant associations between modules and disease, report the number of tested modules and an appropriate multiplicity-adjusted significance measure across those tests; nominal p-values alone do not establish a validated module–disease finding.

title: Multiplicity control for module–disease associations
requirement: When claiming statistical significance for module eigengene or module-score associations with disease, account for the number of modules or other tested associations using an inspectable multiplicity-adjusted result; nominal p-values alone must not be presented as corrected evidence.

title: Cohort-to-result consistency
requirement: When quantitative findings depend on filtering, the reported cohort, sample counts, statistics, and significance calls must remain consistent with the documented filters and recomputable analysis.

title: Execution-status honesty
requirement: Claims about completed analyses, computations, or validation must be clearly distinguished from planned, specified, or unavailable analyses, with direct evidence supporting completed work.

title: Entity identity accuracy
requirement: Names and identifiers used for reported biological entities must accurately correspond to the measured feature and remain consistent throughout the analysis and interpretation.

title: Consistency of reported results with the final analysis cohort
requirement: When a filtering, matching, or preprocessing change alters the analysis cohort, every downstream quantitative claim must be recomputed on that final cohort or explicitly withdrawn; reported statistics, gene rankings, and counts must not be presented as results from a different cohort.

title: Internal consistency of reported results and supporting analysis
requirement: When reporting computed associations, cohort sizes, or filtering effects, the final claims must agree with the submitted code, tables, and documented execution status, including effect direction and the exact analyzed cohort.

title: Cohort-consistent quantitative reporting
requirement: When reporting claim-dependent numerical results, the stated sample cohort, filters, and multiple-testing universe must match the publicly shown computation that produced those results; results from an unfiltered or otherwise different cohort must not be presented as current findings.

title: Alignment of ranking with the requested correlation estimand
requirement: When identifying the strongest gene correlation, the reported transcriptome-wide ranking must be based on the stated correlation measure and clearly distinguished from any covariate-adjusted regression analysis; adjusted coefficients may supplement but must not silently replace the requested correlation ranking.

title: Public support for claimed transcriptome-wide computation
requirement: When claiming transcriptome-wide results, the submission must provide directly inspectable code or output that demonstrably computes the stated screen across the claimed gene set and supports the reported rankings and statistics.

title: Consistency between analysis definition, identifiers, and reported results
requirement: Claimed numerical results, cohort sizes, and entity identities must correspond to the analysis definition and publicly shown computation.

title: Execution–Evidence Consistency
requirement: When claiming that a computation, model, normalization, or result was executed, the submission must provide directly inspectable code and output evidence that supports that claim; planned, illustrative, or incomplete code must not be presented as the source of reported results.

title: Evidence for Claimed Computation and Outputs
requirement: When claiming that a computational analysis, model, or generated result was completed, provide directly inspectable execution evidence linking the stated method to the reported output; do not present placeholder code, undefined variables, or assertions about unseen tables as proof of completion.

title: Execution claims are supported by inspectable outputs
requirement: When claiming that a computation, model, normalization, or result was completed, the submission must distinguish executed work from planned or illustrative code and provide direct public evidence linking the reported result to the executed computation.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When the analysis claims quantitative intermediate results or rankings, those claims must agree with the submitted executable code, stated transformations, and publicly inspectable outputs; material count or value discrepancies must be acknowledged and resolved rather than presented as reproducible results.

title: Consistency between executable analysis and reported quantitative results
requirement: When the artifact reports computed counts, intermediate dimensions, rankings, or final results, those claims must be consistent with the submitted executable code and other public evidence.

title: Consistency of reported quantitative results with the documented computation
requirement: When quantitative intermediate results or final rankings are claimed, the reported values must be directly consistent with the submitted code, transformations, and supplied data; discrepancies must not affect interpretation of the analysis.

title: Deterministic handling of duplicate protein records
requirement: When multiple protein-level records map to one gene, the analysis must use and document a deterministic aggregation or selection rule before three-way matching, preserving interpretable effect-direction and significance evidence.

title: Avoidance of unsupported eligibility cutoffs
requirement: The analysis must not introduce an additional effect-size eligibility threshold that materially excludes candidates unless that threshold is justified by the task or supplied data and its impact is explicitly documented.

title: Deterministic handling of duplicate protein identifiers
requirement: When multiple protein records map to the same gene symbol, the analysis must use and document a deterministic rule for resolving or aggregating those records before the three-way intersection, with the selected effect/significance values and impact on the candidate set inspectable from the submission.

title: Deterministic duplicate-identifier integration
requirement: When a modality contains multiple protein records for the same gene identifier, the analysis must apply a deterministic, documented rule before joining modalities, and the reported counts, effects, and concordance results must correspond to that rule rather than to an uncontrolled many-to-many join.

title: Correct modality-to-file assignment
requirement: When claiming a three-way integration, assign each proteomics file and sheet to the modality it actually represents, and use that assignment consistently in filtering, joins, and reported results.

title: Internal consistency of reported computation
requirement: When reporting computed counts, intersections, exclusions, or rankings, the submitted code, intermediate results, and final claims must describe the same filtering and aggregation pipeline.

title: Internal consistency of reported computed results
requirement: When the submission reports derived numerical results in multiple sections or files, those claims must remain mutually consistent with the documented computation and supporting intermediate outputs.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When reporting computed quantities in multiple sections or files, the submission must keep those claims mutually consistent with the documented intermediate results and supporting outputs.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When reporting derived quantitative results, summary claims must agree with the underlying tables, distributions, code outputs, and other reported totals so that the stated conclusion is reproducible from the submission.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or adjusted values, the submission must ensure that the numerical claims in the narrative and final answer agree with the documented code and publicly reported outputs.

title: Inspectable support for reported computations
requirement: When reporting computed dimensions, cluster assignments, distributions, or statistical results, the submission must include the executable operations needed to reproduce those results within the submitted material, rather than referring only to an unseen implementation or asserting outputs without inspectable support.

title: Executable computational evidence
requirement: When a response claims computed quantitative results, its supplied analysis code must contain executable data-loading and transformation operations that actually implement the described computation, rather than code that would fail or parse the input incorrectly.

title: Executable Analysis Code
requirement: When an artifact claims that quantitative results were produced by included code, the relevant code must be syntactically executable and implement the stated computation.

title: Gene-specific alteration eligibility
requirement: When claiming a MAPK alteration frequency, apply the specified event rules by gene: nonsynonymous mutations for ERBB2, KRAS, HRAS, BRAF, MAP2K1, and ERBB3; only loss-of-function mutations or deep deletions for NF1; and amplification-only CNA calls for EGFR, followed by sample-level deduplication.

title: Internal consistency between computation and reported results
requirement: When reporting computed quantities or statistical results, the artifact must keep the displayed code, table construction, labels, intermediate counts, and final answer mutually consistent.

title: Treatment-timing classification must use available timing annotations
requirement: When the clinical data provide explicit treatment-timing or site annotations, the cohort definition must use those annotations rather than treating an indirect anatomic proxy as equivalent to post-treatment exposure.

title: Executable analysis code matches reported statistical results
requirement: When reporting results from a statistical or set-based computation, the submitted code must unambiguously implement the stated group definitions and produce the reported values; operator precedence or equivalent expression ambiguity must not alter the computed cells or statistics.

title: Post-treatment cohort must include all annotated post-treatment samples
requirement: When reporting a post-treatment HR+/HER2− frequency, the cohort definition must include HR+/HER2− post-treatment primary samples and metastatic samples while excluding treatment-naive primary samples, rather than using metastasis alone as the denominator.

title: Computed contingency results must be unambiguously reproduced by the code
requirement: When claiming a contingency-table statistic or p-value, the submitted computation must use unambiguous set operations whose constructed cells correspond to the reported categories and result.

title: Use explicit treatment-exposure annotations when available
requirement: When the submitted analysis claims to identify post-treatment or treatment-naive tumors, it must use the dataset’s explicit exposure-related annotation and include all samples meeting that definition, rather than substituting an anatomical proxy such as sample type or excluding qualifying post-treatment primary samples.

title: Exposure-status calibration
requirement: When the data do not directly record hormonal-therapy exposure, claims about a post-hormonal-therapy cohort must distinguish verified exposure from a metastatic or other proxy and restrict the conclusion accordingly.

title: Treatment-exposure evidentiary calibration
requirement: When claiming that findings are specific to post-hormonal-therapy tumors, the analysis must distinguish an observed treatment-exposure variable from a proxy such as metastatic status and avoid presenting the proxy as verified exposure.

title: Calibration to alteration operationalization
requirement: When the inferred association depends materially on whether alterations are defined narrowly or broadly, the analysis must identify that dependence rather than presenting one heterogeneous alteration definition as an unqualified mechanistic conclusion.

title: Exposure-status calibration
requirement: When the supplied clinical data do not directly record treatment exposure, calibrate post-therapy claims to the observable cohort definition and avoid presenting an anatomical or metastatic proxy as verified hormonal-treatment exposure.

title: Consistency of Quantitative Claims with Supporting Analysis
requirement: When reporting computed counts or statistics, the answer must agree with the documented code and intermediate outputs, so the claimed result is directly auditable.

title: Consistency of quantitative claims with supporting analysis
requirement: When reporting computed quantities, the final claims must agree with the submitted calculation code, intermediate results, and contingency table.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When an artifact claims computed results, its reported statistics and conclusions must agree with the accompanying executable code, intermediate outputs, and stated contingency data.

title: Complete integration of supplied alteration modalities
requirement: When claiming to assess MAPK pathway alterations, the analysis must incorporate both mutation and copy-number evidence from the supplied files into the primary sample-level endpoint, rather than silently treating mutations alone as the complete alteration class.

title: Explicitly qualify unobserved treatment exposure
requirement: When the data lack a direct treatment-exposure variable, claims about post-hormonal-therapy status must label the selected cohort as a proxy and state that treatment exposure is unverified, rather than presenting the proxy as proven post-treatment evidence.

title: Calibrated treatment-exposure claims
requirement: When treatment exposure is not directly recorded for some included samples, the analysis must distinguish the observable cohort proxy from verified post-hormonal-therapy exposure and avoid presenting the proxy as proven treatment history.

title: Use of all explicitly eligible post-treatment sample types
requirement: When the clinical annotations provide multiple observable sample categories consistent with the target post-treatment cohort, the cohort definition must include those categories or justify their exclusion rather than silently restricting analysis to only one category.

title: Separation of statistical significance from effect-size prioritization
requirement: When claiming that genes are “most significantly” downregulated while also presenting effect-size or biological rankings, the response must explicitly distinguish q-value/p-value ordering from log2-fold-change ordering and identify ties or edge cases that prevent treating one ordering as the other.

title: Internal Consistency of Quantitative Claims
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or results, ensure the final claims agree with the submitted code and intermediate outputs, without transcription, arithmetic, or value-substitution errors.

title: Distinguishes effect-size and significance rankings
requirement: When presenting a ranked differential-expression list, the response must state which metric determines the ordering and must not describe an effect-size-ranked list as a significance-ranked list (or vice versa).

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative claims
requirement: Numerical claims repeated across code, intermediate results, tables, and conclusions must remain consistent with the cited data and with one another.

title: Internal consistency of reproducibility claims
requirement: When claiming a computation or intermediate result, the submitted code, reported dimensions/counts, and downstream interpretation must agree with one another and with the supplied files.

title: Internal consistency between analysis trace, code, and supplied data
requirement: When making reproducibility claims, the response must keep reported file dimensions, filtering rationale, and executable code consistent with one another and with the supplied data, so that the stated computation can be independently reconstructed.

title: Separate statistical significance from biological prioritization
requirement: When identifying leading genes or therapeutic targets, distinguish statistical significance ranking from effect-size, expression-level, or biological prioritization, and do not present a biologically prominent gene as the statistically strongest hit without quantitative support.

title: Calibration of peak-call evidence to accessibility claims
requirement: When using peak calls rather than read-depth measurements, distinguish changes in the called peak landscape from quantitative accessibility changes and avoid presenting binary peak presence or peak burden as normalized read coverage or definitive locus-level differential accessibility.

title: Calibration of peak-call evidence to accessibility claims
requirement: When only peak calls or peak-presence proxies are available, distinguish changes in the called peak landscape from read-depth accessibility changes, and qualify conclusions so they do not present peak burden as calibrated locus-level accessibility or definitive differential accessibility.

title: Replicate-reproducibility quantification under differing peak burdens
requirement: When using called-peak overlap to support a condition comparison, quantify within-condition reproducibility with an explicit overlap rule and report denominators or normalized summaries that make comparisons interpretable despite differing library peak counts.

title: Verification of executed inputs and computations
requirement: When claiming that files were loaded, checked, or used to produce results, distinguish available and executed analyses from manifest references, planned commands, or unavailable inputs using directly inspectable evidence.

title: Replicate-level pairing of comparative summaries
requirement: When reporting per-replicate treatment effects or percentages, explicitly pair each treated replicate with its corresponding control or otherwise define the comparison so the denominator and sample identities are inspectable.

title: Evidence of completed quantitative outputs
requirement: When claiming that a computation produced quantitative results, provide direct inspectable output or another public execution artifact supporting those results; code that merely defines or would generate a calculation is insufficient evidence of completion.

title: Calibrated interpretation of peak-call proxies
requirement: When only thresholded peak intervals are available, distinguish changes in the called peak landscape from changes in calibrated read-level accessibility, and avoid claiming a genome-wide direction or mechanism that the available measurements cannot establish.

title: Evidence for completed computed outputs
requirement: Claims about computed results must be supported by directly inspectable reported outputs or equivalent public evidence, not merely by code that would generate those results if executed.

title: Evidence-calibrated execution and inference claims
requirement: Claims about completed computations, reported outputs, measurement types, and biological conclusions must be limited to what the submitted material directly demonstrates; proxy measurements and missing inputs must not be presented as read-level results or stronger causal/global findings.

title: Calibration of peak-call evidence
requirement: When inferring accessibility changes from peak calls without read-level coverage or normalized counts, distinguish changes in the called peak landscape from quantitative locus-level accessibility and avoid presenting peak-count differences as proof of chromatin closing.

title: Consistency of directional interpretation
requirement: When interpreting directional or condition-specific comparisons, map set membership and quantitative direction to the correct condition and biological meaning, without statements that contradict the reported evidence.

title: Non-circular IDR ordering basis
requirement: When an amino-acid ordering is claimed to represent IDR propensity or another intrinsic property, the ordering must be derived from a single declared reference distribution or external property scale, rather than from the contrast between the two groups being compared.

title: Claim-to-evidence consistency
requirement: When reporting computed results or methodological transformations, the submitted claims must be supported by the accompanying executable code and public intermediate evidence.

title: Consistency between computational claims and supporting evidence
requirement: When the submission claims computed results or a completed analysis, the executable code, reported outputs, tables, and methodological description must agree on the operation performed, dataset/task labels, normalization, ordering, and resulting values.

title: Consistency between computed and reported ordering
requirement: When an amino-acid ordering is claimed or used, the submitted code, intermediate outputs, tables, and final answer must compute and report the same ordering, including any distinction between IDR-profile ordering and full-sequence fold-change display order.

title: Consistency between reported estimands and supporting computation
requirement: Claimed numerical results and interpretations must correspond to the same explicitly defined estimand, filtering population, normalization, and ordering implemented in the submitted code; exploratory per-protein statistics must not be presented as pooled-residue results, and reported labels or vectors must not contradict executable code or audit output.

title: Consistency Between Reported Results and Supporting Analysis
requirement: When claiming computed results or methodological outputs, the submission must keep its narrative, tables, and executable code mutually consistent, with labels, rankings, statistics, and conclusions matching the inspectable implementation and reported values.

title: Consistency of Label-Overlap Handling
requirement: When classification labels can overlap, the submission must make its overlap policy inspectable and ensure that the executable dataset construction, reported counts, and narrative claims implement the same policy; it must not claim that overlaps were removed, relabeled, or excluded when the code retains them.

title: Pre-analysis identifier and label-integrity validation
requirement: When claiming to validate the input dataset, explicitly test before downstream grouping for duplicate protein identifiers and invalid values outside the declared binary label domain, and expose the resulting counts or failures in the submitted material.

title: Transparent handling of conflicting class labels
requirement: When a classification task can contain records carrying both the positive and negative label, make the overlap count and its treatment explicit rather than silently dropping, relabeling, or treating those records as unambiguous.

title: Consistency Between Claims, Code, and Reported Results
requirement: Ensure that methodological claims, reported numerical results, and executable code agree with one another and that claimed computations are directly reproducible from the submitted material.

title: Executable support for derived ordering claims
requirement: When claiming that an IDR- or property-derived amino-acid ordering was computed and applied, the submission must provide executable code that defines the ordering from the reported data, applies it to the stated outputs, and exposes the resulting order or tables for inspection.

title: Inspectability of Reported Computations
requirement: When claiming that a computation produced quantitative results or a derived ordering, provide direct, inspectable output in the submission or executable code that deterministically emits the claimed result; do not rely solely on prose assertions that an unshown run produced it.

title: Claim-to-Code Reproducibility
requirement: For any claimed computed result, the submitted material must provide executable, internally consistent code whose referenced functions, variables, transformations, and ordering logic are defined and match the stated result; prose claims or code containing undefined loaders or omitted result-producing steps do not establish completion.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Public Computation
requirement: When the submission makes quantitative claims about dataset dimensions, sample counts, ordering, or derived outputs, those claims must be directly supported by the accompanying executable code and publicly inspectable results.

title: Claim-to-code and execution consistency
requirement: Claimed computations, dataset properties, and quantitative results must be directly supported by the submitted executable code and must not contradict the code’s actual inputs, definitions, or operations.

title: Direct auditability of reported quantitative results
requirement: For claimed computed outputs that are central to the requested comparison, the submission must provide directly inspectable result values or generated tables, rather than only asserting that code emits them or referring to unavailable output.

title: Consistency Between Claimed Analysis and Public Evidence
requirement: When claiming that a computation was executed or that a result follows from it, the artifact must provide directly inspectable code and outputs that implement the stated operation and support the claim without contradictory descriptions or undefined functions.

title: Consistency Between Reported Results and Supporting Evidence
requirement: When quantitative findings are claimed, the reported values and conclusions must agree with the submitted executable code, intermediate outputs, and other public supporting evidence.

title: Consistency between reported quantitative results and supporting computation
requirement: When the response reports quantitative findings as results of its analysis, those findings must agree with the directly inspectable computations, code outputs, or other public evidence provided in the submission.

title: Consistency Between Reported Claims and Supporting Analysis
requirement: When quantitative results or interpretations are claimed, they must agree with the submitted code, stated variable definitions, labels, amino-acid ordering, and reported intermediate outputs.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency and execution evidence
requirement: When reporting computed quantities or completed analyses, the artifact must provide inspectable support that the reported values agree with the shown computation and that the computation was actually executed.

title: Consistency between quantitative claims and supporting analysis
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or conclusions, the submission must keep the reported values and interpretations consistent with the supplied executable computation and displayed evidence.

title: Correct scope of statistical comparisons
requirement: When interpreting a statistical comparison, the submission must identify the compared groups and avoid treating evidence for one estimand as evidence for a different comparison.

title: Auditable validation and intermediate results
requirement: When claiming that data validation, filtering, overlap checks, or other intermediate computations were completed, the submission must provide inspectable computation and concrete resulting counts or outputs.

title: Consistency of reported claims with supporting evidence
requirement: When reporting computed values, rankings, or comparative conclusions, the final claims must agree with the directly inspectable supporting tables, code outputs, and quantitative results.

title: Consistency Between Computation, Reported Values, and Interpretation
requirement: Assesses whether quantitative claims, labels, comparisons, and interpretations are consistent with the supplied executable code, stated ordering, tables, and reported outputs.

title: Quantitative Traceability of Reported Intermediate Results
requirement: Assesses whether claimed validation, filtering, sample-size, and benchmark results are directly inspectable in the submitted analysis rather than merely asserted.

title: Quantitative claim-to-evidence consistency
requirement: When reporting computed quantities, the artifact must preserve the correspondence between code, labels, ordering, units, and reported values so that each numerical or categorical conclusion is directly checkable from its public supporting material.

title: Multiplicity-aware interpretation of multi-feature tests
requirement: When making inferential claims across multiple amino-acid or other feature-level tests, the artifact must account for the multiplicity of those tests before presenting features as statistically supported findings.

title: Consistency of reported claims with supporting computations
requirement: When the artifact makes quantitative or comparative claims, those claims must agree with the stated ordering, displayed values, and code or other public computational evidence.

title: Non-overlapping interval handling in pooled region analyses
requirement: When pooled sequence content is derived from multiple intervals for the same entity, overlapping or adjacent intervals must not cause the same underlying residues to be counted more than once.

title: Sensitivity across supplied dataset versions
requirement: When the task supplies alternative membership-list versions or cohorts, analyze them as distinct sensitivity populations rather than silently selecting or mixing one version, and report which comparisons are evaluable in each.

title: Consistency of aggregate summaries with reported pairwise results
requirement: When reporting group-level metrics derived from pairwise results, the aggregates and resulting conclusions must be arithmetically reproducible from the reported component values.

title: Consistent exclusion of invalid metrics from comparative summaries
requirement: When a submission declares a dataset–predictor result ineligible under its stated validity or minimum-sample rule, it must not use that result in group comparisons or present it as an estimable comparative metric; any retained exploratory value must be clearly separated from the primary aggregation and conclusions.

title: Separation of exploratory and formal results under inadequate class support
requirement: When a dataset–predictor comparison fails the stated class-size or validity rule, distinguish any descriptive estimate from formal group aggregation and inferential conclusions; do not use the invalid comparison as a supported control contrast.

title: Direct support for reported derived results
requirement: Claimed computed metrics must be directly inspectable in submitted executable code or captured output, with reported values derived from that computation rather than manually entered constants or unsupported post-processing.

title: Evidence-backed execution and computation claims
requirement: When claiming that analyses, aggregations, or generated results were executed, the submission must provide directly inspectable computational evidence linking the reported outputs to the stated procedure.

title: Execution provenance for reported computations
requirement: When claiming that numerical results were computed or reproduced, the submission must distinguish executable analysis from illustrative code and provide inspectable evidence linking the reported values to the executed computation.

title: Executable background-set fidelity
requirement: When claiming a fixed background benchmark, the submitted computation must demonstrably use the complete intended background set—not merely background proteins intersecting an auxiliary membership table—and must report counts that reconcile with that construction.

title: Validated identifier joins for auxiliary scores
requirement: When predictor values or labels are imported from another table, the analysis must validate the identifier interpretation and duplicate handling before using those values in performance calculations.

title: Claim–computation–result reconciliation
requirement: When multiple analytical passes, tables, or output files are presented, the submission must identify one authoritative computation and ensure that the stated conclusions and reported values are generated by, and consistent with, that computation.

title: Authoritative-result consistency
requirement: When the submission includes exploratory, revised, or superseded analyses, it must clearly identify which computation is authoritative and ensure that the reported conclusions, tables, and claimed statistics agree with that computation rather than leaving materially conflicting results presented as final.

title: Sensitivity across supplied cohort variants
requirement: When the analysis uses or makes claims about multiple supplied membership-list or cohort variants, it must preserve their identities and report how the evaluated performance changes across those variants rather than silently substituting one population for another or implying robustness from a single variant.

title: Superseded-result provenance
requirement: When an analysis contains multiple computational passes or revisions, reported conclusions and tables must be explicitly tied to the authoritative executed pass, while obsolete intermediate outputs are clearly marked as superseded and excluded from the final evidence.

title: Validated ID-resolution and observation integrity
requirement: When claiming an ID-resolved benchmark, every score-label join must use a publicly justified identifier mapping and preserve one unambiguous observation per protein; unsupported interpretation of unlabeled ID columns, duplicate expansion, or sequence-to-protein joins must not contribute to reported results.

title: Claim–output consistency for reported results
requirement: When reporting computed results, the narrative, tables, audit counts, and executable computation must refer to the same final analysis; superseded or exploratory outputs must not be presented as authoritative results.

title: Authoritative-result provenance
requirement: When an analysis contains exploratory, superseded, or revised computations, the submitted material must clearly segregate obsolete outputs from authoritative results so that reported conclusions, tables, and cited files all trace to the same final computation.

title: Authoritative result–computation consistency
requirement: When presenting a reproducible analysis, the authoritative code, reported tables, counts, and conclusions must refer to the same computation; superseded or exploratory outputs must be clearly marked and excluded from final claims.

title: Evidence-supported dataset categorization
requirement: When grouping membership flags into MLO participants, membrane-bound controls, or other sets, the submission must use an explicit classification supported by the task or data; ambiguously classified sets must be reported separately rather than silently included in a group aggregate.

title: Authoritative-result provenance
requirement: When the submission contains multiple computational passes, revisions, or generated result tables, it must identify which computation is authoritative and ensure that reported conclusions and tables derive from that computation rather than from superseded outputs.

title: Complete predictor and sensitivity coverage
requirement: When claiming to evaluate the supplied screening task, the analysis must include the available predictor score columns and the requested dataset/sensitivity sheets, or explicitly document why a supplied predictor or sheet cannot be evaluated.

title: Traceability of Reported Quantitative Results
requirement: For every claimed aggregate or headline quantitative result, the submitted material must provide directly inspectable executable computation and/or a public structured output that reproduces the claim, with no contradiction between the code, output, and narrative.

title: Inspectable support for completed computations
requirement: When the submission claims that computed summaries or results were produced, it must provide directly inspectable executable computation and corresponding output evidence, rather than relying only on prose claims or links to inaccessible files.

title: Directly reviewable completeness of requested results
requirement: When a complete set of per-comparison results is claimed, the submission must make the full requested result set directly reviewable, including invalid or omitted comparisons and the associated counts needed to interpret them.

title: Directly Inspectable Evidence for Aggregated Results
requirement: When reporting group-level or otherwise derived quantitative summaries, provide directly inspectable executed code and an output artifact containing those summaries, with the aggregation inputs and exclusions traceable to the underlying per-comparison results.

title: Complete requested predictor coverage
