requirement: When claiming comprehensive screening, the analysis must evaluate all requested and available predictor columns, or explicitly identify and justify each exclusion so omitted predictors cannot silently narrow the comparison.

title: Inspectable support for aggregate claims
requirement: Claimed group-level summaries or contrasts must have directly inspectable evidence in the submission showing how the reported aggregation was computed from the underlying per-comparison results.

title: Traceable claim-to-evidence consistency
requirement: When the submission claims computed values, aggregates, or conclusions derived from them, those claims must be directly supported by inspectable code and/or public output, and must not contradict the reported results.

title: Inspectably supported derived summaries
requirement: When claiming group-level or other derived performance summaries, the submission must provide directly inspectable evidence linking those values to the underlying per-comparison results, such as executable aggregation code or a complete public results table.

title: Inspectable evidence for reported aggregates
requirement: When reporting computed group-level statistics or contrasts, the submission must provide directly inspectable executable aggregation code and a generated or embedded result table whose values support the claims.

title: Consistent ORA universe and pathway membership
requirement: When claiming an ORA result, the pathway size and overlap counts must be defined within the same declared background universe used by the hypergeometric or Fisher contingency table; pathway annotations outside that universe must not be combined with a background-restricted universe.

title: Traceable universe provenance
requirement: When an ORA result depends on a declared gene universe, the universe must be directly supported by the supplied data or explicitly documented external evidence, with its construction and provenance inspectable; an arbitrary or undocumented universe must not drive the reported inference.

title: Evidence-supported analysis universe
requirement: When claiming an ORA result, the declared population universe must be directly derived from supplied data or tied to an explicitly identified, available reference source; an undocumented external universe must not determine the reported inference.

title: Consistency between reported statistics and significance claims
requirement: When claiming significance or non-significance, the artifact must make conclusions that logically agree with its reported p-values, adjusted values, and stated thresholds.

title: Consistency between reported significance claims and p-values
requirement: When claiming nominal significance or non-significance, the conclusion must correctly apply the stated p-value threshold to the reported unadjusted p-value.

title: Consistency of quantitative results with the documented computation
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, counts, or adjusted values, the reported results must match the directly inspectable computation and its stated testing family.

title: Observable-background consistency in contingency tables
requirement: When performing ORA against a stated detectable-gene background, pathway membership used in the contingency table must be restricted to genes present in that background; genes outside the universe must not inflate pathway counts or alter the nonmembership cell.

title: Universe-consistent enrichment tables
requirement: When reporting or computing over-representation statistics, pathway membership and nonmembership must be defined within the same stated detectable background as the query set; full gene-set sizes may be reported descriptively but must not be mixed into the tested contingency table.

title: Universe consistency in contingency tables
requirement: When an enrichment test claims a stated background universe, every cell of each contingency table must classify genes within that same universe; pathway genes absent from the background may be reported descriptively but must not be counted as background members in the test.

title: Execution Evidence Matches Reported Results
requirement: When claiming that computations or generated results were executed, the submitted material must provide inspectable computational evidence corresponding to the reported results, rather than code that is merely plausible, planned, or inconsistent with the outputs.

title: Evidence-backed computation
requirement: When claiming that numerical results were computed or reproduced, the submission must provide direct, inspectable evidence linking those results to executed calculations, rather than relying only on unexecuted code or prose assertions.

title: Internal set-definition consistency
requirement: The gene-set definition and counts must remain consistent across extraction, overlap construction, contingency-table calculation, and reported results.

title: Consistency between computation and reported results
requirement: When reporting computed statistical results, the stated testing scope, contingency-table construction, and numerical outputs must be mutually consistent with the submitted analysis code and its documented intermediate results.

title: Faithful and internally consistent hypothesis scope
requirement: When the task specifies a supplied pathway collection or complete test family, the analysis must test that stated family without unsupported exclusions, and the reported pathway count, multiple-testing correction, ranking, and conclusion must correspond to the pathways actually tested.

title: Universe-consistent ORA contingency tables
requirement: When performing ORA with a specified background universe, pathway-membership counts in every contingency table must be restricted to genes present in that universe; out-of-universe pathway genes must not be counted as non-query pathway members.

title: Multiplicity and ranking consistency
requirement: When reporting a ranked multiple-testing analysis, the stated test set, multiplicity count, BH correction, pathway ranks, and displayed results must consistently refer to the same analyzed pathway collection.

title: Evidence-supported attribution of computational discrepancies
requirement: When claiming that a reported result was corrected because of a discrepancy in prior computation or output, the submission must provide inspectable evidence for the discrepant computation or output, rather than relying on an absent auxiliary file or unverified artifact.

title: Correct handling of tied event times
requirement: When tied event times are present and a Breslow Cox analysis is claimed, the submitted analysis must use a common risk-set denominator for all events at each tied time, with results and code consistent with that implementation.

title: Consistency of reported results with computational evidence
requirement: When numerical results are claimed, the submitted code, exported outputs, cross-checks, and narrative must reconcile to the same values and conclusion rather than leaving material contradictions unresolved.

title: Validity and transparency of the predictor scale
requirement: When hazard ratios are reported, the fitted predictor transformation and the scale of the HR must be explicitly defined and mathematically consistent with the model and p-value used for the claim.

title: Consistency between stated analysis, executable implementation, and reported results
requirement: When an analysis claims completed computations, its documented preprocessing, model specification, test calculation, and reported statistics must agree with the inspectable code and outputs.

title: Consistency of inferential p-value calculation
requirement: When a two-sided Wald p-value is claimed, the submitted computation and reported result must use a mathematically consistent tail calculation without double-counting the two-sided probability.

title: Consistency between stated and executed analysis specification
requirement: When reporting a computed analysis, the stated preprocessing and model specification must match the inspectable code and numerical results used to support the claims.

title: Consistency between reported results and authoritative analysis
requirement: When an analysis presents a primary workflow and quantitative results, the reported statistics and conclusions must be generated by, and remain consistent with, that same documented workflow; superseded alternatives must not be presented as the primary result.

title: Correct calibration of reported inferential p-values
requirement: When statistical significance or p-values are claimed, the reported p-values must use the stated test's correct tail calibration and match the displayed statistic, code, and independent check where provided.

title: Consistency between claimed analysis and reported results
requirement: When reporting computed results, the submission must identify one authoritative analysis specification and ensure that its code, data transformations, statistical settings, output values, and conclusions agree with one another.

title: Consistency of reported results with the authoritative analysis specification
requirement: When an analysis presents a primary workflow and quantitative conclusions, the preprocessing choices, tie method, effect-size scale, statistical calculation, and reported results must agree with one another and with the cited output.

title: Correct computation and reporting of two-sided Wald p-values
requirement: When significance is based on a one-degree-of-freedom Wald statistic, the reported two-sided p-value must be computed from the correct two-sided tail and used consistently for thresholding.

title: Accurate labeling of effect-size scale
requirement: When hazard ratios are reported, the unit of a one-unit increase must match the transformation actually used in the fitted model.

title: Consistency of aggregate counts with the complete result table
requirement: When a complete per-feature result table is claimed, summary counts of tested or qualifying features must be directly supported by that table and the stated threshold rule.

title: Executable trace consistency
requirement: When claiming that an analysis is reproducible, the submitted code must use defined objects and column names that correspond to the documented data transformations and reported output schema.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When the artifact claims that an analysis was executed and reports its outputs, the documented code, exported-result schema, numerical findings, and final conclusion must describe the same computation rather than materially contradicting one another.

title: Estimand-scale consistency
requirement: When a feature transformation or measurement scale changes the Cox estimand, claims and threshold decisions must be explicitly tied to one identified scale and must not combine results from incompatible scales as though they were one analysis.

title: Alignment of estimand, computation, and reported outputs
requirement: When reporting claim-conditional Cox results, the stated abundance scale or transformation, executable analysis, exported results, rankings, and final conclusion must refer to the same estimand.

title: Public reproducibility of claimed analysis outputs
requirement: Claims of completed feature-wide computation must be directly checkable against the submitted executable code and available output schema or contents.

title: Consistency of Analysis, Code, and Reported Outputs
requirement: When results are claimed, the documented analysis code, stated estimand/scale, reported statistics and rankings, and any delivered output schema must agree and be inspectably traceable; material contradictions or reliance on unavailable outputs undermine reproducibility.

title: Evidence for Claimed Computational Validation
requirement: When an artifact claims an independent implementation check or reproduced result, it must provide direct, inspectable evidence showing what was run and that the validation agrees with the primary analysis.

title: Public support for claimed computation and results
requirement: When claiming completed model fitting or numerical outputs, the submission must provide inspectable evidence linking the stated computation to the reported results, such as executable analysis code and a matching exported output; prose assertions or syntax-only checks are insufficient.

title: Consistency of estimand and complete result table
requirement: When reporting a primary analysis alongside transformed or sensitivity analyses, the submission must keep the stated primary estimand, per-feature table, ranking, qualifying-feature count, and focal-feature conclusion aligned; results from different scales or analyses must not be mixed.

title: Independent validation of focal numerical result
requirement: When a focal association is claimed from a custom or nonstandard implementation, the submission must provide direct, inspectable corroboration of that focal result using an independent implementation or equivalent validation evidence.

title: Cross-artifact result consistency
requirement: When reporting numerical findings or rankings, the answer, trace, code, and delivered result table must refer to the same estimand and agree on the corresponding values, schema, and feature ordering.

title: Direct evidence for executed computation
requirement: Claims that an implementation, independent check, or exported result was executed must be supported by inspectable executed output or a reproducible artifact, rather than only prose assertions or code that could have been run.

title: Claim-to-artifact consistency
requirement: When an analysis reports generated tables, rankings, or quantitative results, those claims must remain consistent with the submitted code and delivered outputs, including the stated transformation or estimand.

title: Evidence for claimed execution and validation
requirement: When the response claims that a computation, generated result, or independent implementation check was executed, the submission must provide directly inspectable supporting code and/or output rather than only prose assertions.

title: Separation of estimands across analyses
requirement: When multiple representations or sensitivity analyses are reported, results must be explicitly attributed to the corresponding feature scale or transformation and must not be combined across estimands.

title: Claim–evidence consistency
requirement: When reporting computed results, the stated primary analysis, transformation, deduplication rule, numerical summaries, rankings, and qualifying set must agree with the submitted code and delivered outputs.

title: Inspectably reproducible computation
requirement: When claiming that models, sensitivity analyses, or result tables were computed, provide sufficient executable analysis code and directly inspectable generated evidence to reproduce and verify those claims.

title: Internally consistent quantitative reporting
requirement: When the analysis makes the same cohort or result claim in multiple places, the reported quantities must agree with the documented matching and computation.

title: Inspectably supported computational claims
requirement: Claims about completed analyses and generated results must be supported by submitted, reproducible evidence sufficient to inspect the relevant computation and outputs.

title: Inspectable support for claimed output artifacts
requirement: When claiming that a generated result file or complete output is included, the submission must make that artifact directly inspectable or provide a verifiable, accessible representation; prose claims or links to an unavailable file do not establish its presence.

title: Consistency of matched-cohort quantities
requirement: Claimed cohort counts and event counts must remain consistent across the final answer, analysis trace, and reported results, especially after filtering or joining records.

title: Consistency of reported statistics with supporting computation
requirement: When claiming computed results, the reported statistics and output description must agree with the publicly supplied code and generated output.

title: Claim-to-execution and output traceability
requirement: Claims about completed computation or generated result tables must be directly supported by inspectable execution evidence or a public output whose schema and values match the documented code; prose claims or code that was not shown to produce the claimed result are insufficient.

title: Consistency of estimand and model specification
requirement: The reported hazard ratios and significance conclusions must correspond to the documented predictor scale, replicate handling, tie method, and other model choices; changing these choices without clearly identifying a separate estimand must not be presented as the same analysis.

title: Evidence-based handling of repeated measurements
requirement: When multiple microbiome records share a sample identifier, the analysis must explicitly apply a defensible sample-level handling rule before survival modeling and ensure the reported results use that same rule.

title: Claim–computation agreement
requirement: Claimed statistical results and methodological descriptions must agree with the publicly inspectable code and generated outputs, including the aggregation rule, predictor scale, tie handling, and reported HR/p-values.

title: Alignment between reported results and public computation
requirement: When computed results or methodological choices are claimed, the submitted code, described procedure, and public result artifact must agree on the data handling, model specification, units, and reported numerical outputs.

title: Claim-to-computation traceability
requirement: When reporting computed results, the submission must provide executable, internally consistent analysis code and inspectable output supporting the stated data handling, model specification, estimand, and numerical results.

title: Execution-to-claim reproducibility
requirement: When claiming computed statistical results, the submission must provide inspectable executable analysis and generated output whose preprocessing, model specification, estimand, and reported values agree with the claimed result.

title: Execution-to-claim alignment
requirement: When the submission claims completed computation or generated results, its publicly shown executable code and result artifacts must implement the same data handling, model specification, and reported values.

title: Directly test and report regimen-by-time differences
requirement: When making claims about whether CPA and SPIRO changes differ, perform a direct comparison of subject-level paired changes (or an equivalent interaction test) with multiplicity correction, and report its outcome separately from within-regimen significance.

title: Make claimed protein-level results directly auditable
requirement: When claiming complete protein-level results, provide the relevant identifiers, effect estimates, significance values, and direction in the submitted material or directly inspectable public output rather than relying on an unavailable generated file or prose assertion.

title: Direct regimen-interaction support
requirement: When asserting that protein changes differ—or do not differ—between regimens, the submission must support that claim with a direct protein-level comparison of subject-level changes, appropriate multiplicity correction, and inspectable effect-size and adjusted-significance results; separate within-regimen significance must not be treated as evidence of an interaction.

title: Auditability of claimed result outputs
requirement: When relying on generated result files or tables for protein-level claims, the documented schema and claimed contents must match the inspectable output, so directions, statistics, and significance labels can be reproduced from submitted material rather than from an asserted unseen field.

title: Consistency of Claimed Analysis Artifacts
requirement: When the submission claims to create or use machine-readable result files or other generated outputs, those claims must be directly supported by the shown code or inspectable output, and the reported schema, row counts, and contents must agree with that evidence.

title: Directly test regimen-by-time differences
requirement: When claiming that protein changes differ between regimens, directly compare participant-level paired changes with an explicit between-regimen test and multiplicity correction; do not infer regimen differences from separate within-regimen significance or set overlap.

title: Evidence-backed result artifacts
requirement: When claims depend on generated result files or tables, the submitted material must provide directly inspectable evidence whose schema, row scope, and contents agree with the claims; code or prose alone is insufficient proof of the claimed output.

title: Direct regimen-interaction analysis
requirement: When claiming that protein changes differ between CPA and SPIRO, directly compare participant-level paired changes between regimens, apply multiplicity correction across proteins, and report inspectable effect sizes, test statistics or p-values, adjusted values, and the resulting conclusion; do not infer regimen differences from significance in one arm versus the other or from overlap counts alone.

title: Defined-test handling in multiplicity correction
requirement: When some protein-level statistical tests yield undefined or non-finite p-values, claims based on adjusted results must explicitly identify those tests as untestable, exclude them from the multiplicity correction, and report the resulting tested-assay scope and counts.

title: Reconciled scope of data-quality accounting
requirement: Claimed data-quality totals must distinguish whole-file counts from analysis-subset counts and reconcile with the stated filtering operations and resulting row totals.

title: Valid handling of undefined test results in multiplicity correction
requirement: When reporting multiplicity-adjusted significance across many features, undefined or non-finite test results must be treated as untestable rather than passed into the correction procedure or interpreted as significant; the submission must document their handling and reconcile the tested-feature count with the reported adjusted results.

title: Explicit handling of undefined feature-level tests
requirement: When feature-level tests can yield undefined or non-finite statistics, the analysis must identify those features, exclude or otherwise validly handle them during multiplicity correction, and report the resulting tested universe and impact on counts.

title: Public support for reported quantitative conclusions
requirement: Claimed computed results, especially interaction findings, must be supported by inspectable code and public output that actually produce the reported statistics and conclusions; prose claims alone are insufficient.

title: Defined handling of untestable statistical contrasts
requirement: When feature-level tests produce undefined statistics or p-values, the analysis must identify those features as untestable and exclude undefined values from multiplicity correction rather than silently passing them into the correction or treating them as significant results.

title: Accurate dataset schema and dimensions
requirement: Reported file dimensions, column counts, and named fields must match the supplied data and remain consistent with the documented analysis.

title: Auditable support for reported computations
requirement: When claiming computed numerical results, provide directly inspectable evidence linking the result to the shown analysis, rather than relying solely on planned code, unseen generated files, or prose assertions.

title: Direct and reproducible regimen-interaction analysis
requirement: When claiming that changes differ or do not differ between regimens, implement and report a valid comparison of matched subject-level baseline-to-follow-up changes, with multiplicity correction, distinct from comparing within-regimen significance results.

title: Inspectable evidence for reported computations
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, significance sets, overlap counts, or result tables, the artifact must provide direct inspectable evidence of the computation or generated output, rather than treating executable code or an unshown file as proof that the claimed result was produced.

title: Direct inference about regimen-by-time differences
requirement: When the task asks whether regimens differ, the artifact must directly test the difference in participant-level baseline-to-follow-up changes and distinguish that inference from comparing within-regimen significance or overlapping significant-protein sets.

title: Evidence for reported computed results
requirement: When claiming numerical outputs, generated tables, overlap lists, or reproducibility, the artifact must provide directly inspectable output or clearly distinguish executable code from results that were not included.

title: Consistency between computation and reported results
requirement: When claiming computed rankings, counts, direction summaries, or other derived results, the submitted analysis must use code and reported outputs that implement the same method and agree with one another.

title: Consistency of reported summaries with computed results
requirement: When reporting computed counts, directions, rankings, or other quantitative summaries, ensure they are consistent with the supplied data and the documented filtering or aggregation code.

title: Separation of association from causal or mechanistic claims
requirement: When interpreting observational or modeled associations, distinguish the observed association from causal, mediating, or mechanistic explanations and label unsupported explanations as hypotheses.

title: Consistency of reported directions with computed evidence
requirement: When reporting effect directions, sign counts, or interpretations for a claimed result, the submission must keep those claims consistent with the supplied estimates and with its own filtering and ranking computations.

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Computations
requirement: When reporting computed counts, directions, rankings, or overlaps, the narrative, code outputs, and intermediate results must agree with one another; claimed summaries must not materially contradict the documented calculation.

title: Cross-check reported results against computations
requirement: When claiming computed counts, direction totals, rankings, or other derived results, ensure that the final claims, intermediate results, and supporting code/output agree arithmetically and follow the stated ordering or filtering rule.

title: Consistency of quantitative claims with the reported computation
requirement: When the response reports computed counts, signs, rankings, or other derived numerical findings, those claims must agree with the filtering and aggregation logic and with the presented execution evidence.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims
requirement: Claimed counts, rankings, and other computed results must agree with the submitted code, intermediate outputs, and directly inspectable source-data calculations.

title: Calibration of causal and contribution claims
requirement: Interpretive claims must not infer causation, mediation, or the magnitude of a contributor from association results that do not identify those quantities.

title: Consistency between computations and reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed counts, directions, or memberships, the narrative must agree with the supplied executable analysis and its inspectable outputs; contradictions between code-derived results and prose are penalized.

title: Scope-calibrated interpretation of observational associations
requirement: When making contextual or mechanistic claims from summary association results, the interpretation must not assert quantified contribution, causality, mediation, or major explanatory importance that the supplied analysis cannot establish.

title: Consistent enrichment reference universe
requirement: When claiming enrichment, define the GAHT significant set, comparison universe, and overlap within the same identifier-controlled population; do not use a GAHT count from one measurement universe with a denominator or null universe that excludes or includes different proteins without explicit reconciliation.

title: Alignment with the requested comparison
requirement: The analysis must operationalize the comparison asked by the user rather than replacing it with an arbitrary restrictive subset or ranking rule that changes the estimand, unless that restriction is explicitly requested or clearly presented as a separate sensitivity analysis.

title: Coherent enrichment universe and set denominators
requirement: When reporting enrichment, the GAHT set used as K must be defined on the same measured identifier universe as the hypergeometric population, with any complete-source totals and matched-subset totals clearly distinguished; the code and reported values must implement that distinction consistently.

title: Auditable cross-table identifier join
requirement: When claims depend on combining GAHT results with population sex statistics, the submission must provide direct, inspectable evidence that identifiers were normalized and joined correctly, rather than merely asserting that the tables match.

title: Consistency between reported statistics and supporting computation
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed, the submitted code and explanation must use definitions, denominators, identifier sets, and test parameters that actually correspond to the reported counts, percentages, and p-values.

title: Distinguish complete GAHT hits from matched-universe hits
requirement: When claiming GAHT hit totals or overlap percentages, distinguish the complete significant sets from Supplementary Table 1 from the subsets represented in the Supplementary Table 5 analysis universe, and use the matched subset as the hypergeometric K denominator.

title: Regimen-count definition matches the claimed enrichment population
requirement: When reporting GAHT enrichment or the fraction of significant GAHT proteins represented by the overlap, explicitly define whether the regimen count is the full significant GAHT set or only proteins represented in the cross-platform universe, and compute and label that count consistently rather than silently substituting the matched subset.

title: Consistent Enrichment Universe and Population Counts
requirement: When claiming hypergeometric enrichment, define one eligible protein universe and ensure the universe size, GAHT-success count, sex-selected count, and observed overlap all refer to compatible measurement and filtering domains; do not combine a cross-platform universe with GAHT counts from proteins unavailable in that universe.

title: Unsupported regimen-mechanism inference
requirement: When interpreting differences between regimens, do not present pharmacologic potency, mechanism, or broader remodeling as the cause of differing overlap counts unless the submitted analysis directly compares treatment effects and supports that causal claim.

title: Enrichment-universe consistency
requirement: When reporting hypergeometric enrichment, the population universe and regimen-specific significant set must be defined on compatible protein identifiers: every protein counted in K must belong to the stated M universe, and the observed overlap k must be a subset of both K and the tested top set.

title: Use of the specified ranked comparison set
requirement: If the analysis claims to answer a question about the top-ranked sex-associated proteins, it must select that set by descending sex-association strength, retain the specified number of unique identifiers, and not substitute a broad nominal-significance threshold or another unrequested set.

title: Denominator and universe consistency in enrichment claims
requirement: If overlap percentages or enrichment statistics are claimed, the analysis must distinguish the full significant set from the cross-dataset universe-restricted set and use a hypergeometric population whose universe, success count, sample size, and overlap are mutually consistent.

title: Public executability of claimed computations
requirement: If the analysis claims reproducibility, the submitted code for nontrivial computations must be syntactically complete and executable from the described inputs, without stray fragments, malformed block boundaries, or omitted operations needed to produce the reported result.

title: Causal restraint in observational regimen interpretation
requirement: If differences between regimens are interpreted biologically, the analysis must not present observational overlap differences as causal effects of regimen pharmacology without a direct between-regimen comparison and control for relevant confounding.

title: Consistency of Ranking and Enrichment Universe
requirement: When a ranked reference set is compared with an enrichment universe, the ranked set must be selected only from the same eligible universe used for the overlap and null calculation, excluding entities unavailable for matching before ranking.

title: Consistent enrichment universe and top-set construction
requirement: When enrichment is claimed, the ranked sex-associated set and the GAHT sets must be drawn from the same explicitly defined joined protein universe; exclusions from that universe must be applied before ranking and overlap counting.

title: Claim-to-computation numerical consistency
requirement: Reported computed statistics must agree with the supplied executable code or directly inspectable calculation, including enrichment p-values and downstream conclusions.

title: Consistent selection and enrichment universe
requirement: When selecting a ranked reference set for enrichment, the submitted analysis must define that set from the same eligible joined universe used as the enrichment denominator, so proteins outside the tested universe cannot enter the reference set.

title: Bounded interpretation of observational overlap
requirement: Interpretive claims about overlap must remain association-level and must not infer causal mechanisms, biological pathway targeting, or equivalence to a reference population without direct supporting evidence in the submitted material.

title: Internal consistency of reported computations
requirement: When reporting computed counts, overlaps, directions, or statistics, the submission must use definitions and denominators that remain consistent across code, intermediate results, and final conclusions, with discrepancies reconciled from the supplied data.

title: Consistency between executable analysis and reported results
requirement: When claiming completed computations, the submitted code, intermediate outputs, and final reported values must use the same defined data objects, filters, denominators, and selection rules, without unresolved runtime errors or contradictory counts.

title: Consistency between executable analysis and reported results
requirement: Reported quantitative findings must be directly supported by the submitted code and intermediate checks, with no unexplained contradictions in counts, denominators, or filtering outcomes.

title: Consistency Between Computation and Reported Claims
requirement: Claimed quantitative results, exception lists, denominators, and inclusion rules must agree with the executable analysis and with all reported intermediate results.

title: Internal consistency of computational evidence
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed, the submitted code, intermediate outputs, and final narrative must support the same definitions, denominators, counts, and conclusions without contradictions or materially non-reproducible code.

title: Executable and internally consistent reproducibility
requirement: When claiming computed results, the submitted code and trace must define all inputs and intermediate objects, use compatible operations, and support reproduction of the reported outputs without hidden steps or contradictory snippets.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When reporting computed counts, percentages, classifications, or named exceptions, the submitted code and intermediate results must reproduce and support those claims without contradictory values or stale outputs.

title: Null calibration for directional concordance claims
requirement: When interpreting same-direction agreement as non-random or as evidence of meaningful biological consistency, the analysis must define the tested protein universe and provide a reproducible null calibration specifically for directional agreement, including an appropriate test or justified null expectation and its uncertainty or statistical evidence.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When reporting computed quantitative findings, the final claims must agree with the submitted code, intermediate results, and stated denominators; reported counts and percentages must be arithmetically compatible.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting analysis
requirement: When reporting computed counts, percentages, or statistics, the submission must keep those claims consistent with its supplied code and other stated intermediate results.

title: Executable reproducibility of analytical code
requirement: When the submission claims to provide reproducible computation, its code for material data loading and analysis must be syntactically valid and directly runnable from the stated inputs.

title: Cross-check reported results against the supporting computation
requirement: When reporting computed counts or percentages, the answer must agree with the trace’s code and intermediate results, including across primary and sensitivity analyses.

title: Executable reproducibility evidence
requirement: When claiming a reproducible analysis, supplied code must be directly executable as written and visibly support the reported data loading, transformation, and comparison.

title: Alignment of reported results with executable analysis
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed as computed, the submitted code must be copy-paste executable and its reported outputs must agree with the code’s stated filters, denominators, and intermediate results.

title: Internal consistency of reported computations
requirement: When reporting computed quantitative results, the analysis must use the same definitions and inputs across its code, trace, and final answer, with reported values reproducibly matching the displayed computation.

title: Null calibration of concordance claims
requirement: When claiming that protein overlap or same-direction agreement exceeds chance, calibrate each claimed property against an appropriate, explicitly defined null using the analyzed protein universe and report reproducible test inputs and results.

title: Accuracy of comparator-stratum results
requirement: When reporting menopause or other comparator-stratum concordance, the submitted counts and percentages must agree with the stated filtering and direction rules and with reproducible calculations, separately for CPA and SPIRO.

title: Executable support for reported computations
requirement: Claimed quantitative results must be reproducible from the submitted code and public inputs; code must be syntactically valid, self-contained for its stated purpose, and internally consistent with the reported outputs.

title: Consistency of Reported Results With Supporting Computation
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed as computed, the reported values and conclusions must agree with the submitted code and any directly inspectable outputs.

title: Runnable and Self-Contained Reproduction
requirement: When reproducible computation is claimed, the submitted material must contain directly inspectable, runnable code that loads its inputs and defines the required transformations without relying on hidden state or unavailable preceding snippets.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When presenting computed counts or percentages, the submission must use consistent definitions and report the same results across code, intermediate summaries, trace, and final answer.

title: Complement thresholded overlap with effect-size alignment
requirement: When claiming broad proteomic resemblance or global alignment, quantify association between effect-size vectors across the shared protein universe, rather than relying only on significant-set overlap and sign counts.

title: Consistency Between Computation and Reported Results
requirement: Reported quantitative findings must agree with the submitted executable code and with all corresponding intermediate results and summaries.

title: Claim–Execution Evidence Consistency
requirement: When claiming completed computation, filtering, joining, or numerical results, the submission must provide directly inspectable executed output or equivalent public evidence that matches the documented code and reported values; prose, planned code, or internally inconsistent trace/result pairs are insufficient.

title: Separation of Directional and Significance Estimands
requirement: When reporting directional concordance alongside significance overlap, the submission must explicitly distinguish the population eligible for sign comparison from the subset jointly significant under both analyses, and must not present one as evidence for the other without qualification.

title: Executable trace consistency
requirement: When claiming reproducible computation, the submitted trace must contain executable, internally consistent code whose defined variables, transformations, and reported quantitative results support the stated analysis.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting implementation
requirement: When results are claimed as computed, the submitted executable analysis must implement the documented data preparation, estimand, filters, and counting rules and provide direct, inspectable evidence that it produces the reported results.

title: Execution evidence for reported computations and clusters
requirement: When reporting computed correlations, sensitivity checks, or cluster memberships, the submission must provide directly inspectable execution output or independently reproducible evidence tying each material quantitative claim to the documented computation; code and prose assertions alone are insufficient.

title: Claim-to-execution evidence for quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, correlations, cluster memberships, or other generated results, the submission must provide direct, inspectable evidence tying those claims to the executed analysis—such as preserved output, a complete result artifact, or independently reproducible execution—rather than relying only on code, prose assertions, or unsupported numerical transcription.

title: Evidence-backed execution and result reporting
requirement: When the submission claims that correlations, clusters, sensitivity analyses, or generated outputs were computed, it must provide direct, inspectable evidence linking the executed analysis to the reported quantitative results; code alone, a prose assertion, or an unseen output is insufficient.

title: Execution-result consistency and inspectable computational support
requirement: When claiming computed correlations, clusters, counts, or other analytical results, the submission must provide directly inspectable execution evidence—such as retained output, assertions, or generated artifacts—that is consistent with the reported results; prose claims or merely planned code do not establish completion.

title: Consistency between reported results and executed evidence
requirement: Claimed numerical findings, cluster memberships, and other computed results must agree with the submitted executable computation and its publicly inspectable outputs; unsupported or contradictory prose claims should be penalized.

title: Public claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When reporting computed correlations, cluster memberships, counts, or sensitivity results, the submission must provide public, inspectable computational output or saved artifacts that support those specific claims and must not contradict them.

title: Execution-backed computation and result provenance
requirement: When claiming that a computation, validation check, generated artifact, or exact numerical result was completed, the submission must provide directly inspectable public evidence linking the claim to executed code and its output; unsupported prose, planned code, unseen files, or machine-specific paths do not establish completion.

title: Evidence support for claimed execution and computed outputs
requirement: When the submission claims that checks, computations, or generated artifacts were completed, the claim must be supported by directly inspectable public evidence linking the stated result to executable code or a preserved output; prose assertions alone are insufficient.

title: Traceability and internal consistency of derived results
requirement: When reporting computed cluster memberships, statistics, or other derived outputs, the submission must provide directly inspectable execution evidence that connects the stated results to the documented code and uses mutually consistent memberships, counts, and summaries.

title: Complete and justified score-variable scope
requirement: When the dataset contains multiple published and bespoke score representations, the analysis must include the relevant continuous score variables or explicitly justify each exclusion, so clustering is not driven by an arbitrary subset or mislabeled sensitivity analysis.

title: Primary-analysis scope fidelity
requirement: When the task specifies a primary feature set and method, the claimed primary results must be computed from that specified set and method, with broader or alternative analyses clearly labeled as sensitivity analyses rather than substituted for the primary analysis.

title: Inspectably supported computed outputs
requirement: When claiming computed correlation matrices, cluster memberships, or quantitative summaries, the submission must provide directly inspectable evidence linking the claimed outputs to executable analysis, rather than only prose assertions or code that does not expose the relevant results.

title: Primary-analysis scope and sensitivity separation
requirement: When the task specifies a primary variable subset alongside sensitivity analyses, the submission must explicitly define that subset, perform and report the requested primary analysis separately, and label broader or alternative analyses as sensitivity context rather than substituting them for the primary result.

title: Primary-estimand versus sensitivity-result consistency
requirement: When the task design distinguishes a required primary score subset from a broader sensitivity analysis, the submission must clearly identify the primary estimand and ensure that the final reported memberships, cluster counts, and quantitative summaries correspond to that subset rather than substituting or conflating sensitivity results.

title: Claim-to-computation reproducibility of reported clustering outputs
requirement: When reporting exact cluster memberships or numerical summaries as computed results, the submission must provide directly inspectable executable support or captured output that corresponds to those claims, rather than relying on an unshown run or prose assertion.

title: Primary-estimand scope control
requirement: When the task distinguishes a required primary variable subset from sensitivity variables, the reported conclusion must use the primary subset and clearly prevent sensitivity-only analyses from being presented as the answer.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: Claimed memberships, statistics, and conclusions must agree with the documented computation and its inspectable output; unsupported outcome or predictive claims must not be added to a descriptive correlation analysis.

title: Public execution-result evidence
requirement: Claims of completed computation must be supported by directly inspectable execution results or equivalent public output, rather than only code or prose assertions.

title: Primary-analysis scope and result consistency
requirement: When an analysis distinguishes a primary feature subset from sensitivity analyses, claimed primary results must correspond to the declared primary subset and its documented computation, rather than reporting sensitivity-feature memberships or statistics as the primary answer.

title: Evidence-backed computed-result claims
requirement: When claiming that a matrix, clustering output, summary statistic, or other computation was completed, the submission must provide directly inspectable execution evidence or captured output supporting that claim; executable code alone or an assertion that an output exists is insufficient.

title: Primary-analysis scope fidelity
requirement: When a task designates a primary feature subset and a sensitivity analysis, the answer must derive its requested conclusions from the primary subset and clearly segregate sensitivity-only results.

title: Patient-Level Denominator for Reported Proportions
requirement: When reporting proportions of patients, the claimed denominator must represent unique patients rather than repeated sample or accession rows, with the deduplication rule and its inspectable implementation or resulting counts documented.

title: Patient-Level Denominator for Patient Proportions
requirement: When claiming proportions of patients, aggregate repeated or multiple records so that each patient contributes to the reported denominator at most once, with the patient-level construction and handling of duplicates directly inspectable.

title: Patient-Level Denominator and Aggregation Consistency
requirement: When claiming proportions of patients, the reported denominator and subgroup counts must be patient-level and mutually exclusive, with an inspectable rule for resolving multiple qualifying records or an explicit qualification that results are record-level or overlapping memberships.

title: Non-Mutually-Exclusive Patient Sensitivity Qualification
requirement: When reporting unique-patient counts by subgroup across multiple records, the submission must distinguish overlapping patient-subgroup memberships from a mutually exclusive patient composition.

title: Unsupported Replacement of Supplied Subgroup Labels
requirement: When subgroup assignments are derived from score fields instead of using an available supplied subgroup classification, the submission must provide inspectable validation of that reconstruction against the supplied labels or a documented justification for why the supplied labels are unsuitable.

title: Numerical Reconciliation of Reported Results
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed, the final counts and percentages must reconcile with the artifact’s own inspectable calculations, intermediate counts, and stated denominator.

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Quantities
requirement: When reporting counts, denominators, and percentages, ensure each percentage is arithmetically consistent with its stated count and denominator.

title: Consistency of Duplicate-Patient Audit
requirement: When claiming a patient-level deduplication or reporting duplicate-related sensitivity results, the submission must accurately and consistently reconcile eligible row counts, unique-patient counts, duplicate-patient counts, and the stated effect of duplicate handling.

title: Consistency of Reported Intermediate Results
requirement: When the submission reports intermediate counts, duplicate handling, sensitivity results, or other computed diagnostics, those claims must agree with the submitted code and the resulting data; conclusions must not rely on materially misstated computation details.

title: Directly Reproducible Final Aggregation
requirement: When reporting computed subgroup counts or percentages, the submission must provide inspectable aggregation code applied to the analyzed cohort and directly inspectable output that reproduces the reported totals and percentages.

title: Honor the prescribed fixed-size gene-set definition
requirement: When the task specifies a fixed number of genes per set, use and report sets of that size with the required ranking direction, rather than replacing them with variable-sized significance-selected sets.

title: Align reported results with executed analysis
requirement: When claiming computed memberships, summary statistics, or per-gene values, ensure the reported results and interpretations agree with the publicly shown computation and its directly inspectable outputs.

title: Align quantitative claims with executable support

title: Retention of potentially concordant directions

title: Traceable dataset schema and modality extraction

title: Trace-to-result execution alignment

title: Evidence-backed computational claims

title: Consistency of Reported Computations with Executable Evidence
requirement: When the submission claims that analyses or numerical results were computed, the reported methods and results must be supported by the submitted executable code or other directly inspectable public output, without presenting unexecuted or contradictory computations as completed.

title: Self-contained reproducible implementation

title: Consistency of reported computational results

title: Execution support for reported computational results

title: Evidence-backed execution and result provenance
requirement: When claiming that an analysis, computation, generated result, or output file was completed, the submission must provide directly inspectable executable code and public output or equivalent evidence that supports the claimed result; prose assertions or merely described/unseen artifacts are insufficient.

title: Evidence-backed execution of claimed analyses
requirement: When claiming adjusted results, robustness analyses, sensitivity analyses, or generated outputs, the submission must provide directly inspectable executable code and public output evidence showing that those computations completed and support the reported claims.

title: Public validation of sample-to-metadata alignment
requirement: When analysis claims that expression samples were correctly aligned to clinical metadata, the submission must expose checks that validate accession-set equality and final sample ordering before cohort selection and testing.

title: Executable support for reported computations
requirement: When claiming that analyses, reruns, exports, or robustness checks were completed, the submission must provide directly inspectable executable support or generated public output for those claims.

title: Consistency between inferential claims and executed correction
requirement: When multiple comparisons or sensitivity analyses are claimed, the reported corrected values and conclusions must be generated from the same prespecified tests and consistently documented across code, trace, and answer.

title: Internal consistency of reported analyses
requirement: When the submission makes quantitative or inferential claims, the reported code, intermediate outputs, statistical results, and conclusions must agree with one another.

title: Consistency of reported results with supporting evidence
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or interpretations, the submission must keep the narrative, code, and publicly reported outputs mutually consistent; claimed values must be supported by the documented computation and distributions.

title: Validity of reported multiple-testing adjustments
requirement: When adjusted p-values are claimed, the submission must implement and report a mathematically valid adjustment consistent with the stated correction procedure, including any required monotonicity enforcement for Benjamini–Hochberg values.

title: Internal consistency of reported evidence and conclusions
requirement: When the submission makes quantitative claims, repeated values and the stated interpretation must agree with the reported statistics, distributions, and supporting computations.

title: Correct implementation of multiplicity adjustment
requirement: When multiple hypothesis tests are adjusted, the reported adjusted values must be computed using a valid multiplicity procedure, including any required monotonicity correction for Benjamini–Hochberg.

title: Consistency of claims with reported evidence
requirement: Claimed associations, subgroup differences, directions, and conclusions must be supported by the reported statistics, effect summaries, and documented computations; descriptive differences must not be presented as inferential findings when the relevant test is null or incompatible.

title: Evidence-supported adjusted inference
requirement: When claiming that multiple-testing correction was applied to inferential results, the submission must provide inspectable adjusted outputs for every tested endpoint, not only code or an unverified prose assertion.

title: Evidence-backed inferential results
requirement: When reporting statistical tests or multiplicity-adjusted results, the submission must provide direct, inspectable public evidence that those analyses were actually executed and that the reported values correspond to the stated computation; executable code or an unsupported prose claim alone is insufficient.

title: Concordance of reported computations with public execution evidence
requirement: When reporting completed analyses or numerical results, the submission must keep the described procedure, executable code, saved outputs, and claimed values mutually consistent, and must not present an executable branch or unsupported prose claim as evidence that the computation was completed.

title: Direct support for reported derived statistics
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, the response must provide directly inspectable evidence that the displayed computation actually produces each claimed statistic.

title: Use of explicit treatment-timing annotations
requirement: When the data provide treatment-timing annotations, cohort classification must use those annotations rather than treating a biological or sampling category alone as proof of treatment exposure.

title: Evidence support for claimed computations
requirement: When reporting a computed statistic or derived quantitative result, the submission must provide direct, inspectable support in its executable code or public output for that result.

title: Evidence-supported computed results
