title: Accuracy of data-field assertions
requirement: Claims about available fields, field values, or dataset structure must agree with the supplied data and must not be used to justify cohort definitions when contradicted by inspectable evidence.

title: Consistency of Reported Computations
requirement: For claimed computed results, the final answer must agree with the documented code, intermediate outputs, and quantitative evidence in the analysis trace.

title: Exposure-proxy qualification
requirement: When reporting treatment-group results, distinguish an observed hormonal-therapy exposure from an operational proxy based on sample annotations, and avoid presenting the proxy as direct evidence of post-hormonal treatment.

title: Explicit Post-Treatment Cohort Definition
requirement: When claiming a post-hormonal-therapy frequency, distinguish explicitly annotated post-treatment samples from treatment-naive samples and avoid treating metastasis alone as synonymous with post-treatment exposure when the clinical data provide a broader post-treatment annotation.

title: Functional mutation qualification
requirement: When claiming mutation-defined pathway alterations, distinguish qualifying nonsynonymous or otherwise functionally relevant variants from silent variants before forming the sample-level union.

title: Complete post-treatment cohort construction
requirement: When claiming a post-treatment HR+/HER2− frequency, include every eligible HR+/HER2− sample explicitly annotated as post-treatment, including post-treatment primary and metastatic samples, while excluding treatment-naive primary samples; state the operational limitation if hormone-agent exposure is unavailable.

title: Direct support for claimed computed outputs
requirement: When an artifact claims that a computation produced quantitative results, the submitted code or directly included execution output must visibly generate the claimed counts, percentages, tables, and statistics; prose assertions about unseen or unprinted outputs are insufficient.

title: Executable reproducibility of claimed analysis
requirement: When the response presents executable analysis code as support for reported results, the code must be runnable as written from the stated inputs, with valid parsing, defined variables, and coherent data-flow through the reported computation.

title: Code-to-claim output alignment
requirement: When the response claims that code produced intermediate counts, percentages, tables, or other computed outputs, the code must visibly calculate and emit those claimed quantities rather than merely imply them or report them elsewhere.

title: Auditability of analytical transformations
requirement: When results depend on cohort construction or multi-stage transformations, the response must expose enough intermediate selections and component results to inspect how the final reported quantities were formed.

title: Executable Support for Claimed Computations
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed to have been computed, the submitted code must be directly executable from the provided material, with defined variables, valid file parsing, and filters that match the reported analysis.

title: Direct Evidence for Claimed Intermediate Outputs
requirement: When the analysis claims that executable code reports intermediate stratum counts, denominators, percentages, or other audit quantities, the code or public execution evidence must directly produce those quantities.

title: Executable analysis supports claimed results
requirement: When claiming that results were computed or reproduced, the submitted code must be directly executable from the documented inputs: it uses fields present in those inputs, defines referenced variables, and implements the stated filters and calculations.

title: Claimed component counts reconcile with the computation
requirement: When reporting component-level counts or intermediate outputs, those claims must be directly supported by the computation and reconcile with the reported sample-level union, including overlaps and deduplication.

title: Executable Claim-to-Data Consistency
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed as computed, the submitted code must use the supplied data schema and defined variables consistently, be runnable from the shown material, and produce the reported outputs.

title: Executable Claim-to-Code Consistency
requirement: When reporting computed results, the artifact must provide executable analysis code whose fields, variables, filters, and transformations directly reproduce the stated outputs.

title: Treatment-exposure calibration
requirement: When the requested treatment exposure is not directly recorded, distinguish documented exposure from a disease-state or sampling proxy and restrict cohort claims and conclusions accordingly.

title: Alteration-definition sensitivity and scope
requirement: When claiming a relationship between genomic alteration classes, the analysis must state the operational alteration definitions and assess whether the conclusion changes under materially different supported definitions (such as mutation-only versus CNA-inclusive calls), without treating one definition as universally comprehensive.

title: Consistency between computation and reported results
requirement: When claiming computed counts or statistical results, the narrative results must agree with the submitted code and intermediate outputs, including the test direction and numerical values.

title: Calibrated exposure claims
requirement: When treatment exposure is not directly recorded, the analysis must distinguish a disease-state or sample-type proxy from confirmed hormonal-therapy exposure and limit conclusions accordingly.

title: Exposure-status provenance and claim scope
requirement: When the requested treatment-exposure status is not directly encoded in the supplied data, the analysis must distinguish an operational proxy from verified exposure and limit cohort-specific conclusions accordingly.

title: Exposure-status claims match available annotations
requirement: When treatment exposure is not directly recorded, conclusions must not present a disease-state or sample-type proxy as confirmed post-hormonal-therapy eligibility; the proxy and resulting scope must be explicitly identified.

title: Proxy sensitivity results are separated from the requested answer
requirement: When the requested cohort cannot be isolated, the response must label proxy or sensitivity analyses as supplementary and must not treat their statistical findings as determining the unavailable target cohort.

title: Exposure-status claim discipline
requirement: When the clinical data lack medication-specific hormonal-therapy exposure, claims about post-hormonal-therapy findings must distinguish the metastatic proxy cohort from a confirmed treated cohort.

title: Separation of verified cohort from proxy analysis
requirement: When the supplied metadata cannot verify a required exposure or cohort attribute, the analysis must distinguish that evidentiary limitation from the operational proxy and must not present proxy results as findings for the requested cohort.

title: Treatment-exposure ascertainment and calibration
requirement: When treatment exposure is not directly recorded, conclusions must distinguish a metastatic or other disease-state proxy from a confirmed post-hormonal-therapy cohort and must not generalize proxy statistics to the requested confirmed population.

title: Explicitly distinguish documented treatment exposure from disease-state proxies
requirement: When the requested cohort requires post-hormonal-therapy exposure, claims about that cohort must be conditional on inspectable exposure evidence; metastatic status or other disease-state labels must not be presented as proof of hormonal treatment, and any proxy analysis must be clearly separated from the requested conclusion.

title: Evidence-backed reporting of executed results
requirement: When reporting numerical results for a defined analysis, the artifact must distinguish code that specifies a computation from output directly supported by an execution record, and must not present unverified outputs as completed results.

title: Distinguishing treatment exposure from disease-state proxies
requirement: When cohort membership is inferred from a disease-state or sample-type proxy rather than an explicit treatment annotation, claims about post-treatment exposure must be qualified accordingly.

title: Evidence-backed quantitative claims
requirement: When reporting completed computations or numerical results, the submission must provide direct, inspectable evidence that the stated endpoint was actually executed and verified, rather than relying only on planned code or an unverified output.

title: Consistency of statistical results
requirement: The reported contingency counts, odds ratio, p-value, and test direction must be mutually consistent with the displayed table and the statistical code.

title: Claim–Computation Consistency
requirement: When quantitative results or statistical conclusions are claimed, the reported cohort, alteration definition, contingency counts, test direction, and p-value must agree with the displayed computation and each other.

title: Evidence of Completed Computation
requirement: Claims of executed computations, generated results, or reproducibility must be supported by direct, inspectable execution evidence rather than code or prose alone.

title: Execution-evidence alignment
requirement: When reporting computed counts, statistics, or generated results, the artifact must distinguish outputs directly supported by executed evidence from results that are only specified by code or remain unverified.

title: Directional statistical reproducibility
requirement: When a directional statistical claim is made, the displayed reproducible analysis must explicitly implement the claimed alternative and the reported result must correspond to that direction and contingency table.

title: Treatment-exposure qualification
requirement: When treatment exposure is inferred from sample type or other proxy annotations rather than directly recorded, claims about the post-treatment cohort and its results must preserve that uncertainty.

title: Public computation-result consistency
requirement: When reporting computed results, the artifact must make the displayed code, statistical-test settings, intermediate values, and final claims mutually consistent and directly inspectable.

title: Exposure-proxy qualification
requirement: When the supplied annotations do not establish prior hormonal-therapy exposure, conclusions must distinguish an exploratory cohort proxy from a verified post-hormonal-therapy cohort.

title: Claim–evidence consistency
requirement: When reporting computed results, the numerical claims and endpoint labels must agree with the displayed code and publicly inspectable execution evidence.

title: Treatment-exposure calibration
requirement: Claims about a post-treatment cohort must distinguish documented treatment exposure from an observational proxy when the supplied annotations do not establish prior hormonal therapy.

title: Evidence-consistent reported results
requirement: When reporting computed counts or statistics, the reported values must agree with the submitted code and publicly shown execution evidence.

title: Claim-calibrated treatment exposure
requirement: When making claims specifically about post-treatment tumors, the analysis must distinguish documented treatment exposure from a proxy based only on sample type or metastatic status.

title: Inference strength matches statistical evidence
requirement: When interpreting an association test, the conclusion must reflect whether the reported test provides statistical support for depletion or only a directional tendency.

title: Endpoint-definition consistency
requirement: The cohort, alteration definitions, and reported contingency table must refer to the same prespecified endpoint rather than silently switching between mutation-only, CNA-inclusive, or broadened gene-set analyses.

title: Execution evidence for claimed reproducibility
requirement: Claims that an analysis was executed or reproduced must be supported by direct, inspectable execution output rather than code alone or an unsupported prose assertion.

title: Execution-result consistency
requirement: When reporting computed results, the stated values and inferential conclusions must agree with the displayed code, intermediate outputs, and arithmetic checks.

title: Exposure-proxy calibration
requirement: When treatment exposure or timing is not directly observed, conclusions must distinguish the analyzed proxy cohort from the requested post-treatment population.

title: Statistical result consistency
requirement: When reporting a computed statistical result, the reported value and interpretation must agree with the displayed contingency table, test configuration, and any stated execution output.

title: Unsupported cohort-status inference
requirement: When treatment exposure is not directly observed, claims and quantitative conclusions must distinguish an explicitly labeled proxy cohort from a verified post-treatment cohort.

title: Cross-section numerical consistency
requirement: When the analysis reports computed quantities in multiple sections, the reported values and interpretations must remain consistent with the supporting code and intermediate results.

title: Internal consistency of reported computations
requirement: When the submission claims computed counts, statistics, or p-values, its code, intermediate results, trace conclusions, and final answer must report the same quantities and interpretations.

title: Exposure-status calibration
requirement: When treatment exposure is not directly recorded, the analysis must distinguish the observable cohort definition from any post-treatment or post-hormonal-therapy claim.

title: Claim-to-computation numerical consistency
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or quantitative results, the reported values must remain consistent with the submitted code and intermediate results.

title: Primary-versus-sensitivity alteration separation
requirement: When mutation-defined and CNA-inclusive alteration calls are both analyzed, the analysis must keep their definitions and inferential results distinct.

title: Internal Consistency of Quantitative Results
requirement: When reporting computed or transcribed numerical results, the stated values must agree with the supplied data and with the reported transformations and statistics.

title: Consistency between computation and reported claims
requirement: When reporting computed ranks, counts, or statistics, the narrative, code, tables, and intermediate results must agree with one another and with the supplied evidence.

title: Eligibility of candidates under the stated analysis definition
requirement: Claims identifying leading or therapeutically relevant downregulated candidates must distinguish genes that satisfy the stated direction, effect-size, testing, and significance criteria from genes that are merely exploratory observations.

title: Explicit numerical threshold filtering
requirement: When claiming a threshold-defined result, explicitly apply each required numerical threshold to the relevant columns rather than substituting a precomputed categorical significance flag or an alternative ranking subset.

title: Consistency between computation and reported claims
requirement: When reporting derived ranks, counts, or other computed results, keep the executable filtering/ranking logic, intermediate outputs, and final claims mutually consistent.

title: Separation of statistical significance from effect-size prioritization
requirement: When identifying genes as “most significantly” downregulated, the response must distinguish ranking by inferential evidence (such as p-values or multiple-testing-adjusted q-values) from ranking by fold-change magnitude or biological prominence, and must not present an effect-size or biological-priority ranking as a significance ranking.

title: Separation of statistical ranking from biological prioritization
requirement: When making biological-priority claims about downregulated genes, distinguish them from the statistical ranking and state the separate basis for prioritization; do not present a biologically selected subset as the statistically top-ranked result.

title: Alignment between reported method and executed analysis
requirement: When claiming a constructed region set, coverage analysis, or aggregate result, the submission must accurately describe and provide inspectable evidence for the operations actually performed; interval-overlap proxies must not be presented as merged consensus regions or read-based accessibility measurements.

title: Honest characterization of unavailable measurements
requirement: When alignment files or count matrices are unavailable, distinguish peak-call presence/overlap summaries from consensus-region read coverage, normalization, and accessibility effect estimates, with the distinction supported by the submitted method and file-availability checks.

title: Evidence of completed computation
requirement: When claiming that a quantitative workflow, computation, or result was performed, distinguish executed analyses from templates or planned follow-up code and provide direct inspectable evidence for the claimed execution; do not present unexecuted coverage, normalization, or consensus calculations as completed results.

title: Fidelity of computational claim scope and execution status
requirement: When interpreting interval calls or describing an analysis workflow, distinguish executed, inspectably supported results from proposed or blocked analyses, and do not present peak counts or peak-presence overlaps as read-level accessibility, CPM-normalized coverage, or formal differential-accessibility results without direct coverage evidence.

title: Distinguish peak-call evidence from read-level accessibility
requirement: When alignment-derived coverage, CPM, or log2 fold-change is unavailable, characterize interval counts and overlaps only as peak-call landscape or presence proxies, and do not present them as formal accessibility measurements or directional accessibility results.

title: Separate executed results from proposed workflows
requirement: Claims of completed computation must be supported by inspectable execution evidence; code for unavailable inputs or future analysis must be explicitly identified as a template or follow-up and must not supply claimed results.

title: Calibration of accessibility claims to available evidence
requirement: When read-level coverage or normalized counts are unavailable, distinguish peak-call changes or overlap proxies from measured accessibility and avoid asserting that they establish global chromatin closing.

title: Evidence-backed execution-status claims
requirement: Claims that a computation or workflow was executed must be supported by directly inspectable outputs or execution evidence; proposed or blocked code must be labeled as such.

title: Calibration of claims to executed evidence
requirement: When required inputs or computations are unavailable, distinguish executed proxy analyses from planned or unexecuted workflows and limit conclusions to what the submitted evidence directly supports.

title: Calibration of peak-call evidence versus accessibility
requirement: When BAMs, bigWigs, or an equivalent count matrix are unavailable, distinguish peak-call counts or overlap/presence proxies from read-level accessibility and limit conclusions accordingly.

title: Evidence for claimed execution and results
requirement: When claiming that a computation was performed or that a derived result was produced, provide direct inspectable support distinguishing executed outputs from code templates, blocked workflows, or planned follow-up analyses.

title: Evidence of completed computations
requirement: When claiming computed results or completed analytical steps, provide directly inspectable evidence that the computation was actually executed; planned code, stated intentions, or unavailable inputs do not substantiate completion.

title: Replicate-aware support for landscape claims
requirement: When claiming a treatment-associated change in a called peak landscape, assess within-condition replicate concordance so that differences in peak burden are not presented without evidence of reproducibility.

title: Evidence for input availability and execution status
requirement: When claims depend on the presence or absence of input files, or on completed file-based analyses, provide direct, inspectable evidence of file discovery and analysis execution rather than relying only on prose assertions or planned code.

title: Calibration of claims to executed evidence
requirement: When required read-level inputs or computations are unavailable, distinguish descriptive peak-call observations from normalized accessibility results and avoid presenting planned, blocked, or proxy analyses as completed evidence for definitive locus-level or global accessibility changes.

title: Evidence for blocked-input and execution-status claims
requirement: When claiming that required files, analyses, or outputs are unavailable or unexecuted, provide directly inspectable evidence supporting that status rather than relying only on prose assertions.

title: Consistency of reported quantitative results with supporting analysis
requirement: When the submission claims computed quantitative results, the reported values must be consistent across the answer, trace, displayed computation, and any cited output.

title: Consistency Between Reported Results and Shown Computation
requirement: When claiming that a reported result, transformation, ordering, or comparison was performed, the submitted code and displayed evidence must actually implement and support that claim.

title: Evidence that claimed derived ordering is actually applied
requirement: When outputs are claimed to use a data-derived amino-acid ordering, the submitted code or displayed results must directly demonstrate that the derived order is applied to the reported vectors, rather than merely defining the order or asserting its use.

title: Consistency of Reported Quantitative Results
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed, the answer, trace, and any displayed supporting calculations or tables must report the same values and interpretations; conflicting values for a central metric undermine the result.

title: Inspectable Support for Claimed Derived Outputs
requirement: When claiming that a computation produced derived outputs such as ranked fold changes, replication metrics, or complete result tables, the submission must include directly inspectable output or a displayed calculation that deterministically produces those outputs, rather than relying only on an assertion that an unseen script prints them.

title: Inspectable support for claimed computed results
requirement: When claiming that numerical analyses were completed, the submission must provide directly inspectable evidence linking those results to a runnable computation: executable code must be internally runnable from the submitted material, and claimed outputs must be shown or otherwise directly reproducible without relying on an unseen script or merely asserting that a script emits them.

title: Consistency between claimed comparisons and supporting computation
requirement: When reporting a comparison, statistical result, or interpretation, the artifact must use and identify the same groups, labels, and operands in its displayed code or other directly inspectable computation as those named in the claim.

title: Direct evidence for claimed completed computations
requirement: When claiming that an analysis, result, or reproducibility workflow was completed, the submission must provide directly inspectable outputs or self-contained executable evidence whose required inputs and intermediate objects are defined; planned code with undefined dependencies or no corresponding result output does not establish completion.

title: Consistency between reported metrics and comparative conclusions
requirement: When the artifact ranks methods or interprets quantitative results, each stated winner, ordering, or comparative conclusion must follow directly from the reported metric values and their defined direction; conflicting narrative conclusions must be explicitly qualified or corrected.

title: Execution-to-claim consistency
requirement: When the submission claims that reported metrics were computed using a particular label, background, filtering rule, or aggregation, the displayed executable analysis must implement that rule and support the reported counts and results.

title: Reported-results computation consistency

title: Coverage of available task-relevant evaluations

title: Output–Computation Provenance

title: Trace-to-result reproducibility consistency
requirement: When claiming computed results or summaries, the submitted analysis must show code and inspectable outputs whose filters, scope, and aggregation actually support those claims.

title: Validated integration of auxiliary predictor scores

title: Auditable eligibility and exclusion accounting

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting evidence
requirement: When claiming computed numerical results or conclusions, the submitted tables, code outputs, summaries, and conclusions must agree with one another; reported values must be traceable to the displayed computation or result artifact.

title: Alignment with the stated inferential scope
requirement: When assessing a claim under an explicitly specified hypothesis scope and significance criterion, the response must preserve that scope and criterion rather than silently replacing them with a broader testing family or a different multiplicity threshold.

title: Executable support for reported computations
requirement: When claiming completed quantitative analysis, the submitted executable code must implement the same data definitions and operations used to produce the reported results, so the reported outputs are directly reproducible from the shown computation.

title: Consistency between executable analysis and reported results
requirement: When claiming completed computational results, the submitted executable code must implement the same data selection and transformations described in the report and support the reported quantities.

title: Execution of the claimed query operation
requirement: When a completed computational result is claimed, the displayed executable code must perform the reported query operation itself, rather than substitute a different operation whose output happens to coincide on the supplied data.

title: Executable verification of reported results
requirement: When claiming completed computational results, the submitted executable material must directly verify the key reported quantities and decision—such as by asserting or programmatically extracting the target overlap, statistical values, and significance conclusion—rather than merely displaying code that could produce them.

title: Direct diagnostic support for target-specific results
requirement: When claiming target-specific computed quantities, the submitted executable material must directly select or validate the target and expose its relevant counts, statistics, and ranking so those claims are inspectable without inferring them from an unshown result object.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with the Displayed Computation
requirement: When claiming completed computations or quantitative results, the reported values and conclusions must be supported by the displayed code and its stated intermediate quantities, including the applicable universe, denominators, and filtering steps.

title: Evidence support for ancillary analysis claims

title: Alignment of the inferential scope with the stated question

title: Internal consistency of statistical results
requirement: When reporting a statistical test, the stated counts, test definition, and numerical result must agree with one another and be reproducible from the submitted analysis.

title: Evidence for claimed computed outputs
requirement: When claiming that an analysis produced generated results or a complete output, the submission must provide direct, inspectable evidence of that computation or output rather than relying solely on code, prose assertions, or an unseen result object.

title: Executable support for claimed feature coverage and results
requirement: When claiming that an analysis tested a complete feature set or produced reported numerical results, the submitted material must contain executable, inspectable computation whose actual scope and outputs support those claims; prose assertions or code that silently omits features do not suffice.

title: Claimed analysis coverage is supported by the submitted computation
requirement: When claiming results for every feature or a complete feature screen, the submitted code and inspectable outputs must demonstrably iterate over and report the claimed feature set, without truncation, hard-coded subsets, or reliance on an unseen result file.

title: Reported model specification matches the executed computation

title: Inspectable evidence supports claimed computed outputs
requirement: When claiming completed model results or a complete feature-level output, the submission must provide directly inspectable computation and resulting evidence sufficient to verify those claims; references to unseen files or omitted implementation are insufficient.

title: Alignment of reported effect scale with the requested estimand
requirement: When reporting Cox HRs and p-values for the requested abundance-based association, the artifact must state the covariate scale and ensure that the displayed computation and significance decision use that same scale.

title: Consistency of Reported Rankings

title: Inspectable Evidence for Reported Computation
requirement: When claiming completed cohort construction or statistical results, provide sufficient submitted code and quantitative intermediate outputs to independently inspect the computation; do not rely on an unseen script, prose assertion, or incomplete placeholder for a nontrivial calculation.

title: Correct Survival-Model Implementation
requirement: The Cox analysis must implement the survival risk sets and tied-event handling correctly and use a statistically valid, inspectable calculation of coefficients, uncertainty, and p-values; a nominal Cox label alone is insufficient.

title: Inspectably Reproducible Computation

title: Inspectable implementation of claimed Cox computations
requirement: When claiming computed per-feature Cox estimates, the submission must provide directly inspectable, reproducible code for the likelihood/risk-set calculation, coefficient uncertainty, and p-value—not merely a call to an unseen helper or external file.

title: Validity of reported significance calculations
requirement: When reporting Cox significance results, the submission must use a valid p-value calculation consistent with the reported test statistic and must produce probabilities in the valid [0,1] range.

title: Inspectability of claimed generated result outputs
requirement: When claiming results from a completed feature-wide computation or generated result file, the submission must include the relevant quantitative output or otherwise provide direct, reviewable evidence supporting those claims.

title: Claimed feature coverage matches the submitted computation
requirement: When claiming results for a target feature or a complete feature-wise analysis, the submitted code and data flow must demonstrably include that feature and scope rather than exclude it or use a contradictory feature list.

title: Submitted evidence supports claimed generated results
requirement: When reporting computed estimates, rankings, or complete result sets, the submission must provide direct inspectable evidence in the submitted material—such as displayed output, an included result table, or code that visibly produces the specific claim—rather than relying solely on prose or an unseen/unsubmitted file.

title: Consistency between claimed and implemented statistical test
requirement: When claiming a paired longitudinal analysis, the submitted computational evidence must visibly implement a paired test on matched subject-level changes, and the reported inferential results must correspond to that implementation rather than merely asserting that a paired test was used.

title: Reproducible regimen-interaction computation
requirement: When claiming that changes differ or do not differ between CPA and SPIRO, the submitted material must display executable computation that constructs matched subject-level changes for both regimens, performs the stated between-regimen test for each protein, applies the stated multiplicity correction, and supports the reported interaction results.

title: Direct regimen-by-time comparison
requirement: When claiming that protein changes differ between regimens, directly test the participant-level change difference between CPA and SPIRO, apply multiplicity correction across proteins, and report interpretable effect estimates and adjusted significance results; do not infer interaction from separate within-regimen significance or set overlap alone.

title: Consistency of reported effect direction
requirement: For claimed quantitative changes, the reported direction must agree with the stated change definition and the displayed computation or test statistic.

title: Computational result support
requirement: When claiming completed quantitative results, provide executable analysis code whose variables, inputs, filtering, test outputs, and reported values visibly support those claims; do not rely on unavailable generated files or unsupported assertions.

title: Effect-direction consistency
requirement: Ensure reported effect directions agree with the defined change calculation and the corresponding statistical sign, so that increases and decreases are not reversed in substantive conclusions.

title: Formal regimen-interaction distinction

title: Auditable evidence for claimed computed results

title: Internal consistency of effect direction claims

title: Internal consistency of derived quantitative summaries

title: Accurate endpoint-specific direction summaries

title: Consistency of reported direction counts

title: Identifiable reporting of claimed discovery sets

title: Internal Consistency of Quantitative Claims

title: Inspectable support for reported result sets
requirement: When claiming that a computation produced a complete or ranked result set, provide directly inspectable supporting output or an included result table that permits the claim to be checked; code and an assertion that an unseen or unshown output contains the results are insufficient.

title: Evidence for Completeness Claims

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results

title: Consistency of reported results with supporting computation
requirement: When claiming computed counts, rankings, or quantitative results, the submitted code, intermediate outputs, and final statements must agree with one another; prose must not report results that the shown computation would not produce.

title: Fidelity of reported association directions

title: Support for claimed computations and results

title: Internal consistency of reported quantities

title: Evidence support for reported computations

title: Evidence-supported computed results

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed counts, intersections, percentages, or examples, the submitted analysis must use definitions and code whose outputs agree with the stated results, including cross-regimen intersections and denominator choices.

title: Separation of overlap counts from directional-analysis counts
requirement: When directional concordance is claimed, the analysis must distinguish the full protein-overlap count from the subset with observable sex-effect directions and report the applicable denominator.

title: Task-aligned definition of the sex-associated reference set
requirement: When claiming overlap with general-population sex-associated proteins, the analysis must define a reproducible reference set whose selection rule is justified by the question and supplied data, rather than imposing an unsupported fixed-size or otherwise arbitrary subset that changes the estimand.

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Computations
requirement: When claiming computed statistics or results, the reported values must agree with the displayed calculation, inputs, and intermediate outputs; material numerical discrepancies must be penalized.

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Computations

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results

title: Consistency between reported conclusions and supporting computation
requirement: Claimed quantitative findings must be directly supported by the displayed code and intermediate results, with matching numerators, denominators, and percentages.

title: Explicit reconciliation of comparator estimands

title: Internal consistency of quantitative reporting

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Supporting Computation
requirement: When reporting computed counts, percentages, or derived results, the final claims must agree with the displayed code outputs and intermediate results; unsupported numerical deviations must not be presented as completed findings.

title: Consistency of reported results with displayed analysis

title: Preservation of comparator-stratum heterogeneity

title: Internal consistency of reported computations
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed, the displayed code, stated analysis definition, intermediate results, and final reported values must implement and describe the same computation without material mismatches.

title: Consistency of implemented filters and reported results
requirement: When reporting computed overlap or concordance results, the displayed executable analysis must implement the stated comparator and filtering rules, and the reported counts must agree with the resulting sets and denominators.

title: Internal consistency of reported results

title: Internal consistency of reported cluster memberships
requirement: When the submission reports cluster memberships in multiple sections or files, each score must have a consistent, publicly verifiable membership; overlapping or contradictory assignments must be explicitly resolved rather than left as competing results.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When an analysis reports computed cluster memberships, partitions, or quantitative results, the final claims must agree with the displayed code output and intermediate results; any semantic aggregation or alternative summary must be explicitly distinguished from the algorithm’s actual output.

title: Direct auditability of claimed computed results
requirement: Claims of completed correlations, clustering, or other quantitative analysis must be supported by inspectable code and corresponding quantitative output sufficient to verify the claimed result, rather than by prose assertions alone.

title: Quantitative result-to-evidence consistency
requirement: When the submission claims computed numerical results, the reported values must agree with the displayed computation and intermediate evidence, with discrepancies reconciled or explicitly qualified.

title: Evidence for claimed sensitivity or stability
requirement: When claiming that clustering results, memberships, rankings, or conclusions are stable across thresholds or analytical variants, the submission must provide direct, inspectable comparison evidence supporting that claim rather than only reporting aggregate counts or describing an intended comparison.

title: Trace-supported quantitative reporting
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or results, each material numerical claim must be directly supported by the displayed computation or an inspectable output, with no contradiction between the reported value and the trace.

title: Verified sensitivity-membership claims

title: Direct support for reported quantitative results

title: Object-level validation of stability claims

title: Patient-Level Denominator for Patient Proportions

title: Derived Classification Drives Reported Aggregation
requirement: When subgroup proportions are claimed to be derived from score-based classification, the reported counts and percentages must be computed from the explicitly derived subgroup assignments rather than from a pre-existing label column or another unverified proxy.

title: Linkage of Reported Counts to the Stated Classification
requirement: When subgroup proportions are claimed to be derived from score-based rules, the reported counts must be generated from the inspectable computed classification rather than only from a supplied subgroup label; any supplied label may serve only as a separately validated cross-check.

title: Traceability of Score-Derived Results
requirement: When claiming that subgroup proportions are derived from the specified score cutoff, the reported counts and percentages must be directly traceable to an executed transformation of the relevant scores using that rule, rather than to pre-existing subgroup labels or an unused code path.

title: Claim-to-Computation Consistency
requirement: When subgroup results are claimed to be derived from an operational score rule, the reported counts and percentages must be generated by, or directly traceable to, code applying that same rule; supplied labels or a different transformation must not silently replace the claimed computation.

title: Claim-to-Computation Consistency
requirement: When reporting computed subgroup results, the submitted material must directly demonstrate that the displayed aggregation uses the claimed classification and inputs, rather than a different pre-existing label or an otherwise unsupported calculation.

title: Consistency of Patient-Level Duplicate Resolution
requirement: When a submission claims to report patient-level results and specifies a rule for resolving multiple eligible records per patient, the shown computation must implement that rule so the reported counts are reproducible from the submitted material.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Supporting Computation
requirement: When a submission reports quantitative results and provides supporting calculations or tables, the reported values must agree with those inspectable computations.

title: Ensure reported computations are supported by displayed code
requirement: When claiming completed calculations or quantitative results, the submitted code and inspectable outputs must implement the stated calculation and support the reported counts and summaries, without contradictions such as including self-correlations while reporting diagonal-excluded values.

title: Test coherence robustness to analytical choices
requirement: When claiming that within-set correlations demonstrate a coherent module, assess whether that conclusion is stable under at least one substantively different correlation or shared-variation summary, rather than relying on a single correlation estimator and its central tendency.

title: Consistency between executable computation and reported results
requirement: When reporting computed pair counts or summary statistics, ensure the submitted code demonstrably produces those quantities, including correct exclusion of self-correlations and matching indexing, dimensions, and aggregation rules.

title: Consistency between claimed and implemented correlation method
requirement: When reporting a method-specific correlation result, ensure the executable calculation shown in the submission uses that same method and supports the reported result; do not present results as Spearman (or another method) when the inspectable code computes Pearson instead.

title: Reconcile input-schema discrepancies before defining gene sets
requirement: When the supplied feature table’s dimensions, labels, or metadata conflict with the task’s stated gene-set definition, explicitly identify the discrepancy and justify which columns are eligible for analysis before selecting genes.

title: Execution–claim consistency
requirement: When claiming completed computational results, the submitted code and displayed outputs must directly support the stated method and reported values.

title: Consistency between claimed and implemented computation
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, ensure the submitted executable code actually implements the stated method and supports the reported results, rather than using a materially different method or unsupported output.

title: Quantitative result provenance and internal consistency
requirement: For claimed differential-expression counts, rankings, or significance values, the stated testing universe and exported results must be consistent with the displayed filtering, modeling, and multiple-testing code.

title: Effect-size ranking fidelity
requirement: When claiming that genes are the strongest increases or decreases by effect size, the named ordering must agree with the reported effect sizes.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When claiming completed computations or quantitative results, the stated analysis universe, filtering, exported results, and reported counts must be mutually consistent and directly supported by the submitted code or outputs.

title: Consistency between reported rankings and supporting results
requirement: When claiming that genes or other entities are ranked by effect size or statistical significance, the reported ordering and labels must be consistent with the quantitative results and ranking code shown.

title: Consistency Between Reported Results and Supporting Analysis
requirement: When making quantitative, ranking, or computation-completion claims, the response must keep those claims consistent with its displayed code, intermediate results, tables, and other inspectable evidence.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Supporting Analysis
requirement: When claiming computed quantitative results or rankings, the submission must make those claims consistent with the displayed code, intermediate outputs, and reported totals.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims
requirement: Claimed counts, rankings, directions, and statistics must agree with one another and with the displayed computation or result evidence.

title: Evidence support for completed computation
requirement: Claims of completed analysis and generated results must be supported by directly inspectable computation outputs or reproducible code whose output supports the claim, rather than by prose assertions alone.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims
requirement: When claiming computed results, the artifact must provide directly inspectable support whose reported values are consistent across the analysis code, intermediate outputs, tables, and final answer.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Supporting Outputs
requirement: When numerical or statistical results are claimed as computed, the reported values must agree with the displayed code outputs, tables, and other submitted supporting evidence.

title: Consistency of reported results with supporting analysis
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or gene-level rankings, the claimed values and entity-statistic assignments must agree with the displayed analysis results and supporting outputs.

title: Traceability of reported statistics to the stated analysis
requirement: When reporting a module identity, membership, or statistic as belonging to a particular analysis, cohort, or network, directly demonstrate that it was computed from that analysis; results from a different or secondary analysis must remain explicitly distinguished rather than being reassigned.

title: Multiplicity control for module-association claims
requirement: When claiming statistical significance across multiple tested modules, apply and report an appropriate multiple-testing correction for the module-association tests; nominal p-values alone do not support claims of significant modules.

title: Alignment of reported results with the claimed analysis
requirement: When presenting results for a primary or revised analysis, ensure that the reported module statistics, memberships, and interpretations were generated from that same analysis population, preprocessing, network definition, and testing procedure; results from a different sensitivity or legacy analysis cannot substantiate the primary claim.

title: Consistency between reported modules and executed inclusion rules
requirement: When reporting module-specific results, ensure every reported module, membership, eigengene, and enrichment statistic satisfies the module-selection and exclusion rules shown in the analysis code; do not report excluded clusters as valid modules without a documented, reproducible later step that redefines eligibility.

title: Provenance of reported statistics to the claimed analysis
requirement: When attributing a statistic, module identity, or biological result to a definitive analysis, ensure the displayed computation and evidence derive it from the stated cohort, preprocessing, and network; results from a prior, sensitivity, or differently defined analysis must remain clearly separated rather than relabeled as definitive outputs.

title: Internal consistency of enrichment claims and evidence
requirement: When claiming cell-type enrichment or other marker-based biological interpretation, ensure the reported label, overlap, statistics, and supporting gene/module evidence agree with one another and with the stated analysis output.

title: Quantitative disease-association evidence for dysregulation claims
requirement: When claiming that modules are dysregulated or ALS-associated, directly compare the relevant module summary between ALS and an appropriate comparison group and report an inspectable association statistic; module construction or within-ALS enrichment alone does not establish dysregulation.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting outputs
requirement: When reporting computed quantities or biological labels, keep the narrative claims consistent with the directly shown calculations, tables, and result values; an uncorrected mismatch undermines the claimed result.

title: Consistency between claims and supporting outputs
requirement: When reporting computed results, ensure that numerical values, module labels, cell-type annotations, and significance claims agree with the directly shown tables, code-derived summaries, and other submitted evidence; do not make a substantive claim contradicted by the supporting output.

title: Internal consistency of reported computations and results
requirement: When claiming computed results or statistical procedures, ensure the reported values, labels, interpretations, and method descriptions agree with the directly shown code and output tables; contradictions undermine support for the claim.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When quantitative results or statistical conclusions are claimed, the displayed code, tables, and reported values must use the same test direction, module identity, counts, and statistics; contradictions between these elements undermine support for the claim.

title: Consistency of cell-type interpretation with enrichment evidence
requirement: When assigning a cell-type interpretation to a module, the narrative label must correspond to the marker set, overlap, and enrichment statistics actually reported for that module.

title: Internal consistency of reported analysis evidence
requirement: When reporting computed results or statistical tests, ensure that narrative claims, displayed tables, and reproducibility code agree on the same entity, value, test direction, and significance interpretation.

title: Consistency between claimed results and supporting analysis
requirement: When reporting computed results or statistical interpretations, the narrative, displayed tables, and executable code must use the same entities, counts, test direction, and reported statistics; contradictory labels, values, or implementation details undermine the claim.

title: Consistency between claimed execution and reported results
requirement: When claiming that reported results were produced by a specified revised or completed analysis, distinguish planned code from executed computation and ensure the reported results are directly attributable to that workflow; do not present results from an earlier or different workflow as outputs of an incomplete or unverified run.

title: Consistency between claimed results and the completed analysis
requirement: When reporting results as produced by a particular analysis pipeline, link the reported statistics and outputs to that completed pipeline and distinguish them from results produced by earlier, different, or incomplete runs.

title: Evidence of completed computation supporting claimed results

title: Consistency between reported findings and inspectable outputs

title: Executable support for claimed computations

title: Direct Evidence for Reported Computation

title: Executable support for claimed model results
requirement: When claiming completed model-based results, the submitted code must visibly include the claimed predictor and connect it to the reported coefficient, testing, and output; prose claims or code that cannot execute as shown are insufficient evidence.

title: Consistency between computed and reported numerical results
requirement: Reported quantitative findings must agree with the directly displayed computation or output that purportedly supports them.

title: Effect-measure distinction and evidentiary support

title: Entity identity consistency

title: Execution-status integrity and reproducibility

title: Evidence for completed computational claims

title: Consistency of reported quantitative results

title: Execution-status fidelity

title: Evidence support for claimed computations

title: Evidence support for claimed computations

title: Claimed computation is supported by inspectable evidence

title: Evidence-to-claim traceability

title: Alignment of reported results with the analyzed estimand

title: Evidence of completed computation

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims

title: Evidence of completed computation
requirement: When claiming that a statistical analysis or model was executed, the submission must provide direct, inspectable output supporting that claim, rather than only planned code, prose assertions, or placeholders.

requirement: When claiming computed statistics, scores, or ranked results, the submitted analysis must provide internally consistent, inspectable support linking the displayed code or documented transformation to the reported values and conclusions.

title: Alignment Between Reported Results and Reproducible Computation

title: Internal consistency of reported statistical results

title: Alignment of quantitative claims with supporting analysis

title: Evidence-supported post-treatment cohort claim

title: Direct evidence for reported quantitative results
requirement: When claiming completed computations, the submission must provide directly inspectable execution output or equivalent evidence linking the displayed code to the reported quantitative results.

title: Separate statistical ranking from biological prioritization

title: Executable analysis must support reported ranking and results
requirement: When a response claims that computed results are ranked or filtered in a particular way, its displayed executable code must implement that same operation and therefore provide direct support for the reported output.

title: Displayed computation must directly implement the claimed ranking rule

title: Separate statistical significance ranking from biological prioritization

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Quantitative Results
requirement: When quantitative findings are reported in multiple places, the values must remain consistent with the displayed computation and with each other, so transcription or copying errors do not alter the claimed result.

title: Separation of statistical ranking from biological prioritization
requirement: When claiming that genes are the most significant or most downregulated, the response must explicitly distinguish the ranking metric (such as q-value, p-value, or effect size) from any separate biological-prioritization rationale, and must not present a biologically prominent or highly expressed gene as statistically top-ranked without supporting ranking evidence.

title: Executable-analysis consistency
requirement: When the response claims that quantitative results were computed by displayed code, the code’s filters, ranking operations, and reported outputs must be mutually consistent and capable of reproducing those claims.

title: Consistency Between Computation and Reported Results
requirement: When a response claims that results were computed by displayed code, the code and its documented outputs must use the same filters, ranking rule, and transformations; material discrepancies must not undermine reproducibility of the reported findings.

title: Evidence for claimed completed computation
requirement: When claiming that a quantitative analysis was executed, provide direct inspectable evidence linking the reported result to executed computation and available inputs; planned code, prose assertions, or unavailable files do not establish completion.

title: Calibration of accessibility claims to observed measurements
requirement: When alignment-level coverage or normalized counts are unavailable, distinguish peak-call presence/absence summaries from quantitative accessibility measurements and do not present planned, unavailable, or unnormalized analyses as completed evidence of directional accessibility changes.

title: Calibration of peak-landscape evidence
requirement: When only peak-call intervals are available, distinguish descriptive changes in called peaks or interval presence from normalized accessibility changes and causal chromatin closing, explicitly qualifying claims that require read-level coverage or depth normalization.

title: Evidence support for claimed completed computations
requirement: For any claimed computed result, provide direct, inspectable evidence that the required inputs and computation were actually available and performed; do not treat planned code, prose assertions, or unavailable files as proof of execution.

title: Evidence-bounded reporting of unavailable quantitative analyses
requirement: When required input files or intermediate outputs are unavailable, distinguish completed computations from proposed workflow and do not report normalized coverage, fold changes, or directional region counts as computed from peak calls, planned code, or missing files.

title: Evidence-bounded biological interpretation
requirement: When making mechanistic or downstream biological claims from accessibility data, distinguish descriptive association from demonstrated mechanism and avoid attributing transcriptional or regulatory consequences that were not directly measured.

title: Accounting for sequencing-depth confounding in peak-burden interpretation
requirement: When interpreting between-condition differences in peak counts or called interval burden, explicitly account for library-size or sequencing-depth differences, or limit the claim so that peak-call burden is not presented as normalized accessibility change.

title: Validity of accessibility-direction claims
requirement: When claiming regions increased or decreased in accessibility, distinguish interval-presence or peak-membership differences from read-coverage-based accessibility measurements and do not present the former as normalized directional results.

title: Evidence support for claimed completed analyses
requirement: When claiming that a computation, normalization, statistical analysis, or derived result was completed, provide direct inspectable supporting output or code-result evidence; do not claim results that the submitted material states are uncomputable or supports only with absent/unseen files.

title: Distinguish peak presence from accessibility direction
requirement: When directional region-level accessibility changes are claimed, derive them from inspectable read-coverage measurements with appropriate normalization; do not label condition-specific peak presence or union membership as increased or decreased accessibility. If coverage is unavailable, explicitly restrict the claim to called-peak landscape differences.

title: Multiplicity control for multi-feature significance claims
requirement: When making inferential significance claims across multiple amino-acid composition tests, control and report multiplicity-adjusted significance using a documented procedure; descriptive comparisons without significance claims are not penalized.

title: Executable reproducibility of reported computations
requirement: When claiming that supplied code reproduces results, all referenced inputs and derived columns must be defined or created before use, so the workflow can execute through its claimed analyses without an unresolved runtime dependency.

title: Consistency of quantitative claims with supporting computation
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed, the reported values must agree with the displayed executable computation and its stated inputs or outputs.

title: Evidence-supported quantitative reporting
requirement: Claimed numerical results must be consistent with the displayed computations and supplied data, with material discrepancies between reported values and their supporting calculation treated as unsupported claims.

title: Inspectable evidence for claimed execution
requirement: When the submission claims that a computation or analysis was completed, it must provide direct, inspectable evidence of that completed run—such as captured result output, validated diagnostic output, or an independently checkable generated artifact—rather than relying only on planned code or prose assertions.

title: Direct evidence for completed computational execution
requirement: When claiming that a computation, parsing pass, or diagnostic run completed, the submission must provide inspectable output or another direct execution artifact supporting that completion; code and prose descriptions alone are insufficient, and reported results must not be presented as completed when the trace states execution did not finish.

title: Direct evidence for completed analyses and results
requirement: Claims that a computation, parsing pass, generated result, or diagnostic analysis was completed must be supported by direct, inspectable output in the submission; otherwise the analysis must be explicitly identified as incomplete or unavailable, and unsupported derived values must not be presented as results.

title: Consistency Between Computation and Reported Results
requirement: When numerical results are claimed as computed, the submitted code or other public execution evidence must implement the same definition and direction used by the reported values and interpretation, so the results are independently reproducible from the submission.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When claiming computed numerical results, the reported values must agree with the displayed computation, tables, and repeated summaries; material contradictions must be treated as unsupported results.

title: Alignment Between Computation and Reported Quantitative Results
requirement: When reporting computed quantities, the artifact must provide displayed code or direct computational evidence whose formula, direction, inputs, and outputs support the reported values and interpretations.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed numerical results, the answer must agree with the supporting code, tables, and intermediate results shown in the submission.

title: Inference for composition differences
requirement: When claiming that amino-acid composition differences between PS-Self and PS-Part groups are statistically meaningful rather than merely descriptive, the submission must provide a suitable group-comparison test, report its results, and account for multiplicity when testing multiple amino acids.

title: Inspectable support for claimed generated outputs
requirement: When claiming that derived output files, curves, tables, or other computational artifacts were generated, the submission must provide directly inspectable code or included output that produces or verifies the claimed artifact; a prose assertion about an unseen file is insufficient.

title: Evidence for claimed generated outputs
requirement: When claiming that derived output files or artifacts were generated, the submission must provide directly inspectable generation code or equivalent evidence linking the reported artifact to the analysis.

title: Direct evidence for generated analysis outputs
requirement: When claiming that computations produced output files, curves, tables, or other generated results, the submission must provide directly inspectable output evidence or code whose displayed execution result substantiates those claims.

title: Independent validation of label-column alignment
requirement: When group definitions and counts depend on workbook columns, the submission must independently verify that each named label column maps to the intended classification and that the resulting group construction is semantically aligned, rather than relying only on positional renaming or unvalidated assumptions.

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Quantitative Results
requirement: When reporting computed values or derived summaries, ensure that tables, narrative claims, aggregate statistics, and displayed computation agree with one another; do not leave contradictory transcription or arithmetic errors in claimed results.

title: Reconcile reported results with computations
requirement: When claiming completed quantitative analyses, ensure reported values and derived summaries are mutually consistent with the displayed computation, intermediate tables, and aggregation formulas.

title: Claim-to-evidence consistency
requirement: When reporting computed values or summaries, ensure the submitted tables, intermediate outputs, aggregation values, and conclusions agree with one another.

title: Sensitivity to supplied dataset variants
requirement: When claims concern robustness or generalization across the supplied dataset variants, evaluate the relevant original and training-protein-removed membership sets using a comparable, explicitly documented procedure.

title: Trace-to-Result Numerical Consistency
requirement: When claiming computed statistics or aggregate results, the submitted output must contain directly inspectable evidence that reported values agree with the displayed computation, intermediate outputs, and aggregation.

title: Internal consistency of claimed quantitative results
requirement: Claimed numerical findings and derived summaries must be directly supported by the displayed computations or intermediate outputs and remain mutually consistent throughout the submission.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Supporting Computation
requirement: When reporting computed numerical results or conclusions, the submitted tables and narrative must be consistent with the displayed executable code and independently inspectable intermediate or output evidence.

title: Traceability and internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When quantitative results or conclusions are claimed, the displayed tables and narrative must be directly traceable to the shown computation and mutually consistent, including values reused in aggregates and conclusions.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Supporting Computation
requirement: When numerical results or derived conclusions are claimed, the submitted material must make those claims directly traceable to and consistent with the displayed computation, intermediate outputs, tables, and any reported aggregates.

title: Original-versus-training-removed sensitivity analysis
requirement: When both curated MLO list versions are available and analyzed, report results separately for the original and training-protein-removed lists, including their evaluable dataset/predictor coverage and quantitative performance differences; do not present one version as representative without identifying the other or explaining why it is unavailable.

title: Internal support for reported aggregate results
requirement: When claiming aggregate metrics derived from displayed component results, the submission must provide values that are arithmetically consistent with those components and with the shown computation or audit output.

title: Internal consistency of reported aggregates
requirement: When reporting group-level summaries derived from per-dataset metrics, the aggregate values and conclusions must be directly consistent with the displayed underlying results and documented computation.

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Results
requirement: When claiming computed results, ensure that reported tables, narrative values, sample counts, and conclusions are generated from and consistent with the same stated filtering, labeling, and score-direction rules.

title: Evidence for Completed Computational Claims
requirement: Claims that an analysis was executed, outputs were generated, or results are reproducible must be supported by direct, inspectable evidence in the submission rather than prose assertions alone.

title: Internal reconciliation of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed summaries, ensure that headline values and conclusions are arithmetically and logically consistent with the displayed per-dataset results, supporting tables, and code.

title: Internal consistency and evidentiary support of reported results
requirement: When reporting computed values, aggregates, or reproducibility claims, ensure they are directly supported by the submitted calculations and displayed intermediate results.

title: Arithmetic Consistency of Derived Summaries
requirement: When reporting aggregates, differences, rankings, or group-level conclusions derived from displayed results, ensure they arithmetically reconcile with the stated grouping and underlying per-dataset values.

title: Internal consistency of derived summaries
requirement: When reporting an aggregate, summary statistic, or conclusion derived from displayed per-dataset results, ensure that the reported value and interpretation are arithmetically and directionally consistent with those results and with the stated computation.

title: Executable support for claimed generated outputs
requirement: When claiming that analysis outputs, audits, or result files were generated by submitted code, the displayed code must be executable from the documented inputs and contain the definitions and transformations needed to produce and verify those outputs.

title: Internal consistency of derived summaries
requirement: When reporting aggregate metrics or conclusions derived from displayed per-dataset results, the reported summaries must be arithmetically consistent with those results and with the submitted computation.

title: Coverage of requested predictor families and sensitivity datasets
requirement: When claiming to evaluate the requested screening task, the submission must directly evaluate the available predictor families and both original and training-protein-removed membership sheets, or explicitly mark unsupported combinations as unevaluable with inspectable reasons.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, headline values and conclusions must agree with the displayed code, tables, and intermediate results for the same comparison.

title: Validated Integration of Supplementary Score Sources
requirement: When predictor scores are imported from a supplementary sequence-level table, validate the identifier join and record uniqueness before merging, restrict records to the intended protein population, and demonstrate that the merge does not create duplicate or conflicting protein-level observations.

title: Reconciliation of Reported Quantitative Results
requirement: When quantitative results, contrasts, or summary claims are reported, reconcile them against the displayed computation or output, including arithmetic consistency between component values and derived differences; do not present unsupported or contradictory values.

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Quantitative Results
requirement: Claimed numerical findings, derived contrasts, and headline conclusions must be directly reconcilable with the displayed computation and reported output artifacts.

title: Internal Consistency of Reported Results
requirement: When quantitative results, contrasts, or revised analyses are reported, the submitted material must make the primary result identifiable and ensure that reported values and derived differences are arithmetically consistent with one another and with the stated computation; superseded contradictory values must be clearly labeled or removed.

title: Internally Consistent Quantitative Reporting
requirement: When the submission claims computed quantitative results, ensure that reported summaries, contrasts, counts, and conclusions are arithmetically consistent with the inspectable per-pair outputs and aggregation code.

title: Reconciled Quantitative Reporting
requirement: Claimed numerical results and conclusions must be directly reproducible from the submitted code and inspectable tabular outputs, with consistent definitions, aggregation, and rounding throughout the artifact.

title: Consistency of Reported Quantitative Summaries
requirement: When the submission reports aggregated statistics or conclusions derived from displayed outputs, the reported values and filtering claims must be arithmetically consistent with the shown per-pair results and computation.

title: Consistency of claimed computed results with submitted evidence
requirement: When the artifact claims completed statistical computations or quantitative results, those claims must be supported by internally consistent displayed code, intermediate values, tables, and conclusions.

title: Consistency between reported statistics and conclusions
requirement: When claiming statistical significance, the conclusion must match the reported adjusted or unadjusted statistic and explicitly stated threshold, with no contradictory significance claims elsewhere in the submission.

title: Definition and use of the shared gene set
requirement: When reporting analysis of shared DEGs, the submission must define the shared set from the unique, nonblank gene memberships of both experiment blocks, account for duplicate rows, and use that same set consistently in downstream counts and tests.

title: Evidence-backed computational verification
requirement: When claiming that a computation, result, or independent audit was performed, the submitted material must include direct executable recomputation from the stated inputs rather than merely hard-coded outputs or self-equality assertions.

title: Evidence-supported computation claims
requirement: When claiming that a statistic or result was independently recomputed, the submitted code must calculate it from the stated inputs and parameters rather than hard-code the expected value or merely assert a constant equals itself.

title: Direct computational support for reported results
requirement: Claimed computed statistics must be directly produced or independently checked by submitted executable code using the supplied data and stated inputs, rather than only by assigning the claimed value or asserting that a constant equals itself.

title: Respect for the stated inferential target and threshold
requirement: When the task asks whether a prespecified pathway meets an explicitly stated nominal p-value threshold, evaluate that pathway using the stated test and threshold without introducing unrequested additional pathway testing or multiple-comparison adjustment that changes the claim being answered.

title: Consistency between claimed results and supporting computation
requirement: When the submission claims computed statistics or conclusions, those claims must be directly supported by the displayed executable code, intermediate outputs, or independently reproducible calculations; material contradictions must not be used as evidence for the conclusion.

title: Support for claimed computed results
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or conclusions, the submission must provide displayed, executable calculations whose inputs and outputs support those claims consistently.

title: Consistency between claimed results and inspectable computation
requirement: When claiming completed statistical computations, the reported statistics and conclusions must be supported by the submitted tables, executable code, and any stated audit; material discrepancies between these elements are penalized.

title: Consistency between computation and reported results
requirement: When claiming completed statistical computations, ensure the displayed executable code, intermediate tables, audits, and final numerical conclusions mutually support the same query, contingency table, p-values, adjusted values, and significance claims.

title: Consistency between computation evidence and reported results
requirement: For any claimed computed result, the submitted code, displayed intermediate quantities, tables, audits, and final report must support the same numerical result and inferential conclusion.

title: Internal support for claimed computations
requirement: When claiming computed statistics or conclusions, the submitted code, displayed intermediate quantities, and reported results must be mutually consistent and sufficient to reproduce the claim.

title: Consistent tested-gene universe
requirement: When the submission claims an enrichment result, it must explicitly define the tested-gene universe and use that same universe consistently in the contingency table, p-value, adjusted values, and reported conclusion.

title: Consistency between computation and reported results
requirement: When claiming completed statistical calculations, the submitted code, displayed contingency tables, intermediate outputs, and final numerical conclusions must describe the same computation and be mutually reproducible from the submitted material.

title: Traceable consistency of claimed quantitative results
requirement: For any claimed computed result, the submitted analysis must provide inspectable code or intermediate evidence using the stated inputs and method that supports the same numerical result and conclusion.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Displayed Computation
requirement: When claiming computed statistics or conclusions, the submission must make those claims consistent with the displayed calculations, intermediate results, and reported outputs.
