title: Eligibility-Appropriate ORA Universe
requirement: When reporting an over-representation test, the submission must define the null universe as the eligible genes that could have entered the analyzed experiment and explain why that universe is appropriate, rather than restricting it solely to genes appearing in the tested pathways.

title: Defensible Eligibility Universe
requirement: When performing ORA, the submission must explicitly define the tested-gene universe and justify its eligibility basis, so the null model is not silently changed by restricting genes to pathway coverage or by using an unsupported universe.

title: Auditable Contingency-Table Validation
requirement: When claiming computed ORA statistics, the submission must provide direct, inspectable checks that the contingency-table cells and pathway intersections match the reported query size, universe size, and set memberships.

title: Eligibility-complete ORA background
requirement: When claiming enrichment among genes shared across two experimental DEG lists, the analysis must define an inspectable background that represents genes eligible in both experiments, rather than silently restricting the null to one experiment or an unexplained subset.

title: Directional alignment of enrichment test
requirement: When claiming over-representation or enrichment, the reported p-value must come from a test whose tail alternative matches enrichment rather than depletion, and the displayed computation must use that same directional hypothesis.

title: Consistency Between Reported Results and Reproducible Computation
requirement: When an artifact claims computed results on a specified scale or after a specified transformation, its displayed executable analysis must directly implement that transformation and support the reported results; prose assertions alone are insufficient.

title: Consistency of Reported Computation and Results
requirement: When claiming computed statistics, the submitted code, stated estimand or scale, and displayed numerical results must support the same analysis.

title: Trace-to-result reproducibility
requirement: When quantitative findings are claimed, the displayed computation must use the same data transformation, units, estimand, and statistical convention as the reported result, with no material unexplained numerical contradictions across the trace, tables, and answer.

title: Consistency Between Computation and Reported Results
requirement: When claiming completed statistical results, the submitted code, transformations, analysis scale, and displayed outputs must directly support the reported statistics and conclusions.

title: Claimed results are supported by the displayed computation
requirement: When claiming completed numerical analyses, the reported statistics, scale, and interpretation must be directly reproducible from the submitted code and quantitative outputs.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When claiming completed numerical results, the reported statistics must be directly supported by the displayed computation and must remain consistent across the analysis trace, tables, and final answer.

title: Executable decision-rule fidelity
requirement: When a selection or classification rule is claimed, the displayed executable analysis must implement that rule exactly rather than a materially different condition.

title: Claimed results must be supported by displayed computation
requirement: When completed analyses or numerical results are claimed, the submitted material must provide directly inspectable computation or output that uses the stated construction and yields the claimed result.

title: Claim-to-computation numerical consistency
requirement: When numerical results are claimed as computed, the reported values and derived rankings or selections must be directly reproducible from the displayed executable analysis and its inspectable outputs, without unexplained cross-analysis substitutions or transcription errors.

title: Quantitative result consistency
requirement: When numerical results are claimed, the reported statistics, units, rankings, and selected sets must agree with the displayed executable computation and inspectable outputs.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Executed Analysis
requirement: When claiming completed statistical results, the submitted code, intermediate outputs, exported results, and final conclusions must provide direct, mutually consistent evidence for the reported estimates and significance decisions.

title: Internal validity of reported statistical results
requirement: When claiming completed statistical results, the submitted code, formulas, displayed outputs, and reported conclusions must use a mathematically correct and mutually consistent computation; transformations of model coefficients, test statistics, p-values, and selection filters must be valid and traceable.

title: Evidence support for claimed completed analysis
requirement: Claims of completed model fitting, exported results, or reproducibility must be supported by direct, inspectable evidence in the submission, such as executable analysis code whose outputs agree with the reported findings; prose assertions or references to unavailable outputs are insufficient.

title: Consistency between claimed results and their computational evidence
requirement: When claiming completed statistical results, the reported values and conclusions must be supported by the displayed computation and any cited result artifact, with the code implementing the stated statistic and transformation correctly.

title: Internal support for reported computations and results
requirement: When claiming that analyses, statistics, or exported results were computed, the submitted code, displayed outputs, and stated estimand must support the claim without material contradictions.

title: Executable support for reported results
requirement: When claiming completed computations or exported results, the submitted code and visible outputs must support those claims without contradictions.

title: Correct statistical result construction
requirement: When reporting Cox estimates and Wald p-values, the reported quantities must correspond to the stated coefficient and formulas.

title: Consistency of primary estimand and sensitivity analyses
requirement: When multiple predictor transformations or scales are analyzed, claims about the primary conclusion must identify and consistently use the corresponding scale.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Supporting Evidence
requirement: When claiming completed statistical results, the reported estimates and significance values must agree with the displayed computation, exported results, and any verification output.

title: Alignment of Primary Analysis and Final Conclusion
requirement: The final conclusion must use the analysis explicitly designated as primary, rather than selecting a sensitivity analysis because it crosses the requested threshold.

title: Correct Cox Effect-Size and Significance Transformations
requirement: When reporting Cox-model results, the hazard ratio and Wald p-value must be computed using mathematically valid transformations of the fitted coefficient and test statistic.

title: Faithful Use of the Declared Primary Analysis
requirement: When multiple scales, transformations, or sensitivity analyses are performed, the stated conclusion and reported primary results must come from the declared primary analysis rather than being selected opportunistically from a sensitivity analysis.

title: Validity of Statistical Computation
requirement: When claiming computed Cox results, the displayed implementation must apply mathematically valid effect-size transformations, standard-error calculations, and tail-probability formulas, rather than systematically miscomputing otherwise internally consistent estimates.

title: Consistency Between Reported Results and Supporting Analysis
requirement: When claiming completed computations or quantitative results, the final claims must be consistent with the directly submitted code, outputs, and documented intermediate results.

title: Consistency between reported results and documented computation
requirement: When claiming completed numerical analyses, the reported statistics must be generated by the same preprocessing, deduplication, predictor scale, and model specification shown in the reproducible code.

title: Executable support for claimed analysis outputs
requirement: When a submission claims that code generated completed analyses or complete output tables, the displayed code must be self-contained enough to execute those claimed operations without undefined variables, missing setup, or internally incompatible field references.

title: Adherence to the specified analysis estimand
requirement: When claiming the requested analysis, the submission must use the task-specified preprocessing and predictor scale, rather than substituting an alternative deduplication, transformation, or normalization that changes the estimand or makes the reported result non-comparable to the requested analysis.

title: Claimed results are supported by reproducible displayed computations
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, significance calls, or complete result sets, the submitted material must contain executable, internally consistent code or directly inspectable output that supports those claims.

title: Evidence-supported reported results
requirement: When claiming completed computations or statistically significant results, the submission must provide directly inspectable evidence that the reported claims follow from its displayed code, data-derived outputs, or result tables.

title: Evidence support and internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When claiming computed statistical results, reported significance, counts, or protein-level findings, the submission must provide directly inspectable computational or tabular evidence that supports those claims and must not contradict the displayed analysis.

title: Reproducible verification of shared-protein direction claims
requirement: If the analysis claims that proteins significant in both regimens have concordant or discordant change directions, it must provide directly inspectable computation that joins the shared significant results and evaluates the signs of their estimated changes.

title: Claim-to-result consistency
requirement: When reporting computed protein lists, counts, rankings, directions, or statistics, the submitted material must support those claims with matching displayed results or reproducible calculations; unsupported additions or contradictory rankings are penalized.

title: Reproducible regimen-difference analysis
requirement: When claiming that changes differ or do not differ between CPA and SPIRO, the analysis must show an inspectable participant-level comparison of paired changes, including the test and multiplicity correction used, with results that support the stated conclusion.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: For any reported thresholded result, the submitted code, displayed output, counts, lists, and narrative must use the same analysis universe, threshold, and result definition, with no claimed entities or rankings unsupported by the inspectable computation.

title: Inspectably supported result completeness
requirement: When claiming a complete protein-level result set or signed result table, the submitted material must provide a directly regenerable or inspectable artifact containing the claimed entities and required statistics, rather than relying only on prose or an asserted unseen file.

title: Direct regimen-difference evidence
requirement: When addressing whether regimens differ, the analysis must directly compare participant-level paired changes (or an equivalent interaction model) and report the resulting uncertainty and multiplicity-adjusted evidence, rather than inferring regimen differences from separate within-regimen significance or overlap.

title: Direct regimen-by-time interaction evidence
requirement: When making claims about whether CPA and SPIRO responses differ, evaluate the difference in subject-level baseline-to-6-month changes directly, rather than inferring regimen differences from separate within-regimen significance results or overlap sets.

title: Inspectable support for regimen-interaction results
requirement: When claiming whether protein changes differ between regimens, the submission must provide a directly inspectable interaction analysis and its resulting significance summary; overlap or within-regimen significance alone is insufficient evidence for that claim.

title: Evidence supports claimed computed results
requirement: When an artifact claims completed statistical results, its submitted material must include directly inspectable output or an equivalent reproducible result artifact that supports those claims, rather than relying only on prose assertions or code that is not shown to emit or save the claimed values.

title: Regimen-difference claims require a formal interaction result
requirement: When an artifact claims that changes differ between regimens, it must distinguish within-regimen significance or overlap from the formal between-regimen comparison and provide an inspectable result for that comparison; nonsignificant or absent interaction evidence must not be converted into a regimen-specific conclusion.

title: Inspectably supported interaction results
requirement: When claiming that regimen-specific changes differ (or do not differ), provide inspectable evidence from the submitted analysis: the interaction test implementation, the tested feature count, and the resulting significant-set count or feature-level statistics. Do not support the claim only with prose, planned code, or an unshown output.

title: Evidence support for computed claims
requirement: When claiming completed statistical results or derived counts, provide direct, inspectable evidence in the submission—such as displayed output, result tables, or reproducible intermediate values—that matches the stated computation and supports the claim.

title: Inspectable support for reported inferential results
requirement: When claiming a computed inferential result—especially a between-regimen interaction—provide direct, inspectable evidence in the submission linking the claim to the analysis, such as the tested-assay count and relevant raw/adjusted results or a displayed significant-set summary; code that merely constructs a result table is not proof that the claimed result occurred.

title: Executable evidence chain for reported computations
requirement: When claiming completed statistical results, the submitted code and displayed outputs must be mutually consistent and sufficient to reproduce and verify those results; undefined variables, omitted result tables, or unsupported numerical claims must not be used as evidence of execution.

title: Auditability of assay-level eligibility and missingness
requirement: When results depend on incomplete assay measurements or paired observations, the analysis must distinguish assays with any usable pair from assays eligible for testing and document how those eligibility rules affect denominators and reported findings.

title: Inspectable support for reported computational results
requirement: When claiming computed counts, significance calls, interaction results, or other quantitative outputs, provide directly inspectable supporting evidence in the submission (such as displayed results or output that can be reproduced from the shown code), with internally consistent totals and claims.

title: Inspectably supported regimen-interaction claims
requirement: When claiming that CPA and SPIRO changes differ (or that no assay differs), the submission must provide direct, inspectable evidence from the interaction analysis, including the tested assay count, adjusted-significance result, and enough per-assay statistics or a referenced result table to verify the claim. Code that merely constructs an interaction table, or an unsupported prose count, is insufficient.

title: Protein-level regimen-interaction reporting
requirement: When claiming that six-month changes differ or do not differ between regimens, provide an inspectable protein-level interaction analysis with each tested protein’s regimen-specific effect sizes, raw p-value, and multiplicity-adjusted q-value, while distinguishing this test from within-regimen significance.

title: Evidence for regimen-interaction claims
requirement: When claiming that protein changes differ between regimens, the submission must provide direct, inspectable interaction-test computation and corresponding protein-level statistics; separate within-regimen significance values do not support this claim.

title: Consistency of significant-protein sets
requirement: Reported significant-protein counts, shared/unique sets, and named examples must be derivable from the displayed per-regimen significance results and set-operation logic.

title: Direct regimen-by-time interaction analysis
requirement: When claiming that protein changes differ between CPA and SPIRO, directly compare participant-level paired changes between regimens and report the corresponding effect estimates, raw p-values, and multiplicity-adjusted values; do not infer regimen differences from significance in only one arm.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting output
requirement: When claiming complete, reproducible protein lists, counts, or set memberships, ensure that the narrative and reported summaries are directly supported by the displayed computation or inspectable results, with no contradictory protein-level classifications.

title: Evidence supports reported computations and results
requirement: When claiming completed analyses, numeric findings, or generated result files, the submission must provide direct, inspectable evidence that supports those claims, such as executable analysis code whose displayed outputs correspond to the claims and an accessible results artifact containing the claimed fields and values.

title: Internal consistency of reported findings
requirement: Results, interpretations, set memberships, directions, and quantitative summaries must agree with one another and with the submitted analysis outputs and result tables.

title: Reproducible result-artifact delivery
requirement: When the response claims to provide complete machine-readable results, the submitted artifact must be accessible for public review and its documented schema, row counts, completeness checks, and claimed contents must be directly verifiable.

title: Direct regimen-by-time comparison
requirement: If the solution claims that changes differ or do not differ between regimens, it must perform and report a direct comparison of subject-level baseline-to-follow-up changes between regimens, with multiplicity handling and results distinguishable from within-regimen significance or set overlap.

title: Evidence-backed deliverables and internal reconciliation
requirement: If the solution claims that a generated results artifact supports reported statistics, significance sets, overlap counts, or completeness, the submitted material must provide directly inspectable evidence from that artifact and reconcile its schema, contents, counts, and claims without unsupported additions or contradictions.

title: Inspectably supports claimed computed results
requirement: When claiming completed computations, generated results, or reproducibility, the submitted outputs must contain inspectable fields, records, or equivalent evidence that directly supports those claims; code or prose alone is insufficient.

title: Direct regimen-difference testing
requirement: When claiming that changes do or do not differ between regimens, provide a direct, appropriately adjusted comparison of subject-level changes (or an equivalent interaction test), rather than inferring regimen differences from separate within-regimen significance results.

title: Claim-to-evidence reconciliation
requirement: When reporting computed findings, ensure substantive numbers, directions, significance labels, set memberships, and completeness claims agree with the displayed calculations and delivered result artifacts.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting analysis
requirement: When claiming computed quantitative findings, the final results must be internally consistent with the displayed code, intermediate outputs, and reported summaries, including derived signs, directions, and category counts.

title: Consistency between reported computations and supporting analysis
requirement: When claiming computed rankings, counts, or other quantitative results, the submitted code, intermediate outputs, and final report must support the same result rather than contradicting one another.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When presenting computed rankings, counts, or values, the final claims must agree with the displayed code outputs and intermediate results.

title: Consistency Between Computation and Reported Results
requirement: When claiming computed counts, rankings, completeness, or extracted result lists, ensure the submitted code, intermediate outputs, and final report agree with one another and do not contain duplicated, missing, or otherwise unsupported entries.

title: Internal consistency of computed-result claims
requirement: When claiming complete filtered sets, rankings, or summary counts, ensure the submitted calculations and displayed results support those claims without cardinality mismatches, duplicate entries, or contradictions.

title: Evidence-aware ranking of reported strongest associations
requirement: When labeling associations as “strongest,” “top,” or most prominent, the submission must distinguish effect magnitude from statistical evidence and use the reported adjusted p-values—or explicitly qualify the ranking—rather than treating large absolute estimates alone as stronger evidence.

title: Consistency of Reported Direction Counts
requirement: When aggregate positive/negative association counts are reported, they must be computed from the same thresholded records and reconcile with the reported total for each endpoint.

title: Execution-to-result consistency
requirement: When claiming that a computation was completed, the executable code and displayed intermediate outputs must directly support the reported result, including the stated ranking rule and its outputs.

title: Numerical transcription and internal consistency
requirement: Numerical findings that are repeated across the trace and final answer must remain mutually consistent and must not contradict the displayed supporting values.

title: Scope fidelity to the stated comparison
requirement: When the task asks whether two biological sets overlap broadly, the analysis should evaluate that stated comparison rather than silently replacing one set with an arbitrary narrower subset or an invented ranking requirement.

title: Executable support for reported computations
requirement: For any claimed computed statistic, the submitted executable code and displayed output must implement the stated formula and support the reported value; prose must not substitute for evidence of completed computation.

title: Cross-section numerical consistency
requirement: Central counts, overlaps, and other quantitative claims must remain consistent across the analysis trace, intermediate results, final results, and answer.

title: Consistency between executable analysis and reported results
requirement: When claiming computed counts or statistics, the submitted code and displayed intermediate outputs must use the same data source, filters, and definitions as the reported results.

title: Internal consistency of reported computations
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, the submitted material must make the reported values consistent with the displayed computation, parameters, and intermediate results.

title: Consistency between reported computations and reproducible code
requirement: When claiming a computed statistic, ensure the displayed executable code computes the same quantity with the same parameters and tail convention as the reported result.

title: Consistency between reported computations and displayed code
requirement: For any claimed computed statistic, the submitted code must visibly use the same data universe, parameter definitions, and tail convention described in the method and reflected in the reported value.

title: Consistency Between Computation and Reported Results
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, the artifact must make the reported values consistent with the displayed executable code, parameters, and intermediate outputs.

title: Executable Environment Portability
requirement: When claiming reproducibility, the submitted code must use file paths and environment assumptions that are valid in the stated execution context or provide an executable, inspectable way to configure them.

title: Consistency of reported results with supporting computation
requirement: When claiming completed quantitative analyses, the reported results must be directly reproducible from the submitted code, displayed outputs, and stated denominators; internally contradictory counts or results are penalized.

title: Consistency between reported claims and executed analysis
requirement: When reporting categorized results, counts, or named examples, ensure they are directly supported by the displayed computation and satisfy the stated inclusion rules and comparator definitions.

title: Distinguishing directional discordance from non-replication
requirement: When claiming that proteins are directionally discordant, require evidence that the comparator association is sufficiently supported under the analysis’s stated inclusion rule; a nonsignificant comparator estimate with an opposite sign is non-replication or uncertain direction, not confirmed discordance.

title: Evidence-supported classification of concordance and discordance
requirement: When labeling an entity as a significant overlap, same-direction match, or discordant result, the classification must be consistent with the stated inclusion rules and supported by the displayed estimates, p-values, denominators, and filtering code or outputs; a mere opposite sign must not be presented as statistically supported discordance when the comparator fails the claimed significance criterion.

title: Consistency Between Claims and Demonstrated Evidence
requirement: When reporting computed quantities or significance-based conclusions, the submission must ensure that the stated results are directly entailed by the displayed computation, intermediate outputs, and reported thresholds.

title: Evidence-qualified directional exceptions
requirement: When identifying protein-level directional discordance, distinguish a sign difference supported by significant associations in both datasets from a nonsignificant comparator estimate; do not present the latter as confirmed discordance.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims
requirement: When reporting computed counts, denominators, percentages, or statistical results, the submitted results and answer must match the displayed computation and clearly use the same estimand, inclusion rule, and denominator.

title: Executable reproducibility of the analysis code
requirement: When claiming reproducible computation, the submitted code must be syntactically valid and use the loaded, defined objects and columns consistently enough that the documented filtering, joining, and calculations can actually be rerun from the supplied data.

title: Preservation of the claimed comparison estimand
requirement: When reporting directional concordance or overlap, the eligibility rule used in the computation must match the stated estimand, especially the distinction between all GAHT-significant proteins and proteins significant in both GAHT and the comparator.

title: Evidence-consistent classification of named exceptions
requirement: When naming proteins as significant overlaps or discordances, classify them using the same stated significance and matching rules used for the aggregate analysis, and provide inspectable estimates and significance values sufficient to verify the classification.

title: Distinguishing directional concordance from magnitude agreement
requirement: When interpreting agreement between GAHT and comparator effects, distinguish sign-based overlap from agreement in effect magnitude or rank pattern, and support any claimed magnitude relationship with a reported, reproducible effect-size summary.

title: Internal support and consistency of reported results
requirement: When making quantitative or entity-level claims, the submission must provide inspectable computation or output that supports those claims and must keep filtering rules, denominators, counts, and classifications consistent across code, intermediate results, and conclusions.

title: Consistency of Exception Labels with Significance Filters
requirement: When labeling proteins as discordant or as significant overlaps, classifications must match the stated significance criteria and displayed adjusted p-values; a merely opposite-signed but nonsignificant estimate must be identified as directional only, not as a significant discordance.

title: Internal consistency of reported clustering results
requirement: When reporting computed clustering results, the submission must keep cluster memberships, cluster sizes, singleton counts, and interpretive claims mutually consistent with the displayed computation and intermediate results.

title: Consistency between claimed and executable computation
requirement: When claiming a completed statistical computation, the submitted code must directly implement the named method and produce outputs consistent with that method.

title: Traceability of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or cluster memberships, the submission must provide inspectable evidence tying each reported value and membership claim to the displayed computation or generated output.

title: Self-contained evidence for claimed generated outputs
requirement: When claiming that a complete matrix, reordered matrix, membership table, or other generated result was produced, the submission must provide directly inspectable output or a runnable, fully specified generation path sufficient to verify that claim from the submitted material, rather than relying on an unseen workspace file.

title: Alignment of the analyzed score panel with the requested scope
requirement: When the submission claims to answer the specified 21-score Spearman task, the analyzed variables and reported results must use that requested panel and method rather than substituting additional score families, alternate derived variables, or a different correlation method.

title: Consistency of reported cluster membership with computed output
requirement: When cluster memberships or singleton assignments are reported, those assignments must match the labels produced by the displayed clustering computation and must account for all analyzed scores without contradictory reassignment.

title: Traceability of reported quantitative outputs
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, cluster memberships, or cluster sizes, the submission must make those claims directly inspectable and consistent with the displayed matrix, code outputs, or other public computational evidence.

title: Explicit score-scope and representation reconciliation
requirement: When the source contains multiple score, probability, component, or framework-specific representations, the analysis must explicitly define the score universe being correlated and justify inclusions and exclusions so the reported clusters correspond to the stated question rather than an unexplained subset or expanded scope.

title: Canonical score-scope fidelity
requirement: When the task specifies a target set of scores, the analysis must explicitly define that set from the supplied schema and ensure that the primary correlations and clusters use exactly those variables rather than silently substituting derived probabilities, component scores, or an expanded feature set.

title: Computation-to-report consistency
requirement: When claiming computed correlations, clusters, or validation outputs, the submitted code and inspectable outputs must support the reported memberships and statistics without contradictions between the implemented analysis and the written results.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When reporting computed correlations, cluster memberships, counts, or summary statistics, the submission must provide directly inspectable computational or result evidence that supports those claims and must not contradict its own displayed code, outputs, or intermediate values.

title: Analysis-scope and estimand reconciliation
requirement: When the source contains multiple related score representations, the analysis must explicitly define the score set used for the primary correlation estimand and distinguish included target scores from excluded probabilities, components, labels, or alternate representations.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When reporting computed numerical results, cluster memberships, or summary statistics, the submission must keep those claims consistent with its displayed code and directly reported outputs.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When the submission reports computed statistics, cluster memberships, or pairwise relationships, those claims must agree with the displayed code and intermediate outputs.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, cluster memberships, or interpretations derived from displayed analysis, those claims must agree with the submitted code, outputs, and other inspectable evidence.

title: Consistency of quantitative claims with displayed computation
requirement: When reporting computed numerical results, the submission must keep each reported value consistent with the displayed code, intermediate outputs, and other quantitative claims.

title: Preservation of correlation direction
requirement: When reporting signed correlations or describing relationships as positive or inverse, the submission must preserve the computed sign rather than silently substituting an absolute magnitude or reversing the direction.

title: Consistency of reported quantitative results with supporting computation
requirement: When the submission reports completed calculations or quantitative results, each material reported value must be directly supported by the displayed code, outputs, tables, or other inspectable evidence, with no unexplained discrepancies between intermediate results and the final answer.

title: Claim-to-computation numerical consistency
requirement: When reporting computed numerical findings, every material value, sign, count, ordering, and summary must agree with the displayed computation or directly inspectable output supporting it.

title: Inspectable support for aggregate cluster evidence
requirement: When claims rely on cluster-level pair counts, minima, medians, or completeness assertions, the submission must provide enough direct pairwise evidence or an executable derivation for those aggregates to be independently recomputed.

title: Consistency between computed outputs and reported conclusions
requirement: When the submission reports computed clusters or quantitative results, its final answer must agree with the displayed reproducible code outputs and intermediate results.

title: Consistency between computation and reported findings
requirement: When claiming computed results, the submitted analysis must keep its displayed code, intermediate outputs, cluster memberships, and final conclusions mutually consistent, so each substantive reported finding is supported by the inspectable analysis.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: Claimed quantitative results and cluster memberships must be directly supported by the displayed calculations and remain internally consistent across the trace and final answer.

title: Exact requested score universe
requirement: The correlation and clustering analysis must use the requested 21 continuous endotype scores rather than an overinclusive set containing probabilities, labels, or additional derived scores.

title: Alignment of subgroup definition with the stated estimand
requirement: When the supplied data contain an explicit subgroup variable and the task asks for proportions by subgroup without requiring reconstruction, the analysis must not silently substitute a separately derived classification while presenting it as the requested subgroup composition.

title: Patient-Level Denominator Integrity
requirement: When reporting proportions as patient-level estimates, repeated records or accessions for the same patient must not silently receive multiple weight in the denominator; the unit of analysis and any deduplication rule must be inspectable.

title: Quantitative Result and Computation Consistency
requirement: When reporting computed counts, proportions, percentages, or denominators, the submitted material must make the reported values arithmetically consistent with the displayed counts, denominator, executable calculation, and any shown output.

title: Claim-to-computation denominator consistency
requirement: When reporting patient-level proportions, the submitted computation must use the same deduplicated patient denominator that is stated for the reported results, rather than using qualifying rows or another denominator.

title: Trace-to-result computational consistency
requirement: When claiming computed quantitative results, the submitted code must implement the same cohort filters, deduplication, counts, and denominator used in the reported results.

title: Patient-Level Denominator and Deduplication
requirement: When reporting proportions of patients, each patient must contribute to the denominator once and must receive at most one subgroup assignment, with the selection or aggregation rule directly inspectable.

title: Patient-Level Denominator for Patient Proportions
requirement: When claiming proportions of patients, the reported denominator and subgroup counts must prevent repeated records from causing some patients to receive disproportionate weight.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Displayed Computation
requirement: When a submission claims computed quantitative results, its final counts and percentages must agree with the displayed code outputs and intermediate results.

title: Reproducible Score-Derived Classification
requirement: When claiming subgroup assignments are derived from the lymphoid and myeloid scores, the submission must provide inspectable score-based classification logic and results traceable to that logic rather than relying solely on supplied subgroup labels.

title: Consistency Between Code and Reported Results
requirement: When claiming completed computation, the displayed analysis code, documented parameters, intermediate outputs, and final results must be mutually consistent and reproducible from the submission.

title: Align reported results with inspectable computation
requirement: When claiming completed quantitative analyses, ensure the reported statistics are directly supported by the displayed code or output and that intermediate and final values are internally consistent.

title: Use the corresponding gene set for each group-specific calculation
requirement: When reporting separate within-set results, ensure each group’s correlation matrix and summaries are computed from that group’s own selected membership rather than reusing another group’s gene list.

title: Ensure reported results agree with displayed computation
requirement: When reporting computed numerical findings, maintain consistency between the final answer and the submitted code, intermediate results, and other directly inspectable evidence.

title: Use a justified candidate-gene universe
requirement: When reconstructing gene sets from the supplied expression file, define the candidate universe from explicit file metadata or all appropriate gene columns, rather than silently selecting an unsupported positional subset that changes which genes can enter the analysis.

title: Use the requested primary correlation statistic
requirement: When answering the within-set correlation question, use pairwise Spearman correlation as the primary analysis for both gene sets; Pearson or other statistics may be supplementary but must not replace the requested primary result.

title: Consistency between computation and reported results
requirement: Claimed quantitative results and classifications must agree with the submitted executable analysis and its displayed intermediate or final outputs.

title: Traceability of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed quantities, ensure the submitted code, intermediate outputs, tables, and final answer support the same calculation and values.

title: Reconcile reported results with the demonstrated computation
requirement: When claiming completed quantitative results, ensure the displayed computation and intermediate outputs directly support the reported values and use the same estimand, including consistent off-diagonal handling.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting analysis
requirement: When claiming completed calculations, ensure reported quantitative results and categorical findings are consistent with the displayed code, intermediate outputs, tables, and derived summaries.

title: Align reported results with the displayed computation
requirement: When claiming completed quantitative analysis, ensure that reported statistics, classifications, and interpretations are directly reproducible from the submitted code and intermediate outputs, with labels and values kept consistent across the trace and final answer.

title: Keep the declared operational data scope consistent with execution
requirement: When defining data-derived gene sets or variables, ensure that the fields, score columns, direction conventions, and feature subset declared in the method are the same ones actually used by the shown code and reported results.

title: Reconcile reported results with executed computation
requirement: When claiming completed quantitative analysis, the reported values, classifications, and conclusions must be directly supported by the displayed computation and must agree across trace, results, and final answer.

title: Align stated analysis scope with executed inputs
requirement: When an analysis specifies a candidate universe, panel, direction, or filter, the displayed code must apply that same scope so that the reported results are reproducible from the stated method.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When reporting computed thresholds, DEG counts, rankings, or summary statistics, the artifact must provide inspectable code or output that uses the same analysis definition and supports those claims.

title: Stabilized count-scale variance estimation
requirement: When the analysis claims count-based RNA-seq inference, its displayed computation must estimate or stabilize gene-level mean–variance dispersion across genes rather than relying only on an unmoderated per-gene moment estimate or log-expression residual variance.

title: Accounting for major measured technical batch structure
requirement: When disease groups are materially associated with measured technical batches and the analysis claims an adjusted disease effect, the displayed design must account for the relevant batch variables or explicitly demonstrate that their omission does not confound the estimand.

title: Consistency of Reported Results with Supporting Analysis
requirement: When the response claims ranked genes, directions, statistics, or summary counts, those claims must agree with the displayed computation and supporting results.

title: Consistency of Reported Quantitative Results with Supporting Analysis
requirement: When the response claims computed quantitative findings, those findings must be consistent with the displayed analysis trace and its reported intermediate results.

title: Internal consistency between claimed results and supporting analysis
requirement: When claiming computed results, thresholds, rankings, or totals, the submitted material must support those claims with inspectable code or displayed outputs, without contradictions between the analysis trace and final answer.

title: Execution-status accounting
requirement: When claiming completed gene-level model fitting or derived results, the submission must directly document fit eligibility (including failures, non-convergence, or errors) and ensure that invalid or incomplete fits are excluded from downstream inference.

title: Internal reconciliation of reported results
requirement: Claimed thresholds, totals, subgroup counts, and derived summaries must reconcile with the displayed computation and with one another.

title: Faithful transfer of computed rankings
requirement: When the submission claims ranked entities, the final reported ordering must preserve the ordering produced by the displayed effect-size computation.

title: Consistency between documented computation and reported conclusions
requirement: When reporting computed results, the final claims must agree with the displayed code, intermediate outputs, thresholds, counts, rankings, and directional breakdowns; contradictions must not leave the claimed result unsupported.

title: Quantitative result consistency
requirement: When reporting computed quantitative results, the submission must maintain consistency between the stated cutoff, displayed calculation, reported totals, directional breakdowns, and rankings.

title: Computational claim consistency
requirement: When reporting derived numerical results, the submission must keep the displayed code, intermediate results, final answer, and internal arithmetic mutually consistent.

title: Method-to-implementation fidelity
requirement: When claiming that a named statistical method was used, the submitted code and reported inferential quantities must implement that method rather than an materially different approximation.

title: Executable trace support
requirement: When claiming reproducible computed results, the submitted code and intermediate outputs must form a coherent executable chain that defines the variables used for reported statistics and rankings, without undefined objects or code/results contradictions.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When reporting computed counts, rankings, or statistics, the submission must make those claims consistent with the displayed code, intermediate results, and other reported quantities.

title: Low-expression filtering
requirement: When claiming genome-wide differential-expression results from RNA-seq data, apply and document a defensible low-expression filter before testing, so that genes with essentially no usable signal do not drive unstable statistical comparisons.

title: Identifiable covariate design
requirement: When adjusting for multiple technical or biological covariates, ensure the design matrix is identifiable and avoid simultaneously including redundant or perfectly paired variables that prevent meaningful estimation of the disease effect.

title: Internal consistency of computed results
requirement: When reporting quantitative analysis results, ensure the stated model, executable code, exported outputs, rankings, and numerical summaries describe the same computation and do not contain unresolved contradictions.

title: Evidence-supported computational claims
requirement: When claiming completed analyses, reruns, validation, or quantitative results, ensure the submitted material contains inspectable computation or exported output that directly supports those claims and is internally consistent with the reported values.

title: Consistency between claimed results and supporting evidence
requirement: When reporting computed results, ensure the final claims agree with the quantitative results and calculations shown elsewhere in the submission; do not report a materially different statistic, significance level, or conclusion than the inspectable supporting evidence.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims
requirement: When reporting a quantitative result in multiple sections or outputs, keep the statistic, significance interpretation, direction, and sample definition consistent; do not claim a result that conflicts with the directly reported supporting value.

title: Executable support for claimed computed results
requirement: When claiming that a statistical result or generated table was computed, the displayed code and data flow must actually produce the claimed result, including constructing and passing the complete inputs to each reported calculation.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting calculations
requirement: When claiming computed statistics or adjusted results, the displayed code and quantitative outputs must be mutually consistent and capable of producing the claimed values.

title: Consistency of interpretations with quantitative evidence
requirement: When making statistical or biological interpretation claims, the interpretation must agree with the directly reported effect sizes, p-values, adjusted values, overlaps, and significance status.

title: Consistency between interpretations and reported evidence
requirement: When making biological, statistical, or significance interpretations, ensure they are consistent with the directly reported tables, statistics, and quantitative results; do not assert an association, enrichment, significance level, or replication that the submitted evidence contradicts.

title: Executable support for claimed computed results
requirement: When presenting code as the computation supporting a reported result, the code must actually collect the relevant inputs and perform the claimed calculation so that the reported output is derivable from the shown workflow.

title: Consistency between executed statistical procedure and reported results
requirement: When reporting computed statistical results, the submitted code and described procedure must implement the same test direction, correction inputs, and analysis logic needed to produce those results.

title: Evidence-aligned biological interpretation
requirement: When making a biological or cell-type interpretation from quantitative analysis, the interpretation must be supported by the reported marker overlaps, enrichment statistics, and other displayed evidence rather than contradicting them.

title: Enrichment-tail computation matches the claimed direction
requirement: When claiming marker overrepresentation, the enrichment test must use the overrepresentation tail and the reported p-values/q-values must correspond to that direction.

title: Displayed results must be executable from the shown computation
requirement: For claimed computed results, the submitted code must actually collect and transform the relevant intermediate values needed to generate the displayed outputs.

title: Executable support for reported computations
requirement: When claiming that a computation was performed, the displayed executable code must actually implement the reported calculation and produce the claimed output, including required value collection, correction, and output-writing steps.

title: Consistency of quantitative claims with evidence
requirement: Reported numerical results and significance or replication claims must agree with the displayed tables, intermediate results, and stated statistical tests.

title: Consistency between executed computation and reported results
requirement: When claiming computed statistics or conclusions, the submitted code, displayed outputs, and narrative interpretation must use the same test direction, values, and significance status; internal contradictions must not support the claim.

title: Consistency of quantitative claims with displayed evidence
requirement: When reporting quantitative results or significance claims, the stated direction, magnitude, p-value/FDR, and significance qualification must agree with the displayed statistics and tables.

title: Consistency between executable analysis and reported results
requirement: When executable code is provided as support for a claimed computation, the code's statistical test, tail, inputs, and result-collection logic must be capable of producing the reported output.

title: Consistency between claimed results and displayed evidence
requirement: When claiming computed results, ensure the final claims are consistent with the displayed analysis code, tables, and quantitative results; do not report findings that the submitted evidence explicitly contradicts or fails to support.

title: Consistency between claimed results and submitted evidence
requirement: When making a substantive quantitative or statistical result claim, ensure that the displayed methods, intermediate results, tables, and conclusions support it without contradiction; a claim is not supported when the submission explicitly reports an incompatible result or omits the claimed result from the directly shown evidence.

title: Consistency between reported findings and supporting analysis evidence
requirement: When claiming a statistical result or biological enrichment, the submitted code, tables, and narrative must provide mutually consistent, directly inspectable support for that claim; unsupported or contradicted claims must not be presented as completed findings.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims and evidence
requirement: When reporting quantitative results or biological findings, ensure each claimed value or significance conclusion is directly supported by the displayed calculation or reviewable result and does not contradict other submitted evidence.

title: Quantitative evidence for ALS dysregulation claims
requirement: When claiming that modules are dysregulated or associated with ALS, report a direct quantitative disease-versus-control or disease-association analysis for the claimed module rather than inferring dysregulation solely from co-expression structure, marker enrichment, or gene descriptions.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims
requirement: When reporting computed results, ensure every quantitative claim is consistent with the directly shown tables, code-derived results, and other submitted evidence; conflicting values or interpretations must not be presented as simultaneously valid.

title: Support for claimed enrichment findings
requirement: When claiming statistically significant marker enrichment or another computed association, provide direct evidence for that specific claim, including the corresponding module, statistic, and corrected significance result; claims must not exceed the displayed analysis results.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims and evidence
requirement: When reporting computed quantities or substantive results, keep the narrative, displayed tables, code-derived counts, and stated output summaries mutually consistent; do not assert values or conclusions contradicted by the submitted evidence.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims
requirement: When reporting computed results, ensure that narrative values agree with the displayed code, tables, and stated intermediate counts; do not combine a statistic with a different underlying count or contradict the submitted evidence.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed results, ensure that numerical claims agree with the displayed code, tables, intermediate counts, and related summaries; do not present values that contradict the submitted evidence.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When reporting computed quantities, keep the answer, trace, code, and directly shown outputs mutually consistent; do not state a statistic, dimension, overlap, significance result, or assignment count that contradicts the supporting evidence.

title: Consistency between reported computation and results
requirement: When reporting selected analysis parameters or computed results, ensure the executable code, stated selection rule, and reported outputs agree; do not claim results from a parameterization contradicted by the submitted computation.

title: Calibration of disease-dysregulation claims
requirement: When claiming that modules are dysregulated in ALS, distinguish direct ALS-versus-control evidence from within-ALS associations such as disease duration, and scope the conclusion accordingly.

title: Consistency between executed analysis and reported results
requirement: When reporting computed parameters or results, the submitted code, stated selection logic, and reported values must agree; hard-coded or otherwise executed values must not contradict the claimed diagnostics or output.

title: Accounting consistency for completeness claims
requirement: When claiming that a selected set of genes or records is fully assigned or represented, the displayed memberships, counts, and exclusions must reconcile with that completeness claim.

title: Internal consistency of computation and reported outputs
requirement: When claiming completed analyses or quantitative results, the submitted code, reported values, and directly shown output summaries must agree on executed parameters and accounting quantities; reported module dimensions and assignments must satisfy stated totals.

title: Reconcile completeness claims with reported totals
requirement: When claiming that all selected genes, modules, or other analyzed items are represented, reconcile that claim with the directly reported module sizes, memberships, or other exhaustive output so omissions and double-counting are detectable.

title: Alignment between executable analysis and reported results
requirement: When claiming completed computation, the submitted executable code must use the parameters and procedures that correspond to the reported quantitative results; conflicting hard-coded settings, procedures, or outputs must not be presented as the same run.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed quantities, ensure that material values agree across the code, tables, summaries, and conclusions; do not present a result that is contradicted by other submitted evidence.

title: Accounting for claimed module membership completeness
requirement: When claiming that selected genes are assigned to final modules, provide membership evidence whose module sizes and assignments reconcile with that claim, including any explicitly unassigned or excluded genes.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims and evidence
requirement: When reporting computed results, ensure that numerical summaries, detailed tables, code-derived outputs, and stated completeness claims agree with one another; do not present conflicting values or unsupported additions for the same result.

title: Internal consistency of reported results and computation
requirement: Reported quantitative results must agree with the executed code, displayed intermediate results, summary tables, and claimed output contents; conflicting values for the same analysis result are a material failure.

title: Accounting consistency for module membership
requirement: When reporting module sizes or claiming complete module assignment, the reported memberships, module-size totals, and selected network universe must reconcile directly.

title: Execution-result linkage for selected network parameters
requirement: Claimed network parameters and derived results must be directly linked to the code that was executed, rather than being reported from a different or unspecified parameterization.

title: Consistency between executed method and reported results
requirement: When claiming completed computation, reported parameters and results must be consistent with the executable code and documented intermediate calculations; a hard-coded or alternative parameterization must not be presented as the source of the reported output.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative summaries
requirement: When reporting quantitative findings in multiple summaries, tables, or output artifacts, the values for the same module, statistic, membership, or enrichment claim must agree with each other and with directly shown supporting evidence.

title: Cohort-label completeness and transparency
requirement: When metadata contains explicitly documented ALS-spectrum case labels beyond the exact `ALS` value, the analysis must either include those eligible cases or provide a data-grounded justification for excluding them, and must report the resulting label-specific and final matched sample counts. title: Method-provenance honesty
requirement: When claiming use of a named statistical implementation or procedure, the submission must accurately distinguish literal execution from an approximation and provide inspectable evidence supporting the claimed execution.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When reporting computed coefficients, statistics, rankings, or conclusions, the submission must provide inspectable code and/or output that actually computes and supports the claimed quantity, with consistent parameter indexing and numerical values.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: Claimed model terms and reported numerical results must be directly supported by the displayed computation and result tables, without internal contradictions or unsupported substitutions.

title: Claimed statistics are traceable to the displayed computation
requirement: When reporting computed coefficients, p-values, FDRs, rankings, or significance claims, the submitted code and visible outputs must test the stated target and support the reported values without indexing errors, stale results, or unexplained numerical substitutions.

title: Validation uses the stated biological measurement

title: Claim-to-computation consistency

title: Claim-to-computation consistency

title: Claimed statistics must match the displayed computation

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When reporting computed statistics or rankings, the submitted code and displayed outputs must directly support the reported quantity, target variable, feature identity, and value.

title: Direct evidence for claimed validation computations
requirement: For any claimed secondary validation statistic, provide inspectable computation code or output showing the variables, cohort, and statistic; prose assertions alone do not substantiate completed validation.

title: Correct entity identification and annotation
requirement: When expanding gene symbols or making biological claims about named entities, preserve the supplied identifier-to-symbol mapping and avoid attributing an entity to a different gene or protein.

title: Direct support for claimed computed results
requirement: For each material quantitative result presented as completed analysis, the submission must provide directly inspectable computation or output that supports the claim; prose assertions or references to omitted code are insufficient.

title: Traceable support for claimed computations and quantitative results
requirement: When claiming that analyses, validations, rankings, or numerical results were completed, the submission must provide direct, inspectable computational evidence whose inputs, operations, and outputs support those claims without contradictions.

title: Direct support for claimed computations and results

title: Claimed results are supported by reproducible computation

requirement: Reported numerical values, significance labels, and rankings must agree with the displayed calculation, generated results, and stated ranking operation.
