requirement: For every reported quantitative result or validation statistic, the submitted code, displayed intermediate output, and final report must support the same value, interpretation, and significance status; claims must not rely solely on an unseen file or prose assertion.

title: Direct support and consistency of computed claims
requirement: For any claimed computed result, the submitted material must provide inspectable supporting code or output that uses the stated inputs and method, with no material contradiction between the computation, intermediate results, tables, and final claims.

title: Executable support for claimed analytical procedures
requirement: When claiming that a specific normalization, weighting, moderation, regression, or validation procedure was performed, the submitted code and displayed outputs must directly demonstrate that the procedure was actually applied to the reported results, rather than merely being described or defined.

title: Reconciled cohort and result accounting
requirement: When reporting multi-stage analyses, sample counts, tested-feature counts, and key quantitative results must reconcile across source metadata, matching/filtering steps, displayed outputs, and the final answer.

title: Consistency of reported results and supporting evidence
requirement: When reporting computed results, the answer, trace, tables, and displayed outputs must agree on the values, signs, identities, sample counts, and significance statistics that support the stated conclusion.

title: Accurate characterization of implemented methods
requirement: When claiming a named analytical method or adjustment, the submission must accurately characterize what the displayed computation actually implements and disclose material deviations that affect interpretation.

title: Consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: Claimed numerical results in the final answer must be consistent with the displayed tables, intermediate outputs, and computation used to support them.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When quantitative results are reported in multiple submitted sections, tables, or files, the same analysis result must be represented consistently across those locations; conflicting values for the same statistic or finding undermine support for the claimed result.

title: Reproducible handling of duplicate protein-gene records
requirement: When a protein dataset contains multiple records mapping to the same gene symbol, the analysis must use a documented, reproducible rule that prevents duplicate records from ambiguously or disproportionately determining the gene-level concordance result.

title: Consistency between claimed significance and documented computation
requirement: When the submission claims that a dataset’s results meet an adjusted-significance criterion, that claim must be supported by an inspectable adjustment computation or supplied adjusted values and must not contradict the documented filtering procedure.

title: Arithmetic consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting a computed score, ranking, or transformed statistic, ensure the displayed value is reproducible from the displayed inputs and stated formula.

title: Resolution of duplicate gene identifiers before integration
requirement: When protein-level records can map multiple rows to one gene symbol, explicitly resolve or inspect duplicate mappings before joining modalities so each reported gene-level result has a defensible, reproducible record.

title: Internal consistency of reported computed results
requirement: When an artifact claims that reported quantitative results were computed from displayed inputs and a stated formula, the claimed outputs must be arithmetically consistent with those inputs and formula.

title: Arithmetic consistency of reported combined scores
requirement: When a combined effect score is claimed, the displayed component effects, stated formula, and reported score must agree numerically, including for the ranking used to support prioritization.

title: Consistency of reported derived quantities
requirement: When reporting computed scores, rankings, counts, or other derived quantities, ensure they are reproducibly consistent with the displayed inputs, formula, and code.

title: Honest use of unavailable statistical evidence
requirement: When a requested statistical quantity or correction is absent from the supplied data, do not claim that it was computed or that results pass it; explicitly distinguish available evidence from unavailable evidence.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed quantities such as effect-size products, rankings, counts, or statistics, the displayed inputs, stated formula or procedure, and reported outputs must agree with one another and with the trace; material transcription or arithmetic discrepancies must not be left unresolved.

title: Internal consistency of derived quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed effect combinations or other derived numerical results, the displayed inputs, stated formula, code/output, and reported values must agree and be directly checkable from the submission.

title: Executable support for quantitative ranking claims
requirement: When an artifact claims to compute and report a combined quantitative ranking, its submitted code or other inspectable computation must include every stated factor and be consistent with the reported scores and ordering.

title: Evidence-to-result consistency
requirement: When claiming computed quantitative results, the submitted material must provide directly inspectable computation and output that support the claimed formula and values, without omitted factors or contradictory code.

title: Evidence-supported quantitative computation
requirement: When reporting computed scores, rankings, or filtered results, the submitted material must provide a directly inspectable computation that includes every claimed input and is numerically consistent with the displayed results.

title: Consistency between displayed computation and reported results
requirement: When a submission claims completed computations and reports quantitative results, the displayed code and intermediate outputs must support the same analysis configuration and reported values.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed, the reported summaries must be arithmetically consistent with the displayed counts, tables, code outputs, or other supporting evidence.

title: Internal consistency of claimed results and supporting analysis
requirement: When the submission claims computed results, the displayed code, intermediate tables, and narrative must support the same analysis and quantities without contradictions.

title: Internal consistency of claimed results and executed analysis
requirement: When claiming completed computations or conclusions, the submission must keep the displayed code, reported statistics, tables, and interpretation mutually consistent; material claims must be directly supported by the shown computation rather than by an unshown or contradictory result.

title: Calibrated interpretation of descriptive subgroup differences
requirement: When interpreting clinical enrichment, the submission must distinguish descriptive count or proportion differences from supported inferential evidence and must not present a nonsignificant or inadequately compared imbalance as established severity enrichment.

title: Consistency of quantitative claims with the displayed computation
requirement: Claimed quantitative results, selected parameters, and downstream interpretations must be directly computed by the submitted analysis and remain consistent with the displayed code, intermediate outputs, and each other.

title: Alignment of reported results with supporting computation
requirement: When claiming computed quantities or analytical settings, the submission must ensure that displayed code, reported outputs, and narrative conclusions refer to the same computation and that reported values are internally consistent with the shown evidence.

title: Consistency between reported analysis and downstream computation
requirement: When claiming computed clusters or inferential results, the submission must ensure that the displayed executable workflow uses the same selected clustering parameters and data partition underlying the reported labels, summaries, tests, and conclusions.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When claiming completed numerical results, parameter choices, or derived summaries, the submission must provide displayed, inspectable computation that actually produces those claims from the stated inputs and uses the same parameters and selected labels as the reported analysis.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When claiming completed calculations or quantitative results, the submission must ensure that the displayed code, reported tables, and narrative refer to the same computation and agree on material parameters and outputs.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting analysis
requirement: When claiming completed computations or quantitative findings, the submission must keep the displayed code, intermediate outputs, final results, and interpretation mutually consistent.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative claims and evidence
requirement: When making quantitative claims about computed results, the submission must ensure that reported statistics, conclusions, displayed tables, and supporting calculations agree with one another.

title: Evidence supports claimed normalization or computation
requirement: When the submission claims that a particular normalization or computational procedure was completed, the displayed code or public outputs must directly demonstrate that procedure and support the resulting analysis.

title: Consistency between computations and reported results
requirement: Quantitative conclusions and interpretations must agree with the displayed intermediate calculations, statistical outputs, and summary tables when those computations or results are claimed.

title: Consistency of reported quantitative results with supporting evidence
requirement: When quantitative results or conclusions are claimed, the reported statistics and interpretations must be reproducible from the displayed tables, code, or intermediate outputs.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When the submission reports derived summary statistics alongside distributions or tables, those claims must be mutually consistent with the displayed underlying results.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When reporting computed distributions, summary statistics, cohort totals, or test results, the submission must ensure that these claims are mutually consistent and directly checkable from the displayed tables, counts, and documented calculations.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: Claimed quantitative results and interpretations must agree with the displayed tables, code, arithmetic, and other submitted evidence; contradictions must not materially alter the stated conclusion.

title: Claimed results are supported by the displayed computation
requirement: When reporting computed statistics, distributions, or summaries, the submission must provide internally consistent evidence and displayed code that can produce those claims; reported values must not contradict shown tables, totals, or the operation performed.

title: Consistency of Reported Results With Shown Computation
requirement: When the submission reports computed statistics, p-values, distributions, or derived conclusions, those claims must be directly supported by the displayed code and mutually consistent with the displayed intermediate results.

title: Traceability of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting computed results, the submission must provide displayed data and executable calculations that support those results without internal numerical, statistical, or methodological contradictions.

title: Consistency Between Computation, Reported Results, and Conclusions
requirement: When claiming completed statistical analyses or robustness checks, the submission must ensure that displayed executable code, quantitative outputs, and interpretations describe the same computation and support the stated conclusion.

title: Support for claimed computation and execution
requirement: When the submission claims that an analysis or reported result was computed or executed, the displayed implementation and outputs must directly support that claim and be internally consistent.

title: Evidence-supported execution claims
requirement: When claiming that an analysis ran successfully or that outputs were generated, the submission must provide directly inspectable support showing that the displayed implementation can execute as claimed.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative summaries
requirement: When reporting cluster sizes, distributions, medians, or other derived quantitative results, the reported summaries must be mutually consistent and reconcile with the stated cohort and cluster totals.

title: Calibration of severity and enrichment conclusions
requirement: When drawing severity-stratification or clinical-trial-enrichment conclusions from cluster comparisons, the strength of the conclusion must be consistent with the reported statistical evidence and robustness results.

title: Post-therapy denominator is restricted to the requested cohort
requirement: When reporting a post-hormonal-therapy frequency, the analysis must exclude treatment-naive primary samples from that numerator and denominator, rather than combining them with metastatic or other post-treatment samples without a separately reported justification.

title: Alteration definition is reproducibly bounded to the stated pathway scope
requirement: When claiming a pathway alteration frequency, the response must state a reproducible gene/event boundary and apply it consistently, rather than silently changing the pathway scope in a way that makes the numerator incomparable or underdefined.

title: Consistency between stated alteration rules and computation
requirement: When claiming alteration counts or frequencies under explicit mutation/CNA rules, the submitted computation must implement the same event definitions and thresholds stated in the accompanying rationale and results.

title: Internal Consistency of Quantitative Claims
requirement: When the submission claims computed counts, percentages, or statistical results, its final reported values must be supported by and consistent with the displayed calculations and intermediate results.

title: Internal consistency of reported results
requirement: When a response reports computed results, its final answer and summary claims must agree with the displayed code outputs and quantitative intermediate results.

title: Consistency between reported results and supporting computation
requirement: When claiming computed quantitative results, the submitted code and intermediate outputs must implement the stated alteration rule and support the reported numerator, denominator, and statistical result without internal contradiction.

title: Internal Consistency of Computed Results
requirement: When reporting computed quantitative findings, the final claims must agree with the displayed code, intermediate outputs, arithmetic, and stated analysis rule.

title: Treatment-annotation-based cohort construction
requirement: When defining post-treatment tumors, use the available treatment-timing/site annotation to exclude treatment-naive primary samples while retaining eligible post-treatment primary and metastatic samples; do not equate post-treatment status exclusively with metastasis when the data provide a broader explicit proxy.

title: Internal Numerical Reconciliation
requirement: When reporting computed quantities, the final numerators, denominators, percentages, unions, and statistical tables must reconcile with the displayed intermediate counts and formulas.

title: Internal Numerical Consistency
requirement: When reporting computed counts, percentages, unions, or statistical tables, reconcile the final claims with the displayed intermediate calculations and ensure that equivalent representations of the same result agree.

title: Consistency between reported results and executable analysis
requirement: When claiming computed cohort counts, alteration counts, contingency tables, or test results, the submitted code and documented intermediate outputs must visibly use the same cohort definitions and transformations as the reported results.

title: Exposure identifiability and proxy qualification
requirement: When treatment exposure is not directly recorded for the analyzed samples, the response must not present an anatomic or sampling category as verified hormonal-therapy exposure; any proxy must be explicitly labeled and conclusions limited accordingly.

title: Evidence for treatment-exposure eligibility
requirement: When claiming results for post-hormonal-therapy tumors, the analysis must distinguish an explicit treatment-history annotation from an anatomic or sampling label such as metastasis, and must not present an unverified proxy as the requested cohort result.

title: Internal consistency of quantitative results
requirement: When claiming computed counts or statistics, the displayed contingency table, marginal/overlap counts, expected values, reported test statistic, and p-value must be mutually compatible and traceable to the shown computation.

title: Consistency of Reported Computation
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed, the displayed code, tables, intermediate counts, and reported statistics must support the same computation and remain mutually consistent.

title: Trace-to-result reproducibility
requirement: When quantitative results are claimed, the displayed executable code, intermediate outputs, contingency tables, and reported statistics must support the same operational definitions and values without material contradictions.

title: Executable support for reported results
requirement: When claiming computed counts, tables, statistics, or conclusions, the submitted code and displayed outputs must actually implement the stated definitions and support those claims.

title: Consistency between displayed computation and claimed results
requirement: When claiming completed quantitative analysis, the submitted code must implement the stated cohort/set operations and produce results consistent with the reported counts and statistics.

title: Claim-to-computation consistency
requirement: When claiming completed computations or quantitative results, the submitted code and displayed outputs must implement the same endpoint, inputs, and transformations used to produce those claims.

title: Claimed statistical results are supported by the displayed computation
requirement: When reporting a computed statistic or p-value, the submitted code and intermediate output must visibly implement the stated test on the reported inputs and support the reported value.

title: Alteration definitions are implemented consistently
requirement: When an alteration class includes multiple event types, the computation used for counts, overlap, and testing must include every stated event type consistently.

title: Contingency-table categories are mutually exclusive and exhaustive
requirement: When reporting a 2×2 table, the displayed construction must assign each cohort sample to exactly one cell, with the cell counts summing to the stated cohort size.

title: Reported statistical result matches the displayed computation
requirement: When a submission claims a computed test result, its reported p-value and related statistic must be directly reproducible from the displayed contingency table, test direction, and code.

title: Reported statistics are supported by the shown computation
requirement: When numerical test results are claimed, the displayed executable analysis must compute and report those same values.

title: Contingency-table cells form a valid partition
requirement: When a 2×2 table is claimed to represent mutually exclusive alteration categories, its cells must be computed from disjoint sets that exhaust the analyzed cohort.

title: Displayed analysis is executable
requirement: When completed computation is claimed, the supplied code must be syntactically valid and executable from the documented inputs.

title: Filter-to-result membership consistency
requirement: When claiming that reported genes belong to a filtered result set, the displayed filtering computation and reported statistics must support each listed gene’s eligibility; no listed result may contradict an applied threshold.

title: Ranking implementation consistency
requirement: When a result list is claimed to follow a particular ranking rule, the displayed computation must implement that rule and the reported order must be consistent with it.

title: Alignment of ranking claims with the reported estimand
requirement: When claiming that genes are ranked by significance or by effect magnitude, the submitted analysis must use and clearly report a ranking procedure consistent with that claim; it must not silently substitute one ordering criterion for another.

title: Reproducible support for reported computations
requirement: When claiming that quantitative results were computed by the displayed analysis, the submitted code, stated ranking/filter rule, intermediate counts, and reported results must be mutually consistent and support the claimed values.

title: Consistency between selection rules and reported significance
requirement: When claiming that results are statistically significant or meet a stated filtering rule, the response must apply that same rule consistently to the reported gene set and distinguish statistical ranking from separate biological prioritization.

title: Inspectable evidence for claimed computation
requirement: Claims about filtering, counts, ranking, or derived statistics must be supported by directly inspectable executable computation or equivalent displayed evidence that reproduces the reported results.

title: Execution evidence supports claimed filtering
requirement: When claiming completed filtering, the submitted executable code must visibly implement the stated filter conditions, and the reported intermediate/final counts must correspond to that implementation.

title: Execution evidence supports the reported ranking
requirement: When claiming a ranked result, the submitted code must visibly sort by the stated ranking rule, and the reported ordering or ranks must be consistent with that sort.

title: Internal consistency of reported quantitative results
requirement: When reporting derived quantitative findings, ensure the displayed source values, transformations, and derived statistics agree with one another and with the supplied data.

title: Executable support for derived rankings
requirement: When a ranking or other derived result is claimed, the displayed executable calculation must implement the stated ordering and transformations, so the reported result is reproducible from the submitted material.

title: Replicate reproducibility and condition-level landscape comparison
requirement: When claiming a global treatment-associated change from peak calls, quantify within-condition replicate reproducibility and compare condition-level genomic landscapes using a merged union or equivalent non-duplicative interval summary, rather than relying only on per-sample peak counts.

title: Separate replicate reproducibility from condition-level peak burden
requirement: When attributing a global peak-landscape difference to treatment, independently assess within-condition replicate reproducibility and use it to qualify whether the difference is distinguishable from replicate-level peak-calling variability.

title: Evidence support for claimed completed analyses
requirement: When claiming that a quantitative analysis or result was completed, distinguish executable plans and proxy summaries from results actually supported by the available inputs and inspectable computation; do not present unavailable read-level measurements or derived statistics as completed findings.

title: Evidence support for claimed computed results
requirement: When claiming that normalized coverage, differential-accessibility metrics, or other derived results were computed, provide inspectable evidence that the required source inputs were available and the displayed computation produced those results; if inputs are unavailable, clearly label the result as uncomputed or hypothetical rather than reporting it as completed analysis.

title: Calibration of accessibility claims to the measurement actually performed
requirement: When analysis uses peak presence, peak counts, or interval overlap rather than read-depth coverage, distinguish those measurements from quantitative chromatin accessibility and avoid presenting presence-based regional categories as normalized accessibility changes.

title: Reproducibility and artifact-aware support for global landscape claims
requirement: When attributing a global accessibility-landscape change to treatment, quantify within-condition replicate reproducibility and explicitly assess whether differences could instead arise from sequencing depth, library complexity, or peak-calling sensitivity; do not rely solely on between-condition peak burden or presence summaries.

title: Scope peak-call evidence without equating it to accessibility
requirement: When read-level coverage or normalized counts are unavailable, conclusions must be limited to differences in called peak burden or peak-support presence and must not present those observations as direct accessibility changes or locus-level accessibility effects.

title: Independent support for global peak-landscape claims
requirement: When claiming a global treatment-associated change from peak calls, corroborate the claim with an independent landscape-level check such as within-condition replicate reproducibility, condition-union span, or cross-condition overlap, rather than relying only on per-sample peak counts and the same presence-derived union summary.

title: Match accessibility claims to the measured evidence modality
requirement: When only peak calls or interval presence are available, distinguish the observed called-peak landscape from read-depth accessibility and avoid presenting peak-support differences as direct accessibility measurements.

title: Execution status matches reported evidence
requirement: When claiming completed read-level computation or derived results, distinguish executed calculations from planned code, unavailable inputs, and proxy analyses; do not label proxy or unexecuted results as direct measurements.

title: Evidence support for claimed completed analyses
requirement: When claiming that a computation, coverage analysis, or derived result was executed, provide direct inspectable evidence in the submission that the required inputs were available and the computation produced the reported output; do not treat planned code or unsupported prose as execution evidence.

title: Calibration of peak-call evidence to accessibility claims
requirement: When inferring biological accessibility changes from thresholded peak calls, distinguish changes in the called peak landscape from true normalized accessibility changes, and explicitly account for sequencing depth, library complexity, or peak-calling sensitivity as alternative explanations when read-level coverage is unavailable.

title: Validity of measurement interpretation
requirement: When interpreting a derived accessibility measurement, distinguish read-depth coverage from binary peak presence, interval span, peak counts, or other proxies, and label conclusions according to the quantity actually measured.

title: Within-condition reproducibility of called-region changes
requirement: When attributing a global treatment-associated change to peak-call data, assess whether the pattern is reproducible across biological replicates using an explicit within-condition overlap or concordance measure, rather than relying only on condition-level peak totals.

title: Distinguishing interval proxies from read-level accessibility
requirement: When BAM-based read coverage is unavailable or unexecuted, do not present peak presence, peak counts, or merged interval span as read coverage, CPM, or completed accessibility quantification; label such analyses as proxies and state the resulting inference limits.

title: Distinction between peak-presence proxies and read-based accessibility
requirement: When interpreting directional or regional accessibility results, do not present binary peak presence, called-peak counts, or merged interval span as read-depth/CPM accessibility measurements; label such summaries as interval-based proxies and limit conclusions accordingly.

title: Accurate distinction between interval proxies and read-depth accessibility
requirement: When BAM-derived read coverage is unavailable, distinguish interval presence or merged interval span from read-depth accessibility and do not present proxy-derived directional results as BAM/CPM measurements.

title: Distinction between peak-presence proxies and read-coverage measurements
requirement: When claiming region-level accessibility changes, distinguish binary peak-presence or interval-span summaries from BAM-derived read coverage and do not present a proxy as normalized read-level accessibility.

title: Evidence-calibrated biological interpretation
requirement: When quantitative evidence is limited to descriptive peak calls without read-level normalization or differential testing, avoid presenting mechanistic or genome-wide accessibility claims as established; clearly distinguish observed peak-call changes from conditional biological hypotheses.

title: Evidence support for claimed computations
requirement: When reporting computed read-level, normalized, or differential results, provide direct, inspectable evidence linking the claim to available inputs and an executed calculation; otherwise label the result as not computable and avoid using it as support for the conclusion.

title: Evidence support for claimed computed results
requirement: When reporting derived results from execution, provide direct, inspectable evidence in the submission that the underlying computation was actually performed and produced those results; do not present unsupported values when required inputs or intermediate outputs are absent.

title: Evidence for quantitative-input availability and completed coverage analysis
requirement: When claiming or relying on read-depth, normalized coverage, or differential-accessibility results, directly inspect and document the existence and sample mapping of the required quantitative files; if they are unavailable, explicitly mark those computations and directional counts as not computable and limit conclusions to supported peak-call summaries.

title: Evidence support for claimed computations
requirement: When claiming completed coverage, normalization, differential metrics, or directional results, provide direct, inspectable supporting outputs from the requisite input data; if those inputs are unavailable, mark the result non-computable and restrict conclusions to supported analyses.

title: Consistency between reported claims and executable trace
requirement: Ensure that reported aggregate results correspond to the displayed code and intermediate outputs, rather than relying on an unshown, contradictory, or altered calculation.

title: Evidence for input availability and completed computation
requirement: Claims about input-file availability or completed quantitative analysis must be supported by direct, inspectable file checks or captured computational outputs in the submission, rather than prose assertions alone.

title: Evidence-backed execution of claimed analyses
requirement: When claiming that a computation, quantitative analysis, or derived result was completed, provide directly inspectable evidence linking the stated result to available inputs and an executed calculation or reproducible output; do not treat planned code, prose assertions, or unavailable files as proof of execution.

title: Evidence-bounded interpretation when quantitative inputs are unavailable
requirement: When alignment or signal files needed for read-depth accessibility analysis are absent, distinguish peak-call observations from read-level accessibility conclusions and do not treat peak presence, planned code, or prose claims as evidence of normalized directional changes.
